artigo.texto: How one developer plans to build a big data center in L.A. County where NIMBYs won’t notice - Click here to listen to this article - Share via See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred - The owners of California Country Club want to replace half of their 124-acre golf course near Whittier with a 374,000-square-foot data center, keeping a nine-hole course and clubhouse. - Developers say the project would use less water than the golf course and could help lower nearby electricity costs, but it would need zoning changes and environmental review. - The proposal comes as communities across the country block or delay data centers, including in Southern California, where officials are weighing tighter limits on the projects. As the worldwide build-out of hundreds of billions of dollars in data centers to power artificial intelligence meets growing resistance, one L.A. County landowner says it has a solution — build on a golf course. Some golf courses are struggling; many have plenty of space far from homes. Meanwhile, they often already use a lot of water. California Country Club wants to turn its 18-hole course into a 9-hole course and a data center. The owners say grass-covered land at the club along the 605 Freeway near Whittier could be converted into a data center that uses less water than a golf course and, with a new power infrastructure, could potentially reduce electricity prices in the neighborhood, addressing two common objections to new data centers. The club’s owners, Ramus Development Inc., submitted a proposal to the city to redesign the 124-acre course and add a 374,000-square-foot data center that would occupy 18 acres. The existing clubhouse would remain a feature of the course. “We are committed to a transparent entitlement process and community-focused design,” said Stephen Cho, president of Ramus. Birtcher Development, an Orange County real estate company, is shepherding the proposal through the government approval process and also would build the project, called LA Recreation and Technology Park, if it gets the green light. Birtcher was tasked by the owners with finding the “highest and best use” for the golf course created in 1956, President Brooke Birtcher Gustafson said, and decided that a data center would have the least effect on the nearby community after considering residential, retail, office and industrial options. Aware that data centers concern many U.S. voters, the developers plan to engage with residents outside of City of Industry as well as locals. It will be subject to oversight by the California Energy Commission and the South Coast Air Quality Management District. The project will also receive a city environmental impact report. “We sincerely want to work with the surrounding community on this project, get input and feedback, and be transparent,” Gustafson said. Artificial intelligence and cloud storage operators have been hoovering up data center space and the computer servers inside them, and developers have been racing to build more across the country to meet demand from many other uses. Few are getting built in California, however, though one is planned for a former golf course site in the industrial-oriented San Francisco Bay Area city of Pittsburg. Despite seemingly insatiable demand, data center capacity under construction declined last year for the first time in five years, according to real estate services firm CBRE. Although construction boomed in some places such as Chicago and the Dallas area, those gains were offset by declines around Silicon Valley, northern Virginia and elsewhere. The first quarter of 2026 “produced the largest single-quarter concentration of blocked and delayed data center projects on record, with at least 75 projects worth approximately $130 billion disrupted by local opposition,” said Data Center Watch, an organization tracking opposition to data centers across the U.S. “The quarter reflected a structural shift rather than a cyclical spike: communities have internalized an opposition playbook, legislative sessions introduced formal regulatory uncertainty, and the number of active opposition groups more than doubled across 49 states,” Data Center Watch said. In Southern California, Monterey Park scuttled a proposed data center after vocal community opposition, and Vernon is considering a ban on new development. Los Angeles County has separately blocked large-scale data centers in unincorporated areas while officials develop permanent zoning restrictions. City of Industry has no such restrictions, but it would need to change the golf course’s zoning before development could proceed. Golf courses can be good locations for data centers in urban areas because they are close to users, said Mikey Jaillet, an analyst with CBRE’s Data Center Solutions team. The California Country Club is close to high-voltage electrical power lines and fiber-optic cables that transport data, said Jaillet, who is not involved in the proposed golf course development. The club could tap into the power lines by building its own substation “and take power off the grid in an elegant manner that doesn’t impact other users and ratepayers,” he said.

artigo.texto: A Petrobras incluiu investimentos em sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) e prevê destinar US$ 600 milhões a novas usinas termelétricas em seu Plano de Negócios (PN) 2027-2031, divulgado na noite desta segunda-feira, 23 de novembro. Por outro lado, a estatal reduziu em 54% a previsão de investimentos em geração solar fotovoltaica e eólica onshore, para US$ 800 milhões. No segmento de armazenamento, a Petrobras pretende desenvolver projetos próprios ou em parceria, com destaque para a participação em leilões de reserva de capacidade (LRCaps). A estatal informou que a joint venture Lightsource BP cadastrou projetos com “capacidade relevante” para o certame previsto para dezembro deste ano. Já no segmento termelétrico, o plano de negócios destaca os projetos do Complexo de Energias Boaventura (ex-Comperj), no Rio de Janeiro, com capacidade projetada total de 800 MW. Leilão de baterias e oportunidades de mercado A estatal também informou que a JV Lightsource BP cadastrou projetos com “capacidade relevante” para o LRCap de baterias previsto para dezembro deste ano. Ainda sobre a Lightsource BP, a Petrobras mantém o pipeline de projetos entre 1 GW e 1,5 GW “em estágio mais avançado de desenvolvimento”, apesar da desistência e dificuldade de conexão da Lightsource BP em alguns projetos. A estatal ainda avalia negócios de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação (P,D&I) em minerais críticos, com prioridade para aqueles com maior sinergia com os negócios da empresa, “com destaque para a cadeia de valor das baterias, como prospecção, extração, refino e montagem (pack)”. Já na eletrificação de setores tradicionais e novas demandas, como data centers e mobilidade elétrica, a avaliação da Petrobras é que esses negócios tendem a aumentar a procura por energia elétrica. A estatal também menciona a expansão da comercialização para consumidores no mercado livre. Outro interesse da Petrobras com projetos elétricos é a descarbonização de suas próprias operações, em linha com a meta de neutralidade de emissões operacionais até 2050. US$ 600 milhões para novas térmicas A Petrobras também prevê em seu PN 2027-2031 o investimento de US$ 600 milhões em novas térmicas. No documento, a estatal menciona como projeto de térmica as plantas no Complexo de Energias Boaventura (ex-Comperj), no Rio de Janeiro, com capacidade projetada total de 800 MW. A Petrobras registrou o aumento na potência contratada em térmicas a partir do LRCap de março deste ano, quando foi vencedora de projetos a gás e diesel. Assim, atualmente, a estatal tem 4,6 GW em potência contratada, contra 2 GW antes do LRCap. A receita fixa total do parque é de R$ 65 bilhões. O despacho das usinas a gás pode demandar até 16,6 milhões de m³ por dia, com combustível remunerado à parte, via Custo Variável Unitário (CVU). Redução de 54% em investimentos para solar e eólica A Petrobras reduziu em 53,8% a previsão de investimentos em eólica onshore e solar fotovoltaica, em seu Plano de Negócios (PN) 2027-2031, em comparação com o plano anterior, divulgado no final de 2025. Para o período de 2027 a 2031, a estatal prevê investimentos de US$ 800 milhões em geração renovável de eletricidade, contra US$ 1,73 bilhão previstos no PN 2026-2030. A carteira total de investimentos em energias de baixo carbono também reduziu 17,2%, passando de US$ 6,4 bilhões há um ano, para US$ 5,3 bilhões. Em dezembro de 2025, a Petrobras anunciou a compra de 49,99% da Lightsource BP, a um valor não informado. Na noite desta segunda-feira, junto ao PN 2027-2031, a empresa anunciou a compra de 42% da Neomille S.A., empresa de produção de etanol de milho do grupo CerradinhoBio, pelo valor total de R$ 2,8 bilhões. Ainda neste mês, no dia 12, a estatal adquiriu a totalidade da Logum Logística S.A. (Logum), que executa atividades de transporte, movimentação e armazenagem de etanol, derivados de petróleo e outros biocombustíveis. A Petrobras já tinha 30% de participação no negócio e comprou os 70% restantes a R$ 620 milhões, com pagamento em três parcelas da seguinte forma: R$ 300 milhões no fechamento da operação (closing); R$ 160 milhões após 12 meses; e R$ 160 milhões após 24 meses. Investimentos em hidrogênio aumentam 33% Em hidrogênio de baixa emissão de carbono, a Petrobras planeja investir, entre 2027 e 2031, cerca de US$ 600 milhões. No plano de negócios anterior, a previsão era de US$ 450 milhões. Assim, a disposição para investimentos aumentou 33,3%. Para 2027, a Petrobras planeja iniciar a operação de uma planta piloto de eletrólise de 2 MW no Vale do Açu, no Rio Grande do Norte. No PN 2026-2030, a operação da unidade constava como prevista para 2026. Em 2030, a Petrobras prevê operar outra planta piloto de eletrólise, com 20 MW de potência, na Refinaria de Paulínia, em São Paulo. A estatal também informou sobre parcerias em uma planta de amônia de baixo carbono na Bahia, e de uma planta de e-metanol em São Paulo. Ambas as fábricas têm previsão de operação a partir de 2030. Investimento total para o período Para o período de 2027 a 2031, a Petrobras prevê o investimento de US$ 122 bilhões, sendo US$ 113 bilhões em Implantação e US$ 9 bilhões na Carteira de Avaliação, composta por oportunidades com menor grau de maturidade. A divisão de gás e baixo carbono tem um total de US$ 8 bilhões previstos, sendo US$ 4 bilhões em cada carteira. Esta divisão também inclui projetos em gás natural, biorrefino e biocombustíveis, como etanol, além de captura e armazenamento de carbono (CCS, na sigla em inglês). Para estes negócios, a Petrobras calcula uma taxa interna de retorno média nominal (TIR) superior a 12%. O negócio que deve receber a maior fatia de investimentos é o segmento de Exploração & Produção, com US$ 87 bilhões no total, sendo US$ 83 bilhões em implantação e US$ 3 bilhões em avaliação. A TIR dos grandes projetos de E&P com primeiro óleo a partir de 2027 é de 20%. *Nota atualizada às 14h58 para incluir a compra de 70% da Logum, e às 17h59 para correção do investimen

artigo.texto: - Renewable - 1 min read L&T wins ₹1,000-2,500 crore order for battery storage project in Gujarat The project would feature a three-hour battery energy storage system, with a power capacity of 300 MW and an energy storage capacity of 900 MWh. L&T bags ₹1,000-2,500 crore order to develop 300 MW/900 MWh battery storage project in Gujarat, strengthening renewable energy integration and grid stability. Larsen & Toubro (L&T) on Wednesday said it has secured a significant order to develop a battery energy storage system (BESS) with a capacity of 300 MW/900 MWh at Khavda in Gujarat. As per the company's internal classification, the order falls in the ₹1,000 crore to ₹2,500 crore range. The project will be jointly executed by two of the company's businesses — its Renewables business and L&T Electronic Products & Systems (LTEPS). L&T said the project would feature a three-hour battery energy storage system, with a power capacity of 300 MW and an energy storage capacity of 900 MWh. The battery storage facility is designed to store surplus renewable energy during periods of high generation and release it when power demand peaks. According to L&T, this will help maximise the utilisation of clean energy while strengthening grid stability and improving the flexibility and reliability of power supply. The project will also incorporate liquid-cooling technology. L&T said the advanced battery energy storage solution would use this technology to achieve higher power density, improve safety, and extend the facility's operating life. The company said the facility would play an important role in improving grid flexibility and enabling greater integration of renewable energy into India's power network. The order also strengthens L&T's presence in the energy storage segment, where it aims to leverage its capabilities in delivering large, complex projects.

artigo.texto: [South Korea Forum Weighs Inverter Security in Storage Tenders] At an energy forum in Seoul, Kim Jae-eon, an electrical engineering professor at Chungbuk National University, argued that storage tenders should score inverter security. He said tampering with inverter core software could disrupt battery charging and discharging and threaten the power supply it supports. Some Chinese-made units are sold in Korea under Korean brands, so the equipment name may not match the factory that built it. Kim proposed certification standards so security is weighed alongside price. Korea's storage tender this year does not explicitly score hacking or tampering resistance. Wood Mackenzie reported in June that Chinese-headquartered integrators held 76% of the global storage system market in 2025, with eight of the top 10 based in China. The FCC added foreign-produced inverters to its Covered List on July 28, revised in August to cover remotely reachable models, with exemptions. IRS Notice 2026-15 requires storage projects starting construction after 2025 claiming the 48E credit to assess prohibited foreign entity assistance.

artigo.texto: A fábrica da BYD e o Norte de Minas: torcida ou estratégia? AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 23 de novembro de 2026 A disputa por uma nova fábrica de veículos elétricos mobilizou cidades do Norte de Minas nas redes sociais. Mas o que pesa na decisão de uma montadora? E o que o lítio da região tem a ver com isso? A notícia correu rápido. A BYD, montadora chinesa que já produz carros elétricos e híbridos em Camaçari (BA), avalia investir cerca de R$ 1 bi em uma segunda fábrica no Brasil, desta vez de vans e caminhões elétricos, com previsão de 2 mil empregos. Minas Gerais disputa o projeto com São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro. O governador eleito, Cleitinho Azevedo, afirmou que pretende procurar o presidente da empresa para apresentar o estado. Nas redes sociais, a disputa ganhou contornos locais. Moradores de Araçuaí, Capelinha e outras cidades do Norte de Minas e do Vale do Jequitinhonha passaram a defender que a fábrica fique na sua cidade. Em alguns comentários, a defesa de uma cidade vem acompanhada de ataques à vizinha: uma “não tem água”, outra “não tem estrutura”. A mobilização é legítima e mostra uma região que quer crescer. Mas vale perguntar: até onde essa torcida ajuda, e a partir de que ponto ela atrapalha? O que uma montadora procura Empresas desse porte não escolhem endereço por curtidas. A decisão costuma levar em conta: • Logística: rodovias, ferrovias e acesso a portos, para receber peças e entregar veículos. • Mercado e fornecedores: proximidade dos grandes centros consumidores e das empresas que fornecem componentes. • Infraestrutura: terreno, energia elétrica em quantidade, água e saneamento. • Mão de obra: trabalhadores qualificados ou condições para formá-los. • Segurança jurídica e incentivos: regras estáveis, licenças com prazos previsíveis e condições negociadas com o governo. Camaçari é um bom exemplo. A BYD ocupou o antigo complexo da Ford, num polo industrial já estruturado. E, segundo a imprensa baiana, 86% dos trabalhadores da fábrica são da Bahia: a mão de obra local pesa, desde que esteja preparada. E o lítio? O Norte de Minas e o Jequitinhonha vivem um momento raro. Empresas como Sigma Lithium, CBL, PLS Brasil (Projeto Colina), Lithium Ionic e Atlas Lithium têm minas em operação ou projetos em desenvolvimento na região, de olho no lítio usado em baterias. É natural ligar uma coisa à outra, já que a BYD aposta nas várias etapas da produção, da bateria ao veículo. Mas o lítio sai das minas mineiras ainda como concentrado, e o país tem poucas das etapas que o transformam em bateria. Ter lítio por perto ajuda a contar uma boa história, mas não garante, sozinho, uma fábrica de veículos. Um polo tecnológico no Jequitinhonha? A oportunidade pode ser maior do que uma fábrica. O Vale do Jequitinhonha tem condições de se tornar um polo tecnológico, reunindo no mesmo território: • mineradoras, que extraem e beneficiam o lítio; • empresas de conversão química, que transformam o concentrado em carbonato e hidróxido de lítio; • indústrias que usam esses produtos, como fabricantes de baterias e de veículos; • formação de pessoas, com Senai, cursos técnicos, institutos federais e universidades; • pesquisa e tecnologia, com a academia trabalhando ao lado das empresas. Cada elo atrai o seguinte. Uma fábrica como a da BYD seria uma peça desse polo, não a única. O maior obstáculo hoje é a infraestrutura, em especial as estradas. Para que um polo funcione, a produção precisa chegar com rapidez e segurança aos centros consumidores e aos portos. Em apresentação à Câmara dos Deputados, o próprio Ministério de Minas e Energia listou trechos de rodovias, como a BR-367, entre as obras importantes para o transporte do lítio. Torcida que ajuda, rivalidade que atrapalha Uma cidade que se mobiliza mostra disposição. Mas quem investe olha a região como um todo. Quando cidades vizinhas trocam acusações sem base técnica, o recado que fica é de conflito, não de oportunidade. E a disputa real não é entre Araçuaí, Capelinha ou Salinas: é entre Minas, São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro. Além disso, a cidade vizinha não é concorrente. O desenvolvimento de uma ajuda as outras: trabalhadores circulam entre elas, fornecedores de um município atendem empresas do outro e o dinheiro dos salários se espalha pelo comércio de toda a região. Um grande investimento em qualquer uma delas movimenta também as do entorno. Há um risco maior: transformar cada grande investimento em disputa política ou em boato. Regiões com fama de instáveis, onde a desinformação se espalha e as regras mudam, parecem mais caras e arriscadas para quem decide onde investir. Preparar-se para o desenvolvimento A fábrica pode vir para Minas ou não. Pode vir para o Norte ou para outra região. Mas a lição vale para qualquer cenário: as cidades que se destacam são as que se preparam. Qualificam trabalhadores, organizam dados confiáveis, melhoram a infraestrutura e atuam juntas, como região. artigo.texto: Mulilo has achieved commercial and financial close for its 77 MW / 308 MWh Leeuwpoort Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in South Africa, marking another major milestone in the development of the country’s grid-supporting energy infrastructure. The project is located near Carletonville in the Merafong City Local Municipality, Gauteng, and will connect to the Midas Main Transmission Substation. Leeuwpoort is the first large-scale battery energy storage project in Gauteng to reach financial close. It is expected to strengthen grid stability, improve energy flexibility and support electricity supply in an industrial region with significant mining activity. The project will contribute to South Africa’s efforts to modernize its electricity network and accelerate the transition towards a more reliable and sustainable energy system. The project was awarded under Bid Window 2 of South Africa’s Battery Energy Storage Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme (BESIPPPP). It is the third Mulilo battery storage project to achieve financial close in 2026, following the successful progression of the Mercury and Hartebeesfontein BESS projects. The Leeuwpoort facility will incorporate the Haohan battery energy storage system supplied by BYD Energy Storage. Once operational, it will provide storage capacity and ancillary services to the national transmission system under a 15-year power purchase agreement with the National Transmission Company South Africa (NTCSA). Mulilo will serve as the lead sponsor and oversee several key activities throughout the project’s lifecycle. These responsibilities include construction management, asset management, operations and maintenance oversight, and social impact management. The project also includes a partnership structure aimed at promoting local participation and sharing economic benefits. Reatile Group is serving as the strategic empowerment partner, while a local community trust will ensure long-term community participation and socio-economic opportunities. Commenting on the financial close, Mulilo CEO Jan Fourie said the milestone reflects the company’s commitment to strengthening South Africa’s energy system through utility-scale battery storage. He highlighted the importance of projects such as Leeuwpoort in improving grid stability, unlocking network capacity and supporting energy security. He also emphasized the company’s commitment to delivering long-term value and creating economic opportunities for local communities. Reatile Group Chief Commercial Officer Sunette Smith said the company was proud to partner on the project, describing it as an important investment in South Africa’s energy security and the development of a more resilient and sustainable energy system. The financial close was supported by Mulilo’s shareholders, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Norfund, alongside Reatile Group and several government and energy-sector institutions. These included the Department of Electricity and Energy, Eskom, the Independent Power Producers Office, NTCSA and Merafong City Local Municipality. Financing was arranged through a consortium of lenders comprising Absa Bank, Nedbank and Standard Bank of South Africa. Key advisers included Arup, Bastion, Bowmans, Deloitte, ENS, Fasken, Marsh and Pepper Tree Capital. With Leeuwpoort reaching financial close, Mulilo continues to expand its battery storage portfolio, supporting South Africa’s growing need for flexible grid infrastructure and reliable electricity supply. Em meio à uma ofensiva da indústria eólica para judicializar os leilões de baterias, a Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (Absae) saiu em defesa, nesta segunda (23/11) de uma solução política sobre o rateio de custos, sem prejuízo da concorrência marcada para a próxima semana. Segundo a entidade, a contratação é urgente, uma vez que os projetos precisam começar a operar em agosto de 2028. A Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) prevê a necessidade adicional de 5,5 gigawatts (GW) de potência no sistema em 2028. Entretanto, detalhes do certame marcado para os dias 2 e 4 de dezembro, como o rateio dos encargos, ainda são tema de debates no setor. Na semana passada, a Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (Abeeólica) entrou com uma ação no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) contra a regra que prevê que exclusivamente os geradores de energia arquem com os custos de contratação. A entidade já tinha entrado com uma ação civil pública para suspender os certames. Paralelamente, na Câmara dos Deputados, o PL 3.716/2026, que altera o rateio, tramita em regime de urgência e aguarda designação de relator na Comissão de Constituição e Justiça e de Cidadania (CCJC). A matéria é apoiada por diversas associações do setor, incluindo a Absae. Segundo a entidade, as ações judiciais apresentadas nas últimas semanas fazem parte do processo e não alteram a necessidade dos leilões em dezembro. “Na avaliação da Absae, elas têm origem em uma questão de fundo que deve ser resolvida no campo político, e essa solução, ainda que urgente, pode ser concluída após as sessões públicas, sem comprometer os leilões”, diz a associação em nota. Para o diretor-executivo da Absae, Fabio Lima, o problema não está na condução dos certames, mas na Lei 15.269/2025, que deu ao armazenamento em baterias um tratamento diferente do dado às demais soluções de potência, retirando o consumidor do rateio. “O leilão está no prazo, as regras estão definidas e o mercado está mobilizado. O Brasil precisa dessa potência e flexibilidade em 2028, e cada etapa cumprida agora é tempo garantido para a implantação dos projetos”, defende Lima. “A discussão sobre os encargos deve avançar, mas não pode impedir os certames. Defendemos uma solução legislativa para corrigir essa assimetria, com o avanço do PL 3.716/2026 e sua aplicação também aos leilões em andamento”, completa.

artigo.texto: Prós e contras da IA: como data centers influenciam aquecimento global Especialista em IA analisa como o avanço da tecnologia intensifica o consumo de energia e água nos data centers Os data centers, infraestruturas essenciais para o funcionamento da inteligência artificial, estão no centro de uma preocupação ambiental crescente. O especialista em IA e colunista da CNN Brasil, Álvaro Machado, analisou como o avanço acelerado da IA tem ampliado a demanda energética dessas instalações e quais são as implicações para o aquecimento global. Segundo Machado, o principal impacto dos data centers no meio ambiente ocorre devido a uma expansão acelerada antes de usinas sustentáveis estarem disponíveis. "Tem usinas que demoram anos para estar em operação e os data centers precisam entrar em atividade rapidamente", explicou. Com isso, há um período — que pode se estender por dois a cinco anos — em que essas instalações operam com base em combustíveis fósseis. Demanda energética comparável à de grandes países A dimensão do consumo energético dos data centers é expressiva. A projeção, segundo Machado, é que em 2030 essa demanda ultrapasse a de um país como o Japão, chegando a cerca de 100 terawatts-hora por ano — o equivalente a aproximadamente 13 usinas de Itaipu. Apesar disso, o especialista ponderou que isso não significa que os data centers necessariamente contribuirão para o aquecimento global na próxima década. "A ideia é que os data centers usem cada vez mais energias renováveis", afirmou. Para ele, trata-se de uma indústria em transição: "eles são poluentes, muitas vezes construídos sem respeitar normas ambientais, mas é uma indústria que tende a ser menos poluente do que, por exemplo, a automobilística". Inteligência artificial como aliada do clima Além dos desafios, Machado destacou o potencial da inteligência artificial como ferramenta de combate às mudanças climáticas. O especialista apontou dois caminhos principais. O primeiro é o estímulo à substituição de fontes fósseis por matrizes renováveis. "No Brasil, os projetos de data centers são projetos que usam energia eólica, solar, hidrelétrica", disse, acrescentando que a energia nuclear também tem sido considerada, dada a longevidade desses projetos. O segundo caminho, descrito por Machado como "muito mais interessante", envolve o uso da IA no desenvolvimento de novos materiais. Ele citou como exemplo o MOF (Metal-Organic Framework), uma estrutura metálica capaz de capturar carbono na atmosfera. "A promessa é que a inteligência artificial ajude no desenvolvimento dessas novas moléculas e a gente tenha como melhorar reagindo ao problema do clima ativamente através da tecnologia", concluiu. Nvidia e os impactos geopolíticos da expansão dos data centers Machado também comentou o papel da NVIDIA nesse cenário. Para ele, a empresa tem o maior interesse do mercado na expansão acelerada dos data centers — justamente o período em que mais energia de base fóssil é consumida. O especialista avaliou que a companhia pode desacelerar esse ritmo e "ganhar um pouco mais de consciência social". Sobre quem ganha e quem perde com os movimentos recentes no setor, o especialista avaliou que os beneficiados serão aqueles do lado do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. Ele citou o Brasil como exemplo de país prejudicado, em razão de restrições impostas à venda de placas de vídeo para o país.

artigo.texto: A Moura obteve o credenciamento do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) na rota 2 do regulamento setorial do CFI-Finame para um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) destinado ao leilão de reserva de capacidade na forma de potência (LRCap). O equipamento, que terá a tecnologia da chinesa CATL, será feito no complexo produtivo da companhia em Belo Jardim, no Pernambuco, e será fornecido a empresas participantes da rodada do certame com exigência de conteúdo nacional, marcada para 2 de dezembro de 2026. A rota 2 de credenciamento do BNDES para BESS exige a montagem leve do pack de bateria no Brasil, além do cumprimento do índice mínimo de conteúdo local. Além disso, projetos enquadrados nas rotas 2,3 e 4 têm acesso a até 100% de financiamento via Fundo Clima, com custo nominal de 6,5% ao ano. Na Rota 1, o limite é de até 80%, observadas as regras aplicáveis e a aprovação de cada operação. Segundo a companhia, a escolha da Rota 2 está relacionada ao modelo de industrialização adotado pela Moura. Diferentemente de modalidades que permitem cumprir os requisitos de nacionalização por meio de componentes complementares, essa rota considera processos produtivos ligados ao próprio sistema de baterias, que representa uma parcela expressiva do valor total de um BESS. A Moura informou ainda que essa configuração permite alcançar índices mais elevados de conteúdo nacional e amplia a margem de segurança no atendimento às exigências do leilão. Para os investidores, o credenciamento reduz o risco de desenquadramento dos projetos em relação aos critérios de nacionalização. Em nota enviada à MegaWhat, a Moura informou que seu sistema supera 50% de conteúdo nacional. Segundo a companhia, o cálculo considera, na rota 2, a montagem dos módulos fornecidos pela CATL nos contêineres, a integração dos sistemas eletrônicos e térmicos, além de outros componentes adquiridos de fornecedores nacionais. >> Leia também: Moura pede tarifa zero para importação de baterias destinadas ao LRCap Investimento de R$ 200 milhões em Belo Jardim O modelo industrial da Moura prevê a montagem e integração de módulos de baterias, eletrônica de controle e sistemas de refrigeração, além da incorporação de componentes adquiridos de fornecedores nacionais. A tecnologia de armazenamento será fornecida pela Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (CATL), empresa global do segmento. Para atender às empresas participantes do LRCap, a Moura prevê investir cerca de R$ 200 milhões na ampliação e modernização do complexo industrial de Belo Jardim. A companhia também anunciou capacidade de fornecimento superior a 8 GWh. “Escolhemos uma rota que exige maior participação industrial no Brasil e proporciona uma margem importante de conteúdo nacional. Para quem vai assumir compromissos de fornecimento de potência por 15 anos, isso representa mais segurança e previsibilidade. Nosso diferencial é combinar tecnologia de referência internacional, capacidade industrial brasileira e experiência concreta em armazenamento de energia”, destaca Spartacus Pedrosa, diretor de Operações de Lítio da Moura. Em nota, a companhia destacou que sua estratégia vai além da participação no primeiro leilão. A Moura defende a previsibilidade de novas contratações para sustentar a expansão industrial, a formação de profissionais, o desenvolvimento de fornecedores e a nacionalização progressiva da cadeia brasileira de armazenamento de energia.

artigo.texto: Ameren’s Lincoln County battery energy storage project has residents concerned By Stan Schwartz Troy Free Press Last Wednesday, about 150 people came together in Troy to discuss what, if anything, could be done about the Battery Energy Storage System Ameren has slated for construction in northern Lincoln County. Kenzie Aubuchon’s farm is 1.3 miles from the proposed BESS site. She said Ameren has been trying to buy her family’s land for months. She stated emphatically she does not want to sell. But the possible contamination that could come from an onsite disaster, brought her to the Lincoln County Knights of Columbus for this town hall meeting, which was hosted by Aligned Mommas, a group whose organizers have opposed Ameren’s proposed 250 megawatt BESS slated for northern Lincoln County. “I own 140 acres of a seventh-generation farm … there is no price tag on this farm but (if there’s a disaster) … I cannot return to this farm. I do not want to sell this farm, either. I don’t want Ameren to pay me for it, it is still my farm but how am I going to be compensated? Where am I going to move? How am I going to be compensated for livestock loss? What is my life going to look like moving forward from a disaster?” Nikki Trout, one of the women who started Aligned Mommas, said, “Every opinion should matter, not just the head guy at the fire department or the school board or, you know, XYZ business. It should be all of us coming together. We’re on the same team.” Lincoln County Commissioner Mike Mueller attended the town hall to learn more about the citizens’ concerns on the BESS. “We know that our commissioners are good men,” she added, “and we know that there’s probably things going on behind the scenes that we’re not aware of.” Trout also noted her group is not opposed to AI. “There are many members on our team who use it. Where the conflict comes in, are with unregulated data centers that capture land that has no planning and zoning (oversight) and really there’s no right for the local community to fight back or say no, or have any right or opinion,” she said. She also noted they are not mad or upset with any land owner who sold their property or is in a contract or lease with Ameren. “You do what’s right for your family,” she said. We know that they (Ameren) was knocking on the doors, hard.” She invited representatives from Ameren to attend, but they declined. Rep. Doyle Justus and Troy Alderman Conor Martin, as well as Moscow Mills Mayor Lisa Meyer and Troy Mayor Quentin Laws attended. Geoff Marke from the Missouri Public Service Commission, Office of the Public Council, spoke as well. Aubuchon was also there to read a statement from Mary Geede, who has been researching what a BESS does and the effects it could have on the community. She noted Geede started her quest because of concerns with the county’s water supply. “’You turned on your faucet. Maybe you filled a glass of water for your child’s water bottle before school. You trusted that water and for many of us in Lincoln County, that water comes from a private well. Our children drink it, we cook with it and our children play in the creeks and streams throughout our community. When I learned about Ameren’s proposed battery storage facility in the Millcreek area, my first question was simple. ‘Where is the water going to go? When it rains, where does the runoff travel? What happens during equipment maintenance and cleaning? What keeps it from reaching our creeks and groundwater? ‘If I can’t stop this project, I want to do everything I reasonably can to make it safer.’” Geede’s advocated for a properly engineered water basin management system that not only controls runoff and protects surrounding waterways and watersheds, but also includes the ability to capture, contain, and prevent the release of potentially contaminated water in the event of an accident or an emergency. “’I want to see how the systems are designed and what they’re capable of containing and how they’re maintained,” Geede stated. “I also want qualified professionals to determine appropriate baseline water testing for nearby creeks and private wells.” Laws, who is Troy’s mayor and Lincoln County’s Emergency Coordinator, said he was concerned about what would happen during a disaster. “If something happens, what happens at the school? Do we shelter in place? What do we do with livestock? I mean, what do we do with our fire department people? Are they gonna be trained? Are they gonna have everything they need? We just want some real answers.” He explained those questions would be determined by the layout of the battery systems, the wind, the weather, even the heat from the sunshine. “There’s a thousand points of information that I have to take in while I’m also driving to a scene,” he said. He noted by state statute, the school districts are told they have to have their own emergency operations plan because, legally, they’re in charge of their students. They could incorporate those plans into the city’s and county’s plans. Geoff Marke, the chief economist with the Missouri Office of Public Counsel, said, “On the safety issue, … when Ameren says they’re gonna purchase the equipment, they’re gonna do that sort of stuff. Re-translated, that means rate payers are paying for that.”

artigo.texto: Semtech Q3 CY2026 deep dive: Data center surge and LoRa expansion shape outlook Semiconductor company Semtech SMTC beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in calendar Q3 2026 [fiscal Q3 2027], with sales up 58.4% year on year to $423 million. On top of that, next quarter’s revenue guidance ($480 million at the midpoint) was surprisingly good and 6.6% above what analysts were expecting. Its non-GAAP profit of $1.17 per share was 3.3% above analysts’ consensus estimates. Semtech Q3 CY2026 highlights: - Revenue $423 million vs S&P analyst consensus of $416.5 million (58.4% year-on-year growth, 1.6% beat) - Adjusted EPS $1.17 vs S&P analyst consensus of $1.13 (3.3% beat) - Adjusted EBITDA $145.8 million vs analyst estimates of $136.7 million (34.5% margin, 6.7% beat) - Revenue guidance $480 million at the midpoint for Q4 CY2026, above analyst estimates of $450.4 million - Adjusted EPS guidance $1.33 at the midpoint for Q4 CY2026, above analyst estimates of $1.29 - EBITDA guidance $166.4 million at the midpoint for Q4 CY2026, above analyst estimates of $150.4 million - Operating margin 26.3%, up from 11.6% in the same quarter last year - Inventory days outstanding 96, down from 98 in the previous quarter - Market capitalization $9.72 billion StockStory’s take Semtech’s third quarter saw robust top-line growth and margin expansion, yet the market responded with skepticism, sending shares down significantly after the report. Management pointed to exceptional momentum in its data center business and ongoing strength in LoRa-enabled products as primary drivers of performance. CEO Hong Hou highlighted that “Semtech team delivered another quarter of record financial results, driven by significant growth across our broad data center portfolio and LoRa,” noting continued leadership in 800G optical components and a ramp in 1.6T solutions. The company also credited disciplined operating expense management and increased adoption of its products by hyperscale customers for underpinning strong operational leverage. Looking ahead, Semtech’s guidance reflects confidence in sustained demand from data center customers and further expansion of the LoRa platform. Management emphasized a record backlog and recent design wins across hyperscale cloud providers as key contributors to its outlook. CFO Mark Lin explained that gross margin improvements are expected to be supported by a favorable mix shift toward higher-margin data center and LoRa products, although the company is investing in research and development to accelerate new offerings, especially in photonics. CEO Hong Hou added, “We are confident in the growth framework we outlined at our Analyst Day,” underscoring expectations for continued market share gains and new product ramps. Key insights from management’s remarks Management attributed the quarter’s performance to strong execution in next-generation data center connectivity and traction for LoRa across industrial and consumer segments. - Data center momentum: Semtech’s data center portfolio, including optical, copper, and photonics solutions, experienced significant growth as hyperscale customers ramped up deployments for AI-driven workloads. The company’s 800G products maintained substantial market share, while the 1.6T transition is underway, with management expecting further share gains as industry adoption increases. - LoRa platform expansion: LoRa-enabled products saw record sales, driven by new use cases in smart home, security, and edge AI applications. Semtech demonstrated the LoRa Plus platform’s dual-band capability and multi-protocol support, positioning it as a foundation for future edge intelligence and satellite connectivity. - Active copper advances: The CopperEdge line won new design wins at multiple hyperscale customers, including key applications in both rack-level and onboard interconnects. Management highlighted that linear equalizer solutions delivered lower power and latency compared to traditional retimers, a factor expected to drive broader industry adoption. - Photonics capacity scaling: Semtech continued to invest in expanding photonics manufacturing, supporting demand for higher-performance lasers and optical engines. The company expects this segment to become more margin accretive as scale and new product introductions accelerate. - Security and industrial IoT: In the IoT segment, AirLink routers now integrate with leading cybersecurity platforms and meet federal security standards, broadening Semtech’s reach into mission-critical infrastructure and public safety deployments. Drivers of future performance Semtech’s outlook is shaped by ongoing AI infrastructure buildout, new product ramps, and a strategic shift toward higher-margin solutions. - AI-driven data center growth: Management sees sustained demand for high-speed interconnects as cloud and AI providers upgrade infrastructure. The company expects its transition from 800G to 1.6T products, along with new design wins in both copper and optical segments, to drive above-market growth and margin improvements. - LoRa and IoT diversification: Continued momentum in LoRa, with new features such as multi-protocol support and integration with platforms like Amazon Sidewalk, is expected to further expand addressable markets in industrial, smart home, and public safety applications. - Photonics and margin evolution: Investments in photonics capacity are projected to deliver higher-margin revenue as new lasers and optical components ramp. Management cautioned that near-term margin improvement will depend on product mix and the pace of photonics adoption, with long-term targets anchored in scaling these newer segments. artigo.texto: Malaysian developer Kerjaya Prospek Property Bhd has said one of its subsidiaries is buying 34 battery energy storage system (BESS) units in a deal worth about MYR 5.26 million. The units will go into Menara Vista Petaling, home to the developer’s Bloomsvale project on Old Klang Road in Kuala Lumpur. The order has been placed with a 70%-owned unit of ES Sunlogy Bhd, an engineering firm in which construction group Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd holds a 31% stake. It is the latest in a run of business deals between the Kerjaya companies and ES Sunlogy. Representative image Kerjaya Prospek Property Bhd (KPPROP), formerly known as GSB Group Bhd, has told Bursa Malaysia that one of its units is acquiring 34 battery energy storage system units. The purchase is valued at MYR 5.26 million. Advertisement The buyer is Kerjaya Property Sdn Bhd (KPSB). It placed the order with Sunlogy Asia Energy Storage Sdn Bhd (SAES), a 70%-owned subsidiary of ES Sunlogy Bhd, which accepted it on Tuesday. The order covers the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of the units at Menara Vista Petaling in Kuala Lumpur, at a fixed value of MYR 5,260,619. Menara Vista Petaling is the site of Bloomsvale, the developer’s mixed-use project. It sits on 5.2 acres of freehold land along Jalan Klang Lama (Old Klang Road). Its serviced residence tower has 66 floors and 1,199 units and was completed in 2023. The development also has retail and office space, which adds to the group’s recurring income. A BESS stores surplus electricity for later use. For a building, it helps keep energy costs steady, cushion grid disruptions and manage peak power demand. The order is a related-party deal. Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd holds a 31% equity interest in ES Sunlogy. ES Sunlogy said it had no other transactions with KPSB in the previous 12 months, so its total dealings with KPSB over that period equal the value of this order. Kerjaya Prospek Group chairman Datuk Seri Tee Eng Ho, along with members of his family, has interests in KPPROP. Kerjaya Prospek Group built its ES Sunlogy stake in quick steps. It first subscribed to 70 million new shares for MYR 18.76 million in July, taking a 9.09% stake. It then bought 19.18% for MYR 40.18 million and a further 2.73% for MYR 5.36 million, reaching 31%. In all, it invested about MYR 64.31 million. The chairman said the group intends to keep the stake at 31% for now, which is about two percentage points below the 33% level that would trigger a mandatory general offer. The two groups have worked together for years. ES Sunlogy shareholders approved a recurrent related-party transactions mandate last month to ease routine dealings with Kerjaya Prospek. Earlier this month, ES Sunlogy’s unit Savelite Engineering won two subcontracts worth a combined MYR 25.07 million from Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd for electrical and infrastructure works on Pulau Andaman in Penang. Savelite had also secured an electrical subcontract from Kerjaya Prospek (M) at the start of the year for a development by Pixel Valley Sdn Bhd, a KPPROP unit. Battery storage is a growing line for ES Sunlogy. The company has already put battery systems at construction sites in Singapore to cut the use of diesel generators. It plans to take part in the Large Scale Solar 6 (LSS6) programme as a developer, aiming for at least 100MW with a battery storage component. For KPPROP, the purchase comes as it lines up new projects. The developer has a serviced apartment pipeline with an estimated gross development value of about MYR 2 billion over the next one to two years, backed by a 60-acre landbank. The order is small in value, but it is one of the first times a Kerjaya company has bought battery storage from ES Sunlogy rather than only electrical works. How the 34 units perform in a busy mixed-use building could decide whether similar systems are fitted in the developer’s upcoming serviced apartments. Investors are also likely to keep an eye on the growing number of related-party deals between the companies, since Bursa rules require such transactions to be added together when judging their size. Malaysia’s Energy Commission has also set out safety guidelines for battery storage systems, which will apply to installations of this kind. artigo.texto: O BYD Dolphin GT, novo hatch híbrido plug-in da montadora chinesa, já começou a chegar ao Brasil antes do lançamento, previsto para o primeiro trimestre de 2027. Imagens divulgadas pela página Auto Rod Motors mostram dezenas de unidades estacionadas num pátio no Espírito Santo, sinal de que a fabricante começou a formar estoque para a estreia comercial. Os carros aparecem nas cores cinza e vermelho, sem camuflagem. A movimentação acontece cerca de um mês depois da chegada das primeiras unidades destinadas a testes e validações no mercado brasileiro. A expectativa é que o Dolphin GT se torne o híbrido mais barato da BYD no País, posicionado abaixo do SUV Atto 2 e do sedã King. O preço ainda não foi divulgado. Leia também - Carros de GTA 6 são mais realistas e trazem até combustível, mas não deixam diversão de lado - CFMoto abre novo lote de reservas no Brasil no dia 30 de novembro; veja preços Apesar do nome, o novo modelo não é só uma versão híbrida do Dolphin elétrico vendido hoje no Brasil. É um projeto diferente, com carroceria própria e sistema de propulsão que combina motor a combustão e motor elétrico. Dolphin GT pode ter motor híbrido flex Na Europa, o hatch é vendido como Dolphin G e usa a quinta geração do sistema híbrido plug-in DM-i da BYD. O conjunto combina um motor 1.5 aspirado a gasolina com um propulsor elétrico, com potência combinada de cerca de 176 cv a 212 cv, conforme a versão. O modelo tem duas opções de bateria, de 7,4 kWh e 18,3 kWh. Na configuração mais completa, a autonomia no modo totalmente elétrico chega a 105 quilômetros pelo ciclo europeu WLTP. Para o Brasil, a expectativa é que o conjunto seja adaptado para funcionar também com etanol. A BYD, porém, ainda não confirmou as especificações da versão nacional. O Dolphin GT mede 4,16 metros de comprimento e tem 2,61 metros de entre-eixos. O porta-malas leva 425 litros, que podem chegar a 1.225 litros com o banco traseiro rebatido. Produção brasileira está nos planos da BYD A chegada das unidades importadas antecede a produção nacional do Dolphin GT, prevista para a fábrica da BYD em Camaçari, na Bahia. A unidade ainda passa por ampliação. Em outubro, a fabricante informou que as áreas de soldagem e pintura estavam em fase final de testes operacionais, enquanto a estamparia seguia em construção. Por isso, a expectativa é que as primeiras unidades vendidas no Brasil sejam importadas, até que a fábrica consiga assumir uma parte maior da produção. A nacionalização do Dolphin GT faz parte da estratégia da BYD para ampliar sua presença no mercado brasileiro de eletrificados. Com o hatch, a marca pode disputar uma faixa de preço hoje ocupada principalmente por compactos a combustão e por híbridos convencionais. Ainda não há confirmação oficial sobre preço, versões ou data exata de lançamento do BYD Dolphin GT no Brasil. Carregando ofertas...

artigo.texto: India’s rapid renewable capacity addition, which continues to outpace transmission augmentation, particularly in resource-rich states such as Rajasthan and Gujarat, is increasing grid congestion and the need for storage to absorb surplus generation, shift supply to non-solar hours and ease network constraints. The country's battery energy storage system (BESS) market is moving from tendering to execution, backed by strong policy support and a large tender pipeline, ratings agency ICRA said in a report. "However, the rebound in battery prices, rupee depreciation and aggressive bids make timely battery procurement, robust long-term service agreements and offtake tie-ups critical for project viability," it said. According to the report, strong energy storage demand and a sizeable tender pipeline are supporting growth in the sector, but execution remains a key monitorable. "Operational BESS capacity is also rising, signalling progress from tendering to deployment. Policy support, including the government's Viability Gap Funding schemes announced in 2023, 2025 and 2026 covering 135.8 gigawatt-hours, provides a significant source of capital support," the report said. ICRA added that the viability of the recently aggressively bid projects would critically depend on battery procurement costs and currency movements. For developers in the renewable energy sector, costs not covered by the supplier, including performance penalties, additional batteries and post-warranty maintenance, are important risks. "At a battery pack cost of USD 70 per kilowatt-hour, the cumulative debt service coverage ratio of 1.17-1.27 times is expected at tariffs of Rs 2.60-2.80 lakh per megawatt per month. Competitive procurement and protection against cost escalation remain central to the assessment," the report said. It added that lower upfront funding and supplier guarantees do not eliminate future costs and operating risks, and project assessment should account for eventual duty payments and check whether supplier guarantees adequately cover commitments to the power buyer.

artigo.texto: O Projeto de Lei nº 3.716/2026 pode aumentar o custo da conta de luz dos consumidores brasileiros em até R$ 6,26 bilhões por ano. A estimativa é da Frente Nacional dos Consumidores de Energia (FNCE), que alerta para o impacto da proposta de transferir para todos os consumidores as despesas com sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias. A proposta tramita em regime de urgência na Câmara dos Deputados e propõe retirar dos geradores a obrigação exclusiva de custear a contratação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias como reserva de capacidade. De acordo com a análise técnica da entidade, o custo acumulado pode chegar a aproximadamente R$ 94 bilhões ao longo de 15 anos, período previsto no edital do leilão de baterias marcado para dezembro de 2026. Para a FNCE, a mudança é injusta porque socializa um custo que deveria ser assumido pelos geradores que demandam a contratação dos sistemas de armazenamento. Custo das baterias na conta de luz A estimativa da FNCE considera a receita fixa anual que seria paga como Encargo de Reserva de Capacidade (ERCap) para financiar sistemas de baterias associados a usinas solares, eólicas e outras fontes intermitentes de energia. O estudo utilizou os preços-teto previstos no edital do leilão de baterias e as projeções da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) como referência para estimar um volume máximo de 5 GW em possíveis contratações. A análise apresenta dois cenários de contratação. O primeiro é de 1 GW de cada produto, totalizando 2 GW, com custo estimado de R$ 2,5 bilhões por ano e R$ 37,5 bilhões acumulados em 15 anos. Já o segundo cenário prevê uma contratação de 2,5 GW de cada produto, totalizando 5 GW, com custo estimado de R$ 6,26 bilhões por ano e R$ 94 bilhões acumulados em 15 anos. As estimativas consideram um desconto de 25% sobre os preços-teto do leilão. Para o produto nacional, foi utilizado o valor de R$ 1,76 milhão por MW por ano. Para o produto internacional, a referência foi de R$ 1,58 milhão por MW por ano. Segundo a FNCE, a transferência desses custos para a tarifa de energia poderá aumentar a conta de luz, especialmente para os consumidores residenciais atendidos por distribuidoras cuja contratação de energia é composta majoritariamente por fontes hidrelétricas e termelétricas. FNCE defende manutenção do leilão de baterias Além de questionar a proposta de mudança na legislação, a Frente Nacional dos Consumidores de Energia defende a manutenção do leilão de baterias previsto para dezembro de 2026. A entidade considera prejudiciais as tentativas de suspensão do certame e afirma que o adiamento pode comprometer o enfrentamento dos cortes de geração de energia e dificultar o equilíbrio do sistema elétrico brasileiro. “Não há justificativa técnica ou econômica para mudar o cronograma”, afirmou o presidente da FNCE, Luiz Eduardo Barata. A entidade avalia que a contratação de sistemas de armazenamento é importante para ampliar a eficiência do setor elétrico, reduzir o desperdício de energia renovável e contribuir para a diminuição das emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Baterias podem reduzir corte de renováveis As baterias permitem armazenar energia elétrica para utilização em momentos posteriores, contribuindo para o aproveitamento da geração de fontes renováveis, como a solar e a eólica. A FNCE afirma que a implementação sustentável do armazenamento pode reduzir custos no longo prazo e evitar desperdícios associados ao curtailment. Na avaliação da entidade, o Brasil deveria ter realizado o leilão de baterias antes da contratação de termelétricas no leilão de reserva de capacidade voltado a térmicas e expansão hidrelétrica realizado no primeiro semestre de 2026. A FNCE também argumenta que os geradores que necessitam de sistemas de armazenamento devem assumir os custos relacionados à contratação. Caso a despesa seja transferida para todos os consumidores, poderá haver impacto sobre a inflação e aumento das tarifas de energia para consumidores que, pela composição do portfólio de suas distribuidoras, não precisariam arcar diretamente com essa contratação. A entidade reconhece que os geradores que instalarem baterias poderão repassar os custos aos consumidores que contratarem sua energia, mas considera esse modelo mais adequado do que a criação de um subsídio cruzado para todo o mercado. Segundo a FNCE, as fontes solar e eólica já demonstraram viabilidade econômica e competitividade no mercado de energia, não havendo justificativa para novos subsídios cruzados.

artigo.texto: Hours after the University of Michigan’s Board of Regents voted to approve the University’s and Los Alamos National Laboratory’s planned data center, approximately 350 Ypsilanti Township residents, officials and experts gathered at Eastern Michigan University to oppose the project in a town hall meeting. Attendees condemned the planned data center — which is expected to stretch across 144 acres of the township — and its potential effects on energy costs, water and proximity to indigenous ancestral land. The panelists included Jay Coghlan, executive director of Nuclear Watch New Mexico, a nonprofit that monitors LANL; Michelle Martinez, director of the Tischman Center for Social Justice and the Environment; Ypsilanti Township attorney Doug Winters; Jamie Stuck, the state of Michigan tribal legislative liaison; and state Rep. Jimmy Wilson Jr., D-Ypsilanti. Attendees submitted about 250 written questions to the officials. Coghlan said he believes the choice of the project’s location comes down to one important resource for powering data centers: water. “Why is Los Alamos having the University of Michigan build a data center that’s going to use artificial intelligence to advance new-design nuclear weapons? Why in Ypsilanti?” Coghlan said. “My one-word answer is: water. … (Michigan’s) got water, and we don’t in New Mexico.” Next, Martinez said DTE Energy told shareholders this month it would spend $44 billion over five years to expand its infrastructure, partly to meet data center demand. She said that growth could strain water supplies in two ways: data centers use water on site, and then power plants that supply them, the largest withdrawers of water in Michigan, use even more. “You have this sort of weird trade-off situation with data centers and hyperscale data centers where it’s really difficult to measure,” Martinez said. “And there’s a lot of hydrologists who are increasingly interested in not only what’s being consumed on site, but also what’s being consumed by the power industry.” In response to a question about how to keep the University from buying more land in the township, Wilson Jr. said he plans to reintroduce legislation in January — which he predicts would have bipartisan support — that would require institutions to follow local planning rules when purchasing land outside their home community. The University has indicated that it plans to break ground on the center in late 2027, which it says will expand the University’s computing capabilities and research capacity. Winters argued the project does not serve an educational purpose. “This project is not a University educational purpose,” Winters said. “They have said from day one, this facility is 90% Los Alamos.” Winters then said the township has not set a date to file a legal challenge but does intend to wait until construction begins. “The township board has been very, very adamant that we will use every legal means necessary to stop this,” Winters said. Winters said the Michigan State Historical Preservation Office has advised the University to hire a federal archeologist and contact tribal preservation officers. He told the University the Ypsilanti community’s concerns should be held higher than the potential benefits the data center may provide the University. “You may have extraordinary financial resources,” Winters said. “You may have powerful friends in Lansing and Washington. … but you have come face to face with something your computers cannot calculate, and that is the heart of a community that refuses to be silent.” Ypsilanti Township resident Andy Melichar built a website that compiles residents’ public records requests about the project. He told The Daily he is not broadly opposed to data centers; however, he disagrees with the location of the University’s and Los Alamos’ data center. Experts have criticized the facility for its intended use in nuclear weapons research. “I’m not anti-data center,” Melichar said. “I just am not for putting them where we’re putting them, or for the particular purposes of Los Alamos having nuclear weapons in my backyard. I’m less than a mile away from where they’ll put this in.” Winters told The Daily he believes the project’s most pressing concern for residents is its tie to the federal government, as LANL’s core mission is to solve national security challenges through nuclear weapons design and performance. Michigan’s public universities, including the University, have constitutional autonomy that he believes is being misused in this case. “I think the worst and most pressing issue is the fact that Los Alamos and U-M, has sold its soul to the Department of War,” Winters said. “U-M is a Trojan horse, and they’re abusing their constitutional autonomy by saying, ‘Come on in behind us,’ when … the real dominant partner here is Los Alamos.” Daily News Contributor Eloise Nelson can be reached at eloisen@umich.edu.

artigo.texto: Gelion CEO on Worley partnership, battery scale-up and licensing opportunities Published: 04:50 23 Nov 2026 EST Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF) CEO Matt Wood talked with Proactive about its pre-FEED collaboration with global engineering group Worley to advance production of its nano-encapsulated sulfur (NES) cathode material. Wood explained how Worley's expertise in cathode materials and sulfur processing will help Gelion validate manufacturing processes and develop preliminary designs for a potential pilot plant. The work will cover plant layouts, production requirements, cost estimates and project timelines, helping reduce investment risks ahead of a scale-up decision. The interview also explores growing partnerships across drones, electric vehicles and consumer devices. Wood said existing production capacity can meet near-term demand, but additional volumes will be needed as commercial relationships develop. He outlined the company's strategy of expanding capacity in response to anticipated customer demand, rather than building ahead of the market. Finally, Wood discussed the potential to license NES technology, explaining how the Worley collaboration will help establish the manufacturing processes needed to support future commercial agreements and revenue opportunities. Announced on November 19, 2026, the contract covers two BESS5000 systems with 10 MWh of combined storage capacity. The systems will be installed at Reuteallee in Ludwigsburg and commissioned in summer 2027. SWLB previously ordered a 5 MWh system, now operational at its wood-fired combined heat and power plant. The latest order will bring the combined capacity to 15 MWh. The installations will support decentralized storage, electricity market participation and grid balancing across SWLB’s network. artigo.texto: Romania has added 100 MW of new electricity generation capacity and 36 MW of new energy storage capacity this month, and could reach approximately 1,500 MW of installed energy storage capacity by the end of the year, Energy Minister Dumitru Chisăliță said on Tuesday. “Thanks to intensified monitoring, supervision and discussions with distribution system operators, the energy regulator ANRE and producers, we have managed to bring online 100 MW of new generation capacity and 36 MW of new storage capacity this month,” the minister said at a press conference marking his first month in office, Agerpres reads. He added that the year-end storage target includes projects developed both through investments supported by the Energy Ministry and by private companies. Chisăliță also said the ministry had drawn up competency criteria for appointments to the boards of directors and supervisory boards of state-owned companies, ahead of a wave of board changes expected in 2027, when many current mandates are due to expire. The criteria are intended to improve the selection process and ensure appointments are based on professional qualifications and relevant expertise, he said. The minister also highlighted progress in clearing delayed payments under energy-sector contracts. When he took office, the ministry had 850 contracts with payment delays of up to one year. Payments totalling EUR 200 million were made in November, while a further EUR 280 million is planned for the following month, by the end of the year, with the aim of bringing outstanding payments up to date. Chisăliță said the ministry had also completed the technical documentation for offshore wind energy development, a project that could bring significant additional generation capacity to Romania. He also pointed to efforts to unblock and approve natural gas infrastructure projects, particularly those involving state-owned gas transmission operator Transgaz. Another measure under preparation is an emergency ordinance amending Energy Law 123/2012, currently undergoing public consultation. The proposed changes would require electricity producers to allocate 5% of their output to bilateral contracts and suppliers to purchase 6% of their electricity volumes through such contracts. The measure is intended to increase liquidity and trading activity on the energy market and help reduce electricity prices, the minister said. The Energy Ministry is also preparing changes to the natural gas price framework from April 3, 2027, including an extension and restructuring of the regulated pricing mechanism and the introduction of a one-year transition period towards a fully liberalised gas market. “This draft emergency ordinance is part of the measures we intend to implement over the next three years to ensure a functioning market for both natural gas and electricity,” Chisăliță said. He added that the gas-market proposal was the first of several support schemes and regulatory measures being developed by the ministry, with other initiatives still undergoing consultations and approval procedures with the relevant institutions.

artigo.texto: Opponents of the 1-million-square-foot data center near the eastern edge of Ahwatukee last week escalated their effort to stop it by filing a claim for $11 million against the City of Phoenix. The claim, to which the city by law has 60 days to respond, seeks $1 million on behalf of three residents and $10 million for the Ahwatukee Community Alliance, the nonprofit formed by residents living in the data center’s vicinity. California-based Menlo Digital is erecting the data center at East Thistle Landing Drive and 48th Street on a former call center site it bought in 2015 for roughly $52 million. The site was rezoned in 1997 under a classification allowing data centers, though opponents said that was at a time when data centers were relatively small and fit within a larger building. The claim was filed on the last day of a 180-day period from Phoenix City Council’s approval of site plan changes. The city has 60 days to reject or simply ignore the claim, giving opponents another 180 days to file a lawsuit to press their case in court. City officials could not be reached for comment, although governmental entities in Arizona typically do not comment on pending legal action. Attorney Anthony Ramirez, who is representing the Alliance and filed the claim, said he and his clients intend to take the full 180 days to decide their next step if the claim is rejected or ignored. The claim seeks $1 million on behalf of Alliance President Craig Evans and Alliance members Robert and Faida Faletta “due to the loss of value in property due to the city’s failure to properly permit the Thistle Technology Center as a special permit for data centers…which has resulted in the construction of a data center in a Commerce Park zone despite industrial levels of noise, pollution and activity.” The other $10 million is sought as “nuisance damages due to construction impacts, including noise, pollution, dust and annoyance,” which the claim says have unreasonably “interfered with (Alliance) members’ use and enjoyment of their real property.” That money would be shared by Alliance members who have been “impacted by construction nuisance activity,” according to the claim. Neighbors complained to the Phoenix Planning and Development Department throughout the summer about the construction work, which they said often started well before sunrise, disrupting their sleep. “When you buy a house, you have a right to the enjoyment of that property,” Ramirez said in an interview last week. “We feel that right has been violated.” Calling the facility an “eyesore,” Ramirez said residents’ expectations of peace in their homes had been disrupted by the construction and would be further damaged once the facility is up and running. Ramirez also filed ethics complaints against Phoenix Vice Mayor Kesha Hodge Washington, Councilman Kevin Robinson and one other council member he declined to name for accepting campaign contributions by people connected to Menlo. He said the city Ethics Commission last week dismissed the complaint against Hodge Washington and has scheduled a hearing on one of the other two for mid-December. He said a separate ethics complaint has been filed against all members of the council, including Mayor Kate Gallego, by Brad Follett, the leader of an environmental group in Maricopa called Earth Month Network. Follett did not respond to a request for comment. Ramirez said that while the data center is in an area zoned for commercial and commerce park use, Salt River Project considers the facility to be industrial use. “Why did they not have a full zoning hearing?” he asked rhetorically about Phoenix officials’ approval of the data center. During a town hall Oct. 14 in Mesa that she held on data centers, Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said her office has launched a nuisance investigation into the Menlo facility. "We are investigating the Ahwatukee data center," Mayes told the audience at the Eagles Community Center in Mesa. "We have an open nuisance investigation." "We have investigators looking at this. We will have experts looking at it. We have very good lawyers looking at it, and this town hall is a part of that investigation." Mayes did not explain the scope of her investigation. Nor did she say whether the investigation concerns the effects of construction already underway, potential impacts once the facility begins operating, or both. Nevertheless, her announcement gave residents who have spent months challenging the project their clearest indication yet that a state agency is examining their complaints. "It seems to us like an obvious investigation to launch," Mayes said. City officials have contended that their hands were tied when it came to allowing the data center’s construction because of the mid-1990s zoning of the site. But the Planning and Development Department did respond in October to neighbors’ complaints about the construction noise, stating it would not exempt contractors from a requirement that all construction activity be limited to 7 a.m.-7 p.m. Monday through Friday. On Nov. 20, the same day Ramirez filed the claim against the city, a neighbor complained that construction work had begun at 5 a.m. Planning Director Joshua Bednarik requested the video that residents said they had shot of that activity. Despite the ongoing construction, Menlo has not cleared all the regulatory hurdles for the data center. The Maricopa County Air Quality Department is scheduled to hold a public hearing Dec. 14 on the company's application to operate 72 large diesel-powered generators at the facility. Menlo is seeking permission to release up to 24.9 tons of nitrogen oxides annually — just 200 pounds below the 25-ton threshold identified in its application for additional public notice requirements. Nitrogen oxides contribute to the formation of ground-level ozone, a component of smog that can aggravate respiratory conditions. artigo.texto: ZE Energy, a European electricity flexibility provider, has acquired the 59 MW/472 MWh Magliano Alpi battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Italy’s Piedmont region. The project was acquired from ReFeel New Energy, backed by Gresham House Europe, formerly SUSI Partners. The fully permitted, ready-to-build facility has an eight-hour storage duration and will connect to Italy’s 132 kV electricity network through an existing Terna substation. Magliano Alpi is ZE Energy’s third large-scale standalone battery storage project in Italy, following Sessa Aurunca and Elena. The company operates across France, Italy and Germany and aims to reach 1.5 GW of installed capacity by 2030. ZE Energy acquires 59 MW/472 MWh BESS project in northern Italy The 59 MW/472 MWh Magliano Alpi BESS project in Italy was acquired by ZE Energy from ReFeel New Energy, with permits secured and eight hours of storage duration. artigo.texto: ProLogium Presents Battery Pack 2.0 at NASA Aerospace Battery Workshop for Space Missions and Lunar Infrastructure ProLogium’s GEN4 next generation battery is designed to strengthen mission resilience through intrinsic and active safety, high power with low heat generation, and dual sealing. At the workshop, ProLogium held in-depth technical discussions alongside experts from NASA, BAE Systems, Saft, The Aerospace Corporation and other government agencies on scaling the technology for space missions. HUNTSVILLE, Ala., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — ProLogium Technology made its first appearance at the 2026 NASA Aerospace Battery Workshop, where Founder, CEO and CTO Vincent Yang delivered a presentation titled “Mission-Ready Next Generation Battery: Safe. Powerful. Dense & Scalable.” Yang introduced ProLogium’s Battery Pack 2.0 design concept, outlining how its GEN4 Superfluidized All-Inorganic Solid-State Lithium Ceramic Battery combines high energy density, high-power performance with low heat generation, active safety mechanisms and dual sealing to address the demands of spacecraft and lunar infrastructure, where lightweight design, safety and mission resilience are critical. The official agenda featured technical contributions from NASA, BAE Systems, the Naval Surface Warfare Center, The Aerospace Corporation and Saft, among others. Building on its existing ground-test results, ProLogium aims to pursue flight validation for specific missions and progressively establish flight heritage, laying the groundwork for its expansion into the aerospace battery market. Hosted by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center, the NASA Aerospace Battery Workshop brings together government, industry and research experts from around the world. The program covers advances in battery technology, flight and ground testing, on-orbit operations and fault response. ProLogium presented Battery Pack 2.0, showing how cell-level design can improve fault tolerance in space missions and support manufacturing at scale. From Spacecraft to Lunar Infrastructure With Battery Pack 2.0, ProLogium is targeting two broad application areas: space mobility and infrastructure for lunar work bases. For satellites, spacecraft and planetary rovers, high energy density enables greater energy storage within strict weight and volume constraints, while low heat generation under high-power operation can reduce thermal management demands, creating opportunities to further reduce battery system weight. For lunar infrastructure, battery value centers on long-term reliability and power resilience. In the event of localized equipment failure, power systems must be able to isolate the fault, maintain power to critical loads and restore operation when conditions permit. The same scalable cell architecture can support different battery solutions tailored to the requirements of each mission type. Yang asked during his presentation. Battery Pack 2.0 incorporates fault tolerance at the cell level so that the cell itself provides part of the system’s protection, When something goes wrong, how much of the mission can we preserve? The cell’s own seals can provide an additional layer of protection if external structures are damaged. Low heat generation can ease cooling demands when thermal management capacity is limited. If a fault originates inside the cell, the built-in active safety mechanism can intervene before a chain of heat-generating reactions escalates. For mission operators, these features can help reduce the risk that a local fault interrupts the mission. Aerospace Requirements as a Benchmark for Other Industries Aerospace batteries must deliver high energy density and operate reliably in extreme environments, within tight weight limits and under strict safety requirements. These demands reflect challenges also facing next-generation high-performance batteries in AI data centers, robotics and critical infrastructure. ProLogium sees the safety, reliability and system resilience required for aerospace applications as benchmarks for next-generation battery technology. If GEN4 next-generation batteries are validated under relevant mission conditions, the results could inform product development and commercialization across multiple industries. Vincent Yang, founder, CEO and CTO of ProLogium, said: Aerospace missions push batteries to their limits, reinforcing the direction ProLogium has pursued for years. ” A next-generation battery must combine higher energy density with safety, performance and reliability. If a battery technology can meet the demands of a space mission, the advances it delivers could have a meaningful impact across other industries. That is the vision behind our GEN4 next-generation battery and Battery Pack 2.0. We are using the demands of aerospace missions to guide our validation work and open up applications across industries,” Fourth-Generation Cell Safety, Power and Sealing ProLogium’s GEN4 cells incorporate non-flammable inorganic electrolytes and heat-resistant ceramic separators to provide intrinsic safety, together with a built-in Active Safety Mechanism (ASM). Yang likened ASM to the battery’s “immune system.” Under abnormal conditions such as localized overheating or overcharging, ASM can stabilize the active materials in both electrodes, helping reduce oxygen release and heat generation and suppress the chain of heat-generating reactions. According to ProLogium’s technical data, the ionic conductivity of its Superfluidized Inorganic Electrolyte (SFIE) is approximately five times that of the liquid electrolytes used in the comparison, while its lithium-ion transference number approaches the ideal value of 1, at which lithium ions carry all ionic current. Together, these properties can help reduce polarization and heat generation under high-current operation, supporting fast charging and high-power discharge. The Logithium cell architecture features dual sealing, combining an internal edge seal with an external alum
