Chinese electric-vehicle makers are actively seeking alternatives to their dominant battery supplier, CATL, creating a narrative of an industry challenging an incumbent, though the incumbent's dominance is not necessarily waning. [para. 1] 2. These diversification efforts include Li Auto's 2.6 billion yuan ($397.6 million) investment in Sunwoda's power-battery business, XPeng's increased control over battery-pack integration, and Xiaomi's use of CALB Group and Sunwoda batteries for one of its model lines. [para. 2] 3. Despite these moves, CATL's financial performance and market share remain strong. In the first nine months of 2026, CATL battery installations reached 389.2 gigawatt-hours, a 24.9% year-on-year increase. Its global market share rose to 39.1%, revenue grew 56.2% to 442.1 billion yuan, and net profit climbed 31.6% to 64.53 billion yuan. [para. 3] 4. Supplier diversification and a dominant supplier's continued growth can coexist. Since batteries account for more than 30% of a vehicle's materials cost, seeking lower quotations is an ordinary commercial choice, not an act of disloyalty. However, the procurement calculation has two parts: the immediate visible lower purchase price, and longer-term risks that may take years to surface. [para. 4][para. 5][para. 6] 5. China's new battery safety standard, GB 38031-2025, illustrates this distinction. It requires no fire or explosion and no harm to occupants from smoke, with more specific test conditions, but it remains a minimum standard. Some leading manufacturers conduct more demanding tests, and the safety margin beyond compliance is where meaningful differences emerge. [para. 7][para. 8] 6. CATL chairman Zeng Yuqun highlighted the weakest-link problem, noting that battery pack range and lifespan depend on the worst cell, and CATL claims it has reduced cell failures to parts-per-billion levels. Recent industry incidents support the importance of quality: a battery manufacturer and an EV technology company settled a dispute over cell quality, leading to a recall of more than 30,000 vehicles. In another case, 177-ampere-hour lithium-iron-phosphate cells experienced swelling, leakage, and insulation failures in commercial vehicles, prompting the automaker to extend the battery warranty from eight years or 150,000 kilometers to eight years or 300,000 kilometers. [para. 9][para. 10][para. 11] 7. These cases illustrate that procurement discounts are not the same as reducing lifetime costs. Savings enter accounts immediately, while warranty expenses, recalls, and brand damage arrive later. CATL's challenge is to turn engineering performance into recognizable, measurable brand value through clear warranty terms, faster liability determination, independently verified safety records, and better durability evidence—practical ways to make a premium defensible rather than merely invoking its size. The supplier's strongest response to diversification is to make continued purchases demonstrably worthwhile by offering verifiable quality. artigo.texto: ORANGE COUNTY, Fla. – The east side of Orange County doesn’t have a skyline. It has smokestacks. The Stanton Energy Center, run by the Orlando Utilities Commission, sits a few miles from the restaurants and homes of Avalon Park. It burns natural gas and coal, and it has solar panels on site. Most people nearby say they rarely think about it. Recommended Videos “From zero to 10?” Avalon Park resident Manouchka said when asked how often she thinks about the plant. “Minus five. It does not register.” But what happens at Stanton is changing, and not in the direction OUC had previously planned. OUC initially planned to put one of Stanton’s two coal-fired units into an extended shutdown at the end of May 2026, part of the utility’s long-running move away from coal. Then the federal government stepped in. On June 4, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright signed an emergency order requiring OUC to keep that coal unit, known as Stanton Unit 1, available to run. The Department of Energy later extended the order through Nov. 30. Click here to see the order. “The Department of Energy said, hey, let’s pump the brakes on this and ensure that we have enough capacity to meet our current needs,” said Orlando Alancastro, OUC’s vice president of transmission. The emergency order points to the growth of data centers. It says that in Florida, “projections for resource and transmission growth lag behind what is needed to support new data centers and other large loads.” “As of April 2026, eight data centers are planned for construction in Florida,” the order says. OUC’s CEO, Clint Bullock, raised the same concern at a public workshop earlier this month. “The size of these hyperscalers is like nothing we’ve ever seen. You can’t forecast it into your traditional forecasting. That’s why this is a concern,” Bullock said. Hyperscalers are the massive data centers run by companies such as Google and Amazon. OUC says data centers are only part of the picture. The utility points to faster-than-expected growth in electric vehicles, more manufacturing, and a lack of new power generation across Florida. “There hasn’t been a whole lot of new generation that has been built in the last several years,” Alancastro said. Recent winter and summer weather events have also increased peak energy demand. As a result, OUC is increasing its reserve margin from 15% to 20% to help ensure reliable service during periods of high demand. At the workshop, OUC proposed its Electric Integrated Resource Plan, a 20-year roadmap, which does not take coal off the table. The workshop presentation is posted on OUCFuturePlanning.com. Under the plan, Stanton Unit 1 comes back online in 2028, converted so it can run on either coal or natural gas. Stanton Unit 2 gets the same conversion in 2029. The plan does not set an end date for burning coal at Stanton. “It leverages existing infrastructure. The cost to convert those units are far more economical than building a new resource,” Alancastro said. The plan also adds 150 megawatts of solar and 100 megawatts of battery storage by 2035. A gas plant with carbon capture and 345 megawatts of nuclear power are penciled in for the 2040s. Castro described those as placeholders that could change as technology develops. OUC says the plan still meets its goals of cutting carbon emissions 50% by 2030 and 75% by 2040, compared with 2005 levels. Coal’s share has already shrunk. According to OUC, coal made up 41% of its generating capacity in 2019 and 27% in 2025. Solar grew from less than 1% to 11% over the same period. What it means for your bill OUC says the plan would raise bills by about 1% a year for the next 5 years. There is some short-term relief. OUC is proposing a fuel charge cut that would lower a typical residential bill, based on 1,000 kilowatt-hours a month, by about $5 starting in April 2027. Avalon Park resident Jenna Egensteiner said she supports cleaner energy but wants the details. “Cleaner energy is obviously where you want to go. It’s just how, when, how much, for what,” she said. How to weigh in OUC is taking public comments on the plan through Dec. 4 at oucfutureplanning.com. The OUC board is scheduled to vote on the plan and the proposed fuel cut on Dec. 15.

artigo.texto: A Moura obteve do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) o credenciamento do sistema de armazenamento de energia que vai montar em Belo Jardim, no Agreste de Pernambuco, para as empresas que disputarem o leilão de baterias de 2 de dezembro. A empresa diz ser a primeira fabricante credenciada pela chamada Rota 2, a modalidade do banco que exige mais produção no país e que abre aos compradores a possibilidade de financiar até 100% dos itens elegíveis pelo Fundo Clima, contra até 80% na Rota 1. O aval saiu no Credenciamento de Fornecedores Informatizado (CFI), o cadastro que habilita produtos ao Finame, a linha do BNDES para compra de máquinas e equipamentos nacionais. Além de comprovar que o sistema cumpre as exigências de fabricação nacional, o credenciamento permite que os investidores avaliem o acesso às linhas de financiamento do banco. O percentual de até 100% depende das regras aplicáveis e da aprovação de cada operação, ressalva a Moura. >> Siga o canal da Movimento Econômico no WhatsApp A sessão de 2 de dezembro do Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Potência (LRCAP) recebe os projetos com conteúdo local mínimo de 15%, calculado pela metodologia do BNDES, e tem preço-teto de R$ 1,76 milhão por megawatt ao ano, 11% acima do teto das propostas sem essa exigência. A Moura informa que a sua solução comprovou índice superior ao exigido, mas não divulga o número. Os demais sistemas disputam a sessão de 4 de dezembro, e a Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (ABEEólica) pediu à Justiça Federal, em 16 de novembro, a suspensão dos dois certames. Os vencedores vão vender potência ao sistema elétrico por 15 anos, com início do fornecimento em agosto de 2028. Os contratos serão atendidos por sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS, de Battery Energy Storage System, na sigla em inglês), que guardam eletricidade para devolvê-la à rede quando necessário. No modelo da Moura, a tecnologia de armazenamento vem da chinesa Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL). O Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) vê risco de o país ter déficit de potência acima do limite regulatório a partir de 2027. Rota 2 conta a montagem das baterias como conteúdo nacional A diferença entre as rotas está no que é feito no Brasil. Há modalidades que aceitam cumprir a nacionalização com componentes complementares, enquanto a Rota 2 exige processos produtivos ligados ao próprio sistema de baterias, que responde por uma parcela grande do valor de um BESS, de acordo com a empresa. Em Belo Jardim, a Moura vai montar e integrar os módulos de baterias, a eletrônica de controle e os sistemas de refrigeração, e incorporar peças compradas de fornecedores nacionais. A empresa afirma que esse arranjo alcança índices mais altos de conteúdo nacional e deixa uma margem de segurança acima do mínimo do leilão. O índice reconhecido no credenciamento pode variar de acordo com a configuração de cada projeto contratado. Para o investidor, a margem reduz o risco de o projeto deixar de cumprir a regra de conteúdo local ao longo do contrato, argumenta a Moura. “Escolhemos uma rota que exige maior participação industrial no Brasil e proporciona uma margem importante de conteúdo nacional. Para quem vai assumir compromissos de fornecimento de potência por 15 anos, isso representa mais segurança e previsibilidade”, diz Spartacus Pedrosa, diretor de Operações de Lítio da Moura. Só uma empresa tinha sistema credenciado até o fim de outubro O credenciamento no BNDES tem duas etapas. Primeiro, a empresa é aceita como fornecedora, e depois o banco analisa o sistema de baterias, item por item, para verificar o conteúdo nacional e a capacidade de produção diante do cronograma de entrega. Até 29 de outubro, só a brasileira You.On tinha concluído o processo completo, de acordo com reportagem do site Capital Reset publicada naquele dia. Na mesma data, a Moura estava entre pelo menos nove empresas em credenciamento, ao lado das brasileiras WEG e SecPower, das chinesas BYD, Gotion, TBEA e Trina e da canadense Canadian Solar. A Moura também buscava o credenciamento como fornecedora de software, com a Automa e a Reivax. O chefe da área de transição energética e clima do BNDES, Alexandre Esposito, disse esperar que todas cumpram as exigências, com níveis diferentes de conteúdo local. O banco tem quatro rotas de credenciamento. Além do mínimo de 15%, a Rota 1 exige pelo menos três componentes produzidos no Brasil, sendo um deles estratégico, e as demais pedem conteúdo local nas próprias baterias. Da Rota 2 em diante, o financiamento do BNDES vem todo do Fundo Clima, com custo nominal de 6,5% ao ano, enquanto na Rota 1 o fundo cobre 80% e o restante sai de outras linhas do banco. Moura prevê R$ 200 milhões para ampliar fábrica em Belo Jardim Para atender às empresas do leilão, a Moura prevê investir cerca de R$ 200 milhões na ampliação e na modernização do complexo industrial de Belo Jardim. A empresa anuncia capacidade de fornecimento acima de 8 gigawatts-hora (GWh). A fabricante desenvolve sistemas de armazenamento de energia desde meados da década de 2010 e lançou comercialmente o Moura BESS em 2019. Hoje, soma mais de 40 projetos instalados no país, com produção em Belo Jardim e suporte técnico em Itapetininga (SP). A empresa defende previsibilidade nas novas contratações depois deste primeiro leilão. Para a Moura, a continuidade das contratações sustenta a expansão das fábricas, a formação de profissionais, o desenvolvimento de fornecedores e a nacionalização gradual da cadeia brasileira de armazenamento de energia. Chinesas preparam fábricas de baterias na Bahia e em Sergipe Duas empresas chinesas também preparam fábricas de baterias de armazenamento no Nordeste. A chinesa Windey Brasil, braço do Windey Energy Technology Group, entrou no cadastro de fornecedores do BNDES em 19 de novembro, com o sistema Voltpack L5015 ainda em análise naquela data. A Windey constrói uma fábrica de R$ 100 milhõ

artigo.texto: Denza Z9GT: conheça a perua elétrica de luxo de 1.156 cv em impressões ao volante Denza Z9GT combina três motores elétricos, 1.156 cv e tecnologia de luxo em uma perua que acelera de 0 a 100 km/h em 2,7 segundos. Crédito: Estadão Com apenas duas rodas apoiadas no asfalto, o Denza B5 movimentou um avião Boeing 747-400 de aproximadamente 180 toneladas no aeródromo de Dunsfold, em Surrey, no Reino Unido. A marca de luxo da BYD promoveu o desafio extremo para testar os limites SUV híbrido. A aeronave escolhida para a demonstração, aposentada em 2020, mantém os motores e o interior completo. Isso significa que sua massa equivale a cerca de 72 vezes a capacidade nominal de reboque do utilitário esportivo, declarada em 2.500 kg. Leia também - Cadillac Escalade V8: dirigimos o SUV queridinho das estrelas que a GM promete ao Brasil - Chevrolet Celta e BYD Yuan Plus: veja os carros usados que vendem mais rápido no Brasil - Depois de 1,3 milhão de multas canceladas, free flow volta a punir quem não paga o pedágio Para superar essa diferença de peso sem modificações no trem de força original, o modelo contou com toda a entrega do conjunto de fábrica. A motorização combina um propulsor 1.5 turbo a gasolina — que atua apenas como gerador durante o reboque — a três motores elétricos (dois para tração, um em cada eixo) e à bateria Blade LFP de 31,8 kWh, gerando 544 cv e 77,4 kgfm de torque. Por sua vez, a operação sobre apenas um lado do veículo exigiu adaptações estruturais pontuais para garantir aderência e equilíbrio dinâmico, com o teste dividido em três etapas: - Primeira arrancada: o SUV puxou o avião na configuração padrão, utilizando as quatro rodas. - Segunda tentativa: os engenheiros retiraram uma das rodas e adicionaram 2.000 kg de lastro interno. - Fase final: a equipe removeu outro pneu (deixando apenas o lado esquerdo no chão) e instalou estabilizadores nos eixos, engate sob medida e 4.500 kg de peso extra no lugar dos bancos traseiros. Somando as três passagens, o Denza B5 percorreu 1.600 metros com o avião engatado e precisou aguardar o asfalto secar parcialmente após uma chuva forte nas tentativas finais. Quem assumiu o volante foi Mark Gallifant, técnico sênior da BYD no Reino Unido, superando seu recorde anterior ao rebocar um ônibus de dois andares lotado. De acordo com a fabricante, o feito garante dois recordes inéditos: é o primeiro carro de produção a rebocar um avião sobre duas rodas e o primeiro a deslocar um Boeing 747 usando exclusivamente energia elétrica. Após os percursos, as vistorias técnicas não apontaram desgaste estrutural no chassi, nos pneus ou no trem de força, indica a empresa. Denza no mercado brasileiro Para atrair visibilidade para seus carros e tecnologias, a BYD tem estabelecido desafios públicos com seus carros - o que a fez, por exemplo, quebrar um recorde de velocidade recentemente. No Brasil, a Denza especificamente tem conquistado mercado no segmennto premium. Em outubro de 2026, o B5 fechou o quinto mês consecutivo na liderança dos SUVs de luxo no país, somando 577 unidades emplacadas contra 405 do BMW X1. No acumulado de janeiro a outubro de 2026, o modelo da BYD chegou a 3.777 registros. O ritmo de vendas reduziu para apenas 172 unidades a vantagem do rival alemão, que acumula 3.949 emplacamentos na disputa anual da categoria. Carregando ofertas...

artigo.texto: Material ultrafino poderá abrir caminho a novas formas de armazenamento de energia e hidrogénio - Um material ultrafino, com uma espessura de uma camada, pode ser crucial no armazenamento de energia. Investigadores da Universidade Victoria de Wellington descobriram os MXenes. - Estudos publicados na Nature Communications revelam que uma reacção química pode propagar-se significativamente numa folha de MXene, revelando resultados inesperados. - Compreender os MXenes poderá levar ao desenvolvimento de soluções energéticas mais eficientes, embora a aplicação prática ainda possa demorar alguns anos. Partilhar Uma equipa internacional de investigadores descobriu que uma única camada de um material bidimensional, conhecido como MXene, consegue armazenar hidrogénio. A descoberta permite compreender melhor as propriedades destes materiais, que poderão vir a contribuir para tecnologias de armazenamento de energia mais rápidas e eficientes. Um material com uma espessura de apenas uma camada poderá vir a desempenhar um papel importante no desenvolvimento de novas tecnologias de armazenamento de energia. Uma equipa internacional de investigadores, que inclui cientistas da Universidade Victoria de Wellington, na Nova Zelândia, descobriu que os MXenes, uma classe de materiais bidimensionais ultrafinos, conseguem armazenar hidrogénio numa única camada. O estudo, publicado na revista científica Nature Communications, revela também um comportamento inesperado destes materiais: uma reacção química iniciada num ponto muito pequeno de uma folha de MXene pode propagar-se por uma parte significativa da sua superfície. Para observar este fenómeno, os investigadores utilizaram um microscópio de elevada resolução e analisaram a forma como a água, a electricidade e o hidrogénio interagem com pequenas partículas deste material. Os resultados mostraram que a reacção química consegue percorrer distâncias muito superiores às inicialmente previstas, revelando um nível de conectividade interna que não tinha sido observado anteriormente. Segundo Kim McKelvey, investigador principal do MacDiarmid Institute, da Universidade Victoria de Wellington, a descoberta permite compreender melhor os processos que ocorrem à escala microscópica em materiais com potencial para futuras tecnologias energéticas. “Os resultados mostram como uma única camada do material pode armazenar hidrogénio, desafiando os pressupostos existentes sobre o comportamento dos MXenes e abrindo novas possibilidades de investigação”, explica. Compreender os materiais para melhorar o armazenamento Os MXenes são materiais bidimensionais que têm despertado interesse científico pelas suas propriedades e pelo potencial de aplicação em dispositivos de armazenamento de energia, baterias e tecnologias baseadas em hidrogénio. Compreender a forma como estes materiais interagem com diferentes elementos e como as reacções químicas se propagam no seu interior poderá ajudar a desenvolver soluções electroquímicas mais eficientes. Nicola Gaston, directora do MacDiarmid Institute, considera que o conhecimento dos processos fundamentais é essencial para o desenvolvimento de novas tecnologias energéticas. “Quanto mais compreendermos estes processos, mais bem preparados estaremos para conceber materiais que poderão, um dia, contribuir para um armazenamento de energia mais rápido, baterias melhoradas e tecnologias de hidrogénio”, afirma. A investigadora destacou ainda a importância de encontrar novas formas de armazenar hidrogénio de maneira segura e eficiente, um passo considerado fundamental para tornar este vector energético uma opção mais viável no armazenamento e transporte de energia limpa. Apesar do potencial identificado, os investigadores reconhecem que a aplicação prática desta descoberta ainda poderá demorar alguns anos. O trabalho, que envolveu equipas de Berlim, Dublin e Wellington, representa sobretudo um avanço no conhecimento das propriedades dos MXenes e dos mecanismos que poderão orientar o desenvolvimento de futuras tecnologias de armazenamento de energia.

De apoios de cabeça a emissões do V8, entenda o que é avaliado na homologação do SUV americano e quais adaptações podem ser necessárias O Tribunal de Haia, nos Países Baixos, definiu a primeira derrota da Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) na disputa judicial contra a BYD envolvendo o SUV híbrido BYD Ti7. A corte holandesa determinou que a fabricante britânica destrua imediatamente todos os documentos e arquivos digitais apreendidos em agosto nos escritórios da montadora chinesa nas cidades de Schiedam e Hoofddorp. A decisão atendeu integralmente aos protestos da BYD, que classificou a operação dos oficiais de justiça como uma invasão excessiva. Leia Também: Pela sentença, a JLR tem o prazo de 24 horas após a notificação formal para eliminar os dados. O descumprimento acarretará multa de cerca de € 50 mil por hora de atraso, com teto fixado em € 500 mil, além da condenação da britânica ao pagamento de € 25.376 em custas processuais. A origem do caso e a suspeita de engenharia reversa O conflito começou quando a JLR acusou a rival asiática de infringir direitos de propriedade intelectual do Land Rover Defender no desenvolvimento do BYD Ti7. A fabricante britânica suspeitava que a concorrente tivesse recorrido à engenharia reversa — desmontando uma unidade do Defender — para reproduzir soluções técnicas do utilitário. Essa desconfiança motivou as buscas nas sedes da marca chinesa na Europa. Contudo, o tribunal concluiu que a apreensão configurou uma busca indiscriminada e sem alvo definido, conhecida como fishing expedition. Segundo o magistrado, os arquivos recolhidos — que incluíam planos de lançamento e dados financeiros — não eram necessários para comprovar uma eventual cópia, sobretudo porque o SUV sequer era comercializado na União Europeia à época. Histórico de disputas da JLR na China Este não é o primeiro embate da JLR com uma fabricante do país asiático. Em 2019, a companhia obteve uma decisão favorável na China contra a Jiangling Holdings, responsável pelo Landwind X7, cujo alvo da cópia era o Range Rover Evoque. O Tribunal Distrital de Chaoyang, em Pequim, reconheceu que o modelo chinês reproduzia características do Evoque e determinou a interrupção de sua fabricação e vendas. Por outro lado, a relação da JLR com a indústria chinesa também é marcada por parcerias estratégicas. Em 2012, a britânica uniu-se à Chery em uma joint venture e, em 2024, as empresas avançaram para licenciar o nome Freelander e desenvolver elétricos com arquitetura da Chery, gerando frutos como o Freelander 8, produzido em Changshu. Futuro do BYD Ti7 e chegada ao Brasil Mesmo com o resultado desfavorável nos tribunais da Holanda, o veredito não define se o BYD Ti7 infringiu ou não as patentes de design da JLR. Portanto, há muito mais para se desenrolar neste caso. Não à toa, o CEO da fabricante britânica, PB Balaji, reforçou que a empresa não abrirá mão de proteger juridicamente suas criações contra plágios. Enquanto a briga jurídica avança, o modelo expande sua presença internacional. No Reino Unido e em mercados europeus, o Ti7 é comercializado na versão Excellence AWD, equipada com tração integral e conjunto híbrido plug-in (sistema DM-p) que entrega 408 cv de potência combinada, associado a um motor 1.5 turbo a gasolina. A BYD divulga aceleração de 0 a 100 km/h em 4,8 segundos e bateria Blade de 35,6 kWh, que garante autonomia elétrica de aproximadamente 119 km. No mercado britânico, o utilitário tem preço anunciado de 47.995 libras (cerca de R$ 342,8 mil em conversão direta), posicionando-se consideravelmente abaixo do Defender 110 equivalente. Para o mercado brasileiro, a estreia do BYD Ti7 foi confirmada durante uma convenção de concessionários em Mendoza, na Argentina, conforme revelou o jornalista Jorge Moraes, da CNN. A expectativa é que o Brasil receba a configuração de cinco lugares, distinguindo-se da versão Excellence AWD europeia, que leva sete assentos. Na China, onde é comercializado pela submarca FangChengBao, essa variante de cinco lugares mede 5 metros de comprimento, 2 m de largura, 1,86 m de altura e 2,92 m de entre-eixos (enquanto a versão internacional com três fileiras é maior, com cerca de 5,15 metros). Além disso, o modelo traz uma vasta lista de equipamentos, que inclui central multimídia de 15,6 polegadas, painel digital de 10,25 polegadas, som com 18 alto-falantes, ar-condicionado de três zonas, teto panorâmico e refrigerador no console. Com esse pacote, o utilitário tem tudo para agitar o segmento nacional em 2027.

artigo.texto: BYD is making its presence felt as much as possible just about everywhere, including the Land Down Under. They say that models like the Sealion 7 benefit the people who need them the most, including in rural areas; they joined forces earlier this month with the AFL (Australian Football League) by signing a major partnership with the Hawthorn Football Club, and back in October already celebrated 150k unit sales in the region. As far as models are concerned, BYD made available in September the smaller ATTO 2 DM-i featuring the Dual Mode 4.0 Super Hybrid platform and the Blade battery using Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) chemistry, as well as the ATTO 3 featuring the new e-Platform 3.0 EV architecture with 800 volts. Now it’s time for a proper flagship of the people mover variety – the company first confirmed the all-new BYD M9 minivan was coming to Australia back in August and then announced the pricing configuration in September, with the model starting from AU $61,990 for the base eight-seat M9 Dynamic model and from AU $72,990 (over $48k) sans OTR for the seven-seat M9 Premium variant. The Chinese brand now announces the arrival of the BYD M9 on the market, with BYD's first new energy people mover bringing together the “brand's expertise in new energy vehicle mobility with the versatility Australians expect from large and well-appointed mobility.” Initially, the first version touching down in the Land Down Under is the top-spec seven-seat Premium grade, featuring a 2+2+3 configuration with luxurious leather-appointed and second-row captain’s chairs, a 15.6-inch rear entertainment screen and a 12-speaker audio system among the highlights. The more versatile eight-seat M9 Dynamic featuring a 2+3+3 seating arrangement will come before the end of the year, and both share the latest DM-i Dual Mode 5.0 Super Hybrid system, three-zone air-conditioning, and 470 liters (16.59 cu. Ft.) for luggage with all seats raised. With the rear seats folded, the M9 has 2,036 liters of space – or 71.9 cubic feet of storage. The Dynamic grade has Frequency Selective Damping technology, while the Premium gets BYD's DiSus-C Intelligent Damping Body Control system, but the intelligent plug-in hybrid system is common to both. It consists of a 1.5-liter turbocharged Xiaoyun gasoline engine and a permanent magnet synchronous electric motor with a combined output of 191kW for Dynamic and 218kW for Premium – that’s 256 hp or 292 horsepower. The Dynamic features a 20.4kWh BYD Blade Battery offering up to 80 km of pure electric range or 50 miles, while the Premium version is even more capable thanks to its larger 36.6kWh battery – EV range soars to 145 km or 90 miles. Total combined range is 790km and 850km, respectively, based on WLTP – or 491 and 528 miles, respectively. Both the M9 Dynamic and Premium are solely available with front-wheel drive, though, and feature three intelligent operating modes: EV Pure Electric, HEV Series, where the gasoline engine only acts as a power generator, and HEV Parallel, where both the gasoline and electric motor work together. Inside, BYD gives the driver a 12.3-inch digital instrument display and a 15.6-inch infotainment touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Numa carta dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, Wopke Hoekstra, os ministros do Ambiente da Dinamarca, Finlândia, Alemanha, Luxemburgo, Países Baixos, Portugal, Espanha e Suécia manifestam “forte apoio” ao Sistema de Comércio Europeu de Licenças de Emissão 2 (CELE 2). O CELE 2 é um mercado de carbono complementar ao CELE original. Enquanto o CELE original abrange as emissões da produção de eletricidade e de calor, da indústria pesada, da aviação e do transporte marítimo, o CELE 2 incide sobre novos setores, como as emissões criadas pela utilização de combustíveis em edifícios e no transporte rodoviário. Criado em 2023, o CELE 2 tinha entrada em vigor inicialmente prevista para 2028, mas países mais dependentes dos combustíveis fósseis, como a Itália ou a Polónia, têm apelado a que essa data seja adiada ou que o sistema seja aligeirado. Foi perante esta pressão que, na cimeira do Conselho Europeu de outubro, os líderes da União Europeia (UE) comprometeram-se a avaliar o impacto do CELE 2 antes da sua entrada em vigor em 2028. Na carta hoje dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, que partiu da iniciativa da Dinamarca, os oito ministros frisam que o CELE 2 é hoje “mais importante do que nunca”, numa altura em que “a perturbação dos fluxos de energia através do Estreito de Ormuz voltou a expor a vulnerabilidade da Europa”. “É evidente que temos de reduzir a nossa dependência dos combustíveis fósseis importados, de modo a diminuir a nossa exposição às tensões geopolíticas e aos choques de preços, que prejudicam a competitividade europeia, afetam negativamente as empresas e as famílias, colocam em risco a nossa segurança energética e nos tornam vulneráveis a pressões políticas”, defendem. Os ministros consideram, por isso, que, “ao proporcionar um meio economicamente eficiente de acelerar a descarbonização dos setores dos transportes rodoviários e dos edifícios”, o CELE 2 “reforça a segurança energética da Europa, reduzindo a dependência das importações de combustíveis fósseis e promovendo a eletrificação”. “O CELE 2 desempenha, assim, um papel fundamental no reforço da resiliência da Europa e da sua autonomia estratégica aberta”, insistem. Os ministros recordam ainda que o CELE 2 é “parte integrante de um compromisso mais amplo, que procura alcançar um equilíbrio delicado entre ambição, eficiência em termos de custos e solidariedade”. Dirigindo-se ao comissário europeu do Clima, os ministros manifestam-se “disponíveis para trabalhar de forma construtiva com a Comissão”, para garantir que o CELE 2 entra em vigor “em conformidade com o calendário já acordado”.

artigo.texto: If a qualifying data center opens in your county, a Texas lawmaker wants the company behind it to pay you every year. You could qualify even if you live on the other side of the county. Your kids could qualify, too. So what might that actually pay? Under House Bill 1273, a data center authorized to draw 100 megawatts of power would owe at least $1 million for a full year of operation. Split that among 100,000 eligible residents and it comes to $10 per person before administrative costs. The payment could be higher depending on how much money the facility brings in and how many residents qualify. Recommended Videos Democratic state Rep.-elect Cecilia Castellano filed the bill Nov. 20. It would also pause covered construction for two years and give voters a direct role in approving projects. The annual payments would apply only to qualifying projects that first receive a permit under the proposed law after it takes effect. Who would get paid? Your primary home would have to be in the county that hosts the data center for at least 183 days of the year. Renters would qualify, and a parent or legal guardian would receive a child’s payment on their behalf. Income and citizenship status would have no bearing on eligibility. The developer and operator would each be legally responsible for the full amount owed. The annual payment would be whichever of the following is higher: - 2% of gross receipts from services provided using the facility, such as data processing, computing capacity, AI training and data storage. - $10,000 per megawatt of power the facility is authorized to draw at its peak. Eligible residents would receive equal shares by June 1 each year. The bill allows up to 2% of the fund to go toward administrative costs. What would voters get to decide? Under the bill, a project outside city limits would need a majority vote in a countywide election. A project inside city limits would have to win two separate votes, one in the city and one countywide. The ballot would show how much power the facility expects to draw at peak demand and how much water it expects to use each year. Which data centers would the bill cover? The rules would apply to new data centers designed to draw at least 20 megawatts or with at least 50,000 square feet devoted primarily to computing equipment. The bill would also cover expansions that increase a data center’s maximum power demand by at least 10 megawatts or add at least 25,000 square feet of space for computing equipment. Along with voter approval, the projects would need a state permit backed by studies on water use, electricity demand, noise and emissions. The bill would also repeal certain data center sales tax exemptions. When would the bill take effect? If passed, HB 1273 would take effect Sept. 1, 2027. It could take effect immediately if at least two-thirds of the elected members of each chamber vote for it. The two-year pause on covered projects would begin on whichever date the law takes effect.

artigo.texto: EVE Energy's Comprehensive AIDC Energy Storage Portfolio Makes Its Global Debut at RE+ 2026 New portfolio for AI data centers spans source-grid, power-distribution and cabinet-side applications LAS VEGAS, Nov. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- EVE Energy showcased its full-scenario energy storage solutions for AI data centers (AIDC) at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, alongside emerging all-solid-state and sodium-ion battery technologies. The company also held a product launch during the event, introducing an integrated portfolio designed to address data center power requirements from the source-grid connection through power distribution to cabinet-level backup. As demand for AI computing capacity accelerates, energy storage is moving beyond auxiliary backup to become an essential part of data center power infrastructure. With AIDC projects advancing toward large-scale deployment, EVE says its portfolio is designed to address needs across the data center power chain. Drawing on experience in power, energy-storage and consumer batteries, together with coordinated development across lithium, sodium and hydrogen technologies, EVE says it can provide both cells and systems for AIDC applications through an integrated offering. Its three-layer architecture covers source-grid, power-distribution and cabinet-side applications, supporting needs from millisecond-scale load smoothing to long-duration energy management. Three-layer product portfolio makes global debut, addressing AIDC power challenges At RE+ 2026, EVE placed its AIDC energy storage portfolio at the center of its exhibit, while also showcasing solutions for commercial and industrial, residential and telecommunications applications. Products highlighted at the event included the 20-ft, 5 MWh, 1P S5-1P high-power ESS; a dedicated 315 Ah frequency-regulation cell; the Fortron backup power cabinet; and a high-rate, rack-level BBU+CBU energy storage system. EVE says the portfolio is intended to provide the reliable power infrastructure needed as AIDC deployments scale. The S5-1P is designed to deliver 5 MWh of energy capacity with 1P power capability in a standard 20-ft container. Its dedicated 315 Ah frequency-regulation cell has a volumetric energy density of 395 Wh/L. The company also reports no lithium plating at the cell interface under 1P charge/discharge and 1.22P frequency-regulation conditions, supporting safety and long service life in high-rate applications. Designed for transient, high-power loads, the Fortron 6C/10C backup power cabinet supports continuous discharge at up to 10C and can deliver 660 kW for five minutes. It has a 15-year design life and is compatible with uninterruptible power supply (UPS) backup systems and high-voltage direct current (HVDC) applications. Its modular architecture is designed for factory pre-integration and rapid deployment, with layered cell, thermal and fire-safety protections. At the cabinet side, EVE's rack-level BBU+CBU system is designed to smooth power fluctuations across a 1-millisecond-to-10-second window. The BBU uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) high-power cells in a high-density 3U form factor and supports discharge rates of up to 48C. According to EVE, the LIC hybrid supercapacitor responds in 1 millisecond or less and is rated for more than one million high-rate pulse cycles. The company lists autonomous system response at 2 milliseconds or less, helping maintain stable power delivery as AI computing loads change. Integrated, full-chain delivery simplifies procurement and operations Unlike project configurations assembled from multiple vendors, EVE's integrated AIDC energy storage offering is designed to deliver three customer benefits. First, it simplifies procurement through a single-source solution, reducing the need to coordinate multiple cell manufacturers and system integrators while helping shorten project timelines and lower decision-making costs. Second, it provides clearer accountability: battery cells, the battery management system (BMS), system integration, thermal management and fire protection are developed within a coordinated architecture, helping address responsibility gaps that can arise in multi-vendor systems. Third, it reduces operations and maintenance (O&M) complexity through a common technical platform and a single service point of contact, supporting AIDC facilities that operate 24/7 while helping lower lifecycle O&M costs. EVE says it is committed to building the energy foundation for the AI era through full-scenario AIDC energy storage products and to becoming a trusted global energy partner for AI computing infrastructure. At RE+ 2026, the company presented its solutions to customers in China and international markets as it looks to accelerate AIDC energy storage deployments. Its stated goal is to provide safe, efficient and lower-carbon power support for AI infrastructure worldwide, helping keep computing operations and token generation reliable.

artigo.texto: The Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (UPERC) has approved power procurement agreements and tariffs for 375 MW/1,500 MWh of standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Uttar Pradesh. The projects will be developed with viability gap funding (VGF) support under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF) and are expected to strengthen the state’s electricity supply management, support renewable energy integration and improve grid stability. In orders dated November 19, 2026, the commission approved the tariffs discovered through a competitive bidding process conducted by Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL). The projects will supply stored energy on demand for 15 years from their respective commercial operation dates. Their scheduled commissioning date is December 7, 2027, with VGF support of Rs. 18 lakh per MWh. The procurement process attracted 13 bidders, of which 12 qualified during the technical evaluation. Eleven bidders subsequently participated in the electronic reverse auction conducted on May 2, 2026. Following the auction, UPPCL allocated the total capacity of 375 MW among three successful bidders based on the lowest discovered tariffs and the applicable bucket-filling mechanism. Under Petition No. 2404 of 2026, UPERC approved a tariff of Rs. 6.45 per kWh for KCC BESS Private Limited, a special purpose vehicle of KCC Buildcon Private Limited. The company will develop a 187.5 MW/750 MWh standalone battery storage project. The commission also approved the power procurement agreement signed between UPPCL and the company on June 1, 2026. In Petition No. 2405 of 2026, the commission approved the same tariff of Rs. 6.45 per kWh for Agastya Solar UP1 Private Limited, a subsidiary of Agastya Green Energy Limited. The company has been awarded 62.50 MW/250 MWh of storage capacity under a power procurement agreement dated June 8, 2026. Meanwhile, Petition No. 2403 of 2026 involved the 125 MW/500 MWh project awarded to MKC Kashivisvanath Ji Energy Private Limited, a subsidiary of MKC Green Energy Limited. UPERC approved a slightly higher tariff of Rs. 6.46 per kWh and cleared the power procurement agreement signed on June 3, 2026. UPPCL informed the commission that the discovered tariffs of Rs. 6.45 and Rs. 6.46 per kWh were competitive compared with previous procurement benchmarks. The corporation highlighted its earlier procurement through NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited (NVVN), where tariffs ranged between Rs. 6.71 and Rs. 6.72 per kWh. The newly discovered rates therefore offer a lower procurement cost for the approved storage capacity. During the hearing held on October 1, 2026, the commission raised concerns over UPPCL’s failure to initially submit the complete set of bidding documents along with its petitions. UPERC expressed displeasure over the omission and directed the corporation to provide the missing records. UPPCL subsequently apologised and submitted the required documents through an additional affidavit filed on October 23, 2026. After examining the submitted records, bidding process and applicable guidelines, the commission was satisfied that the procurement had followed the approved competitive bidding framework. It consequently approved the discovered tariffs and power procurement agreements for all three projects. The approved battery storage capacity is expected to help Uttar Pradesh manage peak electricity demand, improve the utilisation of renewable energy and provide greater flexibility in grid operations. UPERC has directed the concerned parties to take timely action to ensure that the projects achieve their scheduled commissioning deadline of December 7, 2027. artigo.texto: - Power - 2 min read Battery price rebound, rupee fall threaten viability of India’s BESS projects: ICRA The rating agency flags procurement costs, currency movements and execution delays as key risks despite policy support and a growing tender pipeline. India's rapidly expanding battery energy storage system (BESS) market is facing fresh financial viability challenges as a rebound in battery prices, rupee depreciation and aggressive project bidding put pressure on developers' returns, according to a report by rating agency ICRA. While strong policy support and a growing tender pipeline are driving the sector's expansion, the ability of developers to procure batteries at competitive prices and execute projects within stipulated timelines will remain critical to their financial sustainability, ICRA said in its November 2026 report on the Indian renewable energy sector. ICRA's sensitivity analysis indicates that at a battery pack cost of $70 per kWh, BESS projects would generate a cumulative debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.17-1.27 times at capacity tariffs of ₹2.60-2.80 lakh per MW per month. The DSCR measures a project's ability to generate sufficient cash flows to meet its debt repayment obligations. A relatively narrow coverage margin could leave developers with limited financial flexibility if battery procurement costs rise further or project execution faces delays. Battery procurement costs and currency movements have emerged as key variables determining the viability of aggressively bid projects, the rating agency said, underlining the importance of competitive procurement strategies and protection against cost escalation. ICRA also highlighted the need for robust long-term service agreements (LTSAs) and firm offtake arrangements to safeguard project economics. The concerns come as India's battery storage market moves from the tendering stage towards actual project execution. Rising renewable energy capacity, which continues to outpace transmission augmentation, particularly in resource-rich states such as Rajasthan and Gujarat, is increasing grid congestion and the need for storage infrastructure. Battery storage systems are expected to play a crucial role in absorbing surplus renewable generation during solar hours and shifting electricity supply to periods when solar generation declines. Government support through viability gap funding (VGF) schemes announced in 2023, 2025 and 2026, covering a cumulative 135.8 GWh of storage capacity, is providing significant capital support to the sector. However, policy incentives and lower initial funding requirements alone may not eliminate the financial and operational risks associated with BESS projects. ICRA cautioned that developers also need to account for eventual duty payments under the MOOWR scheme, performance penalties, additional battery requirements and post-warranty maintenance expenses. These costs may not necessarily be covered by supplier guarantees. The rating agency said project assessments should examine whether supplier guarantees adequately cover developers' commitments to power buyers, particularly in cases where equipment performance falls short of contractual requirements. With battery costs, currency movements and execution timelines becoming increasingly important to project economics, timely procurement and adequate financial safeguards will be crucial for developers navigating India's expanding energy storage market.

artigo.texto: FERNANDA BRIGATTI, MARCOS HERMANSON E JOÃO GABRIEL FOLHAPRESS A política de incentivo a data centers virou lei há dois meses, mas até agora os interessados em usar os benefícios fiscais que ela criou ainda não sabem quais são as regras de habilitação, os prazos, como será o uso de energia e até mesmo quais serão os equipamentos comprados com isenção de PIS, Cofins e IPI. O principal entrave para a regulamentação é o uso do gás natural como fonte de energia nessas estruturas, o que opôs os ministérios da Fazenda e do Meio Ambiente -contrários à ideia- ao de Minas e Energia -a favor. Segundo pessoas que participam das negociações, as pastas envolvidas chegaram a um acordo sobre todos os outros pontos da regulamentação há mais de um mês. O que atrasou o avanço da proposta durante esse tempo foi o debate sobre o combustível fóssil. A brecha para o uso do gás foi aberta por uma negociação costurada pelo presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP), a partir de um lobby do setor. O texto original previa que os data centers teriam de ser abastecidos por energia limpa ou renovável. O Senado mudou a obrigação para fontes renováveis ou de “baixa emissão”. Após uma discussão técnica que envolveu quatro ministérios e a Casa Civil, caberá ao presidente Lula bater o martelo sobre o tema. Os ministérios do Meio Ambiente e da Fazenda são contrários à liberação do gás por entenderem que ele contradiz o propósito original do projeto, que vinculava o incentivo tributário ao uso de fontes renováveis. As pastas chegaram a apresentar uma proposta de regulamentação que criava tantas condicionantes ao uso do combustível fóssil que, na prática, ele se tornava inviável. O Ministério de Minas e Energia, por sua vez, defende o gás como fonte para data centers. No dia em que a lei do Redata (Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenters) foi sancionada, a pasta divulgou nota na qual defende a presença do gás e informa que o combustível foi “classificado pela Agência Internacional de Energia (IEA) como de baixa emissão de carbono e de transição energética.” O setor de gás afirma que a demanda por energia dos data centers será alta e terá de ser estável, sem riscos de intermitências, o que termelétricas a gás podem oferecer. Entre as empresas que acompanham a regulamentação da política de incentivo, a fonte de energia é vista como uma questão secundária e que poderia ser tratada em uma norma separada. Também se discutiu a possibilidade de a regulamentação prever que o gás natural só seria usado quando outras fontes não estiverem disponíveis. TRATATIVAS Após a aprovação do projeto, o governo reuniu integrantes do Meio Ambiente, Indústria, Fazenda, Minas e Energia e Casa Civil para definir o critério técnico de fonte de “baixa emissão”, necessário para definir quais fontes entram e quais ficam de fora da lista. As partes avançaram em acordo sobre essa definição, segundo um integrante do governo ouvido pela reportagem, mas agora aguardam um despacho com o presidente Lula, que é quem vai dar a palavra final sobre quais fontes entrarão no programa. Os membros do grupo envolvido na discussão técnica esperavam apresentar o decreto ao presidente nesta semana, após o retorno de Lula ao Brasil, o que ocorreu na noite de segunda (16). Um integrante desse grupo, ouvido pela Folha, avalia que a regulamentação segue importante, mesmo com a demora e a mudança do arcabouço tributário a partir de 2027, porque garante o imposto de importação zerado e viabiliza potencialmente a isenção do ICMS. A preocupação de representantes de entidades é a de que o fim do ano se aproxima e, com isso, o incentivo fiscal previsto na legislação praticamente chega ao fim. Para 2026, o governo federal previu na Lei Orçamentária uma reserva de R$ 5,2 bilhões em isenções de PIS, Cofins e Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados. No próximo ano, esses tributos serão extintos e substituídos pela CBS (Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços). Mas as empresas que aderirem ao Redata ainda terão garantia de cinco anos de isenção do imposto de importação para produtos sem similar nacional. A isenção vale mesmo que produtos hoje isentos passem a ser fabricados no Brasil. A regulamentação do Redata também é considerada importante para que o setor conquiste a isenção do ICMS (Imposto sobre Consumo, Mercadorias e Serviços) no Confaz, o conselho que reúne os secretários estaduais de Fazenda. Entidades organizadas no Fórum das Associações do Setor Elétrico (Fase) enviaram cartas aos ministérios se posicionando pela regulamentação da política. “Cada mês sem regulamentação representa, portanto, não mera postergação, mas perda efetiva de capacidade de atração de investimentos, sem ganho arrecadatório, uma vez que os equipamentos não adquiridos tampouco gerarão tributos.” O setor elétrico vê no Redata também a possibilidade de dar vazão aos excedentes de geração eólica e solar, uma vez que cerca de 20% dessa produção foi cortada em 2025 para evitar sobrecarga do sistema integrado. “Os data centers que o Redata busca atrair estão entre os principais vetores de crescimento da carga [demanda] do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), e sua regulamentação é indispensável para que os investidores conheçam as condições e os procedimentos de implantação dos projetos”, diz a carta. A demanda de data centers deve passar de cerca de 0,3 GW médio em 2026 para 5,7 GW médios em 2030, ou quase um terço do crescimento da carga do SIN no período. As entidades defendem a publicação imediata da regulamentação. Além do impasse dentro do governo quanto aos parâmetros do uso do gás natural nesses projetos, a lista de equipamentos beneficiados sem similar nacional também é frente de embates. Uma minuta de decreto de regulamentação que circula entre entidades de tecnologia acendeu um alerta em algumas delas, que consideraram o rascunho muito restritivo, dizendo que ele inviabilizaria praticamente a política de incentivo. artigo.texto: The Real Economics of AI Infrastructure: Power, Cooling and the Price of Growth Key Highlights - The WEF argues that AI campuses should be assessed as part of the wider power, water, land, fiber and community systems they depend on. - Nuclear uprates, existing powered sites and new generation agreements offer potential supply pathways, but differ in timing, cost and execution risk. - Utilities and regulators are increasingly addressing who pays for new infrastructure and how existing customers are protected from large-load expansion. - Workload management and flexible demand could help campuses deliver more computing within constrained power supplies, though gigawatt-scale performance remains to be proven. - Water availability, cooling choices and the ability to retrofit for future hardware are becoming central to permitting, resilience and long-term investment decisions. A data center can have an excellent power usage effectiveness (PUE) rating and still be a poor infrastructure investment. It may be located on a grid that cannot deliver additional power, rely on increasingly contested water supplies, or require extensive reconstruction to accommodate the next generation of AI hardware. None of those shortcomings will necessarily register in conventional facility-efficiency metrics. That is the argument underlying the World Economic Forum’s September 21 report, Data Centre Sustainability and Resilience: A Decision Playbook for AI Infrastructure, developed in collaboration with Marsh. Rather than defining sustainability primarily through the performance of an individual facility, the report examines an AI campus in the context of the power generation, transmission, cooling, water, land, fiber, supply chains and communities on which it depends. The scale of the challenge was reinforced by the International Energy Agency’s November release of its World Energy Outlook 2026, which projects that global data center electricity consumption will approximately double to 1,000 terawatt-hours (TWh) by 2030 under its Stated Policies Scenario. Since the WEF report’s publication, announcements from hyperscalers, utilities and infrastructure suppliers have begun to put its recommendations to the test. Google has entered into a major nuclear uprate agreement and a separate set of power arrangements in Wyoming, while Amazon is supporting the evaluation of nearly a gigawatt of advanced nuclear generation in Indiana. NVIDIA is placing greater emphasis on computational output relative to power consumption and the ability to dynamically manage an AI factory’s electrical load. OpenAI has outlined a program intended to make future campuses responsive to grid constraints. Meanwhile, regulators, communities and utility customers are increasingly questioning who should bear the costs and risks of AI infrastructure expansion. A Trillion-Dollar Opportunity, With an Important Qualification The WEF estimates that more sustainable and resilient development practices could help unlock $700 billion to $1 trillion in global data center investment through 2030 by reducing project delays and cancellations. It is a substantial figure, but one better understood as an indication of the scale of investment potentially at risk than as a forecast of recoverable capital. The estimate is based on applying an assumed 10%–15% exposure to project delays and cancellations against a projected $7 trillion in investment. Delayed investment, however, is not necessarily lost investment. Projects can also be derailed by deteriorating economics, financing constraints, equipment availability or changing demand assumptions that better environmental and infrastructure planning alone cannot resolve. For a developer unable to establish when utility service will be available, the financial consequences of delayed energization can easily outweigh modest improvements in facility efficiency. A campus that requires unanticipated transmission or water infrastructure may face a substantially different capital budget from the one originally presented to investors. Given the pace of technological change, a facility design that cannot accommodate successive generations of processors may also strand mechanical and electrical investments long before the building reaches the end of its useful life. Against this backdrop, the WEF’s central recommendation is not simply to spend more money on sustainability initiatives, but to identify the constraints that could undermine a project’s financial returns before making commitments that are expensive to reverse. Its framework encompasses development pathways, common decision principles, recommended metrics and market-specific constraint profiles, with guidance for developers, operators, enterprise customers, financial institutions and policymakers. For developers, that means evaluating whether a proposed site can support both the initial project and subsequent expansion. For investors, it means looking beyond conventional construction costs and projected returns to assess exposure to delays, regulatory uncertainty and infrastructure dependencies. The framework does not prescribe a single solution. Its value lies in identifying the trade-offs that could undermine a project’s economics while there is still an opportunity to address them. Nuclear Uprates Show the Appeal of Existing Infrastructure One of the clearest examples came on October 6, when Google and Constellation announced a 20-year agreement supporting 890 MW of additional nuclear generating capacity at 11 operating reactor units in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey. Constellation outlined more than $4.3 billion in planned investments to increase the thermal and electrical output of existing facilities, with the first uprate expected in 2028. The approach aligns with the WEF’s emphasis on evaluating infrastructure as a system. artigo.texto: Power Latin America Speeds Up Battery Storage: Brazil Auctions in December, Mexico Extends Registration Battery storage projects are gaining traction throughout Latin America. Released Wednesday, November 25, 2026 Written by Leonardo Aguirre for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas) Summary Battery storage projects are gaining traction throughout Latin America. Brazil to Hold BESS Auctions in December After Brazil's National Electric Energy Agency (ANEEL) approved the bidding documents on October 27, the country will hold its first auction dedicated exclusively to battery energy storage systems (BESS) on December 2 and 4. The results are expected to be approved in April 2027 and the 15-year supply contracts to take effect on August 1, 2028. Interest was record-high: the Energy Research Company (EPE), the planning agency for the region, received 6,091 proposed projects totaling about 297 gigawatts, while the government plans to contract between 5 and 6 GW. The system operator (ONS) identified more than 50 GW of remaining capacity in 373 substations and blocks across 25 states and the Federal District. The Northeast concentrates 71% of the registered capacity, but 41 of its blocks are listed as lacking capacity for this auction. The main risk is who pays the bill: a legislative change regarding the distribution of the contract would require modifying the bidding terms and could postpone the auction. Mexico, for its part, has extended the registration of storage projects in its strategic call until March 1, 2027. The Ministry of Energy published its call on May 15 and set a reference of 935 megawatts (MW) of storage not associated with generation plants, distributed by regional control management: North (245 MW), East (180 MW), Northwest (160 MW), Baja California (140 MW), Peninsular (140 MW), Baja California South (50 MW) and Western (20 MW). In this case, a different scheme was chosen, since there is no award date: each project must pass studies by the National Center for Energy Control of Mexico (CENACE) and the decision of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE), to then be developed in partnership with the latter. The operating rules and remuneration for storage have not yet been published, which conditions the financing. Elsewhere in Latin America, Argentina and Colombia have already allocated capacity, and the region doubled its storage capacity in one year. On July 3, Argentina awarded, through Resolution 155/2026, 700.5 MW of batteries in 20 AlmaSADI projects: 185 MW in the province of Buenos Aires, 211.5 MW in the Northeast, 150 MW in the Northwest, 86 MW in the Littoral and 68 MW in the Pampa. All are outside the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area, which had already received 713 MW in AlmaGBA. The target date for the contracts is January 1, 2027, and the maximum commercial authorization is December 31, 2029. Colombia awarded nearly 100 MW of batteries at the end of July, associated with solar projects and deliveries between 2030 and 2035, despite buyers expressing interest in a much larger amount. Although no specific auctions are recorded in Chile, the country is a pioneer and absolute regional leader in the development of BESS projects, concentrating two-thirds of the total regional capacity. The Industrial Info Resources Power Project (IIR) database reflects this asymmetry: while for Latin America it has 721 active projects involving the installation of BESS systems (both in stand-alone installations and support in generation plants and electrical substations), only 88 of these projects are in Mexico, compared to 409 in Chile. The Global Market Intelligence (GMI) project database offers a list of detailed project reports. The recent acceleration in the development of BESS projects in the region is mainly due to a grid problem. In Brazil, cuts in wind and solar generation for energy reasons totaled 18.67 terawatt-hours (TWh) between January and September 2026, 52.7% more than a year earlier, with estimated losses of R$15.5 billion (US$2.7 billion). The Northeast accounted for nearly 83% of the curtailment up to August, and the ONS estimates that storage could reduce these cuts by between 40% and 50%, depending on the auction results. The intermittency explains the design of other mechanisms. Colombia included a supply product from 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. (local time), the peak demand slot when solar power falls. In Chile, most batteries are in the north and take advantage of solar energy, which the system does not consume. The demand for data centers adds pressure on the nodes themselves. Industrial Info Resources is tracking 71 active data center projects in Mexico, led by the CloudHQ campus in Colón, Querétaro, and 277 in Brazil, with Dataspots in Nova Iguaçu and Terranova in Praia Grande. Key Takeaways - Brazil will hold its first auction dedicated exclusively to BESS projects on December 2 and 4. - Mexico has extended the registration of storage projects in its strategic call until March 1, 2027. - Chile is the regional leader in the development of BESS projects. artigo.texto: Trump ameaça proibir data centers de americanos fora do país. Regulamentação do Redata no Brasil empaca. Presidente dos EUA informou que estaria disposto a impor um 'imposto enorme' para impedir que empresas norte-americanas construam data centers fora do país. Aqui no Brasil, a regulamentação do Redata empaca e ninguém explica o porquê. O presidente Donald Trump ameaçou tributar empresas norte-americanas que construírem data centers no exterior — uma medida que, segundo ele, ajudaria o setor de Inteligência Artificial do país a manter-se à frente da China. “Não vamos permitir que nossas empresas construam data centers fora do nosso país”, disse Trump em uma coletiva de imprensa na Casa Branca, na semana passada, após sua viagem à Ásia, informou a Reuters. Ele declarou que imporia um “imposto enorme” às empresas caso elas construam data centers no exterior. Trump não forneceu detalhes sobre como planeja aplicar esses impostos às empresas de tecnologia e de IA que apoiaram sua presidência. A medida, se vingar, afeta muito o mercado brasileiro. Empresas como a Equinix, Digital Realty, AWS, Google e outras teriam de rever seus projetos em plena época de debate sobre soberania digital. As declarações mais recentes de Trump seguem outras iniciativas relacionadas à IA, incluindo uma determinação para que grandes empresas de tecnologia construam suas próprias usinas de energia, bem como um plano de ação voltado a garantir a supremacia na área de IA. Segundo a agência de notícias, Trump tem defendido enfaticamente a construção de data centers nos Estados Unidos, embora estados e comunidades em todo o país tenham manifestado resistência devido à demanda por eletricidade, aos custos de serviços públicos e a outros impactos locais. Na semana passada, o Departamento de Comércio dos EUA tomou medidas para restringir a exportação de chips avançados de IA para diversos países do Sudeste Asiático — parte de um esforço mais amplo para impedir que a China obtenha essa tecnologia por meio de terceiros países. E que também afetou diretamente o Brasil. Enquanto isso, a prometida regulamentação do Redata, para depois da volta do presidente Lula ao Brasil da viagem à Ásia. Aqui o texto empacou na Casa Civil e não há explicações sobre o porquê.

artigo.texto: CBRE Group Eyes Mid-Double-Digit Growth as Data Center and Infrastructure Demand Builds CBRE Group CBRE expects to grow in the “mid-double digits” next year and finish the current year strongly, Chairman, CEO and President Bob Sulentic said at JPMorgan’s Ultimate Services Investor Conference. Sulentic said the company’s outlook remains largely consistent with what it articulated on its most recent earnings call. He also pointed to growth in infrastructure services and recurring businesses as factors that have made CBRE less dependent on the commercial real estate capital markets cycle. Infrastructure and data center demand CBRE has shifted its business mix toward what it calls resilient businesses, which generate recurring revenue and are countercyclical or acyclical, Sulentic said. He said those businesses now represent 60% of the company’s business. Infrastructure work spans all four of CBRE’s reporting segments and includes assignments involving data centers, energy, water and transportation. Sulentic said the company is ahead of its previously discussed goal of reaching $10 billion in infrastructure-related revenue by 2030. On its latest earnings call, CBRE discussed having $7 billion in that type of revenue next year, he said. In data centers, CBRE oversees construction, installs network infrastructure and provides mechanical, electrical and plumbing project services, as well as ongoing facilities management. Sulentic said refitting existing data centers is also a significant opportunity as operators seek more computing capacity. Sulentic said the midterm election results could slow new data center development for a time, but he does not expect a notable impact on CBRE’s business. He cited demand that has exceeded the company’s capacity, its expanding overseas presence and work on existing facilities. CBRE’s Direct Line acquisition added U.S. data center network infrastructure capabilities, while Onnec provides similar services outside the United States, including in the Nordics and Malaysia, Sulentic said. Facilities growth and capital markets Sulentic expects CBRE’s traditional facilities management business to grow at a low-teens rate overall. He projected mid-teens or better growth for its local facilities management business, compared with high-single-digit to potentially double-digit growth in large corporate outsourcing. Capital markets remain important to CBRE, but their effect on the company’s overall growth trajectory is smaller than it was a decade ago, Sulentic said. Uncertainty about interest rates has recently caused some participants to move to the sidelines, he said. CBRE expects capital markets-related activity in commercial real estate to remain “flattish” through at least the middle of next year. Sulentic said greater certainty about rates could encourage more trading in the second half, though he does not expect rates to fall substantially. In leasing, CBRE expects double-digit growth in the fourth quarter and mid- to high-single-digit growth next year, led by industrial leasing. Sulentic said office leasing has also been strong, though limited availability of Class A space in the United States has created challenges. Acquisitions and buybacks Sulentic said strategic acquisitions remain CBRE’s preferred use of capital, with opportunities in technical services, facilities management, critical infrastructure and project management. The company also supports its real estate investment businesses through co-investments and direct investments. CBRE continues to repurchase shares when it believes they trade below intrinsic value, Sulentic said. He said buybacks have likely been the company’s largest use of capital over the past few years, while adding that CBRE has not been capital constrained in pursuing acquisitions and real estate investments. About CBRE Group CBRE CBRE Group, Inc. is a commercial real estate services and investment company serving property owners, occupiers, investors and developers. Its services include property leasing and sales, property and facilities management, project management, valuation, consulting and commercial real estate financing. The company also provides real estate investment management and development services. Through its global operations, CBRE serves clients across a range of property types and markets, including offices, industrial facilities, retail properties and data centers. artigo.texto: SAN DIEGO (KGTV) — The battle over data centers has entered a new era. Several local cities have banned the facilities, while others have passed moratoriums. However, Cal State University San Marcos Political Science Professor Larry Gerston said a local ban can only go so far — and comes as Trump is insisting the facilities be built in America. Gerston told ABC 10News he's writing a book called Breaking Point. "It's about the issues that are driving concerns in America." Gerston said. Gerston said one of the main concerns, on both sides, has to do with data centers. "And so the question is, of course, if it's worth having it, what are the gains from having it versus the losses from having it? That's the conversation. That's the national conversation. That's the state conversation. That's the local conversation." Gerston said. That local conversation on large-scale data centers has been dominated by resistance. It's been about a month since the City of San Diego temporarily halted the development of data centers, in response to a potential project at the Naval Information Warfare Systems Command — or NAVWAR — site in the Midway District. Escondido also put a pause on their development. Poway banned them outright. At the federal level, it's a different story. "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country. We're not going to allow that to happen," Trump said in a press conference last Friday after meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Gerston said, "In other words, that leads to a bit of a controversy given resistance that we have — and therein lies the problem." Part of the problem is a loophole, per se, in the system. Local bans have little to no influence on federal land. For example, since the NAVWAR site is owned by the U.S. Navy, a city ban alone wouldn't stop a data center from being built there. Gerston said public opinion could provide the real power. "I think you can expect to see Congress act on that. You can expect to see it go all the way to the President's desk, and at that point, as they say, where the rubber meets the road, we'll have to see just what the President says." Gerston said. artigo.texto: Gelion CEO on Worley partnership, battery scale-up and licensing opportunities Published: 04:50 23 Nov 2026 EST Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF) CEO Matt Wood talked with Proactive about its pre-FEED collaboration with global engineering group Worley to advance production of its nano-encapsulated sulfur (NES) cathode material. Wood explained how Worley's expertise in cathode materials and sulfur processing will help Gelion validate manufacturing processes and develop preliminary designs for a potential pilot plant. The work will cover plant layouts, production requirements, cost estimates and project timelines, helping reduce investment risks ahead of a scale-up decision. The interview also explores growing partnerships across drones, electric vehicles and consumer devices. Wood said existing production capacity can meet near-term demand, but additional volumes will be needed as commercial relationships develop. He outlined the company's strategy of expanding capacity in response to anticipated customer demand, rather than building ahead of the market. Finally, Wood discussed the potential to license NES technology, explaining how the Worley collaboration will help establish the manufacturing processes needed to support future commercial agreements and revenue opportunities. artigo.texto: UPCL Invites Bids for 41 MW/102.5 MWh Battery Storage Projects 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Uttarakhand Power Corporation has invited bids to establish 41 MW/102.5 MWh of grid-interactive standalone Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) across six 33/11 kV substations in Uttarakhand. The projects will be developed under the Build-Own-Operate model through capacity charge-based competitive bidding, with Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support of up to Rs. 1.8 mn per MWh. The tender, numbered CCP-I/49/2026-2027, was issued on November 17, 2026. The pre-bid meeting is scheduled for November 26 at 11:30 am at UPCL’s Dehradun office, with online participation available. Bidders must submit queries by 5 pm on the same day through the designated tender email address. The combined capacity will be distributed across substations in Uttarkashi, Haridwar and Tehri districts. The identified locations are Kalyani and Dhanarigaad in Uttarkashi, SIDCUL Sector 8 and Jwalapur 2 in Haridwar, New Manglaur in Roorkee, and Rajakhet in Tehri. Individual project capacities range from 4 MW/10 MWh to 10 MW/25 MWh. Selected systems must complete two charge-discharge cycles daily. Each cycle will include 2.5 hours of discharge during the morning peak and another 2.5 hours during the evening peak. UPCL will provide land at its substations to successful developers under a Right of Use arrangement. The VGF assistance will be provided as non-recurring financial support and funded entirely by the central government. Developers will handle design, financing, supply, installation, commissioning, operations and maintenance. Projects must be commissioned within 12 months of the later of the effective date of the Battery Energy Storage Purchase Agreement (BESPA) or land handover, while the BESPA will run for 12 years after full commissioning. The tender requires an earnest money deposit of Rs. 41.3 mn, while the bid submission and opening schedules are set out in the Notice Inviting Tender. artigo.texto: Balmer Lawrie Invites Bids for 522 kWh BESS and Solar Project 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Balmer Lawrie & Co. has invited online bids to establish a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with a 600 kW solar power plant at its industrial packaging facility in Taloja, Navi Mumbai. The contract covers the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of a 522 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery storage system. The proposed BESS will store surplus electricity generated during daylight hours and supply it during the evening and periods of peak demand. The project is intended to improve solar power utilisation and strengthen energy management at the facility. The tender has been issued through the company’s e-procurement portal under reference number 0100PC3430. Eligible bidders must be registered entities with an average annual turnover of at least Rs. 9 mn during the financial years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. They must also demonstrate experience in solar power execution, including at least one grid-connected solar installation with a capacity of 300 kW or higher. Bidders must be based in Mumbai or within approximately 200 km by road, maintain an office or authorised service centre in Maharashtra and hold a valid state electrical contractor licence. A site visit to the Taloja facility is mandatory, with bidders required to submit valid attendance proof. A gate pass alone will not be accepted. No advance payment will be made to the successful bidder. The tender was published on November 17, 2026, and proposals must be submitted by November 27 at 16:00 hours, with opening scheduled for 16:05 hours the same day. The selected bidder must confirm purchase-order acceptance within seven days and complete the project within 10 weeks of site clearance. The tender requires an Earnest Money Deposit of Rs. 45,000, although eligible Micro and Small Enterprises with valid registration are exempt. Security Deposit is set at 3 per cent of the basic order value, while 10 per cent of the total order value will be retained as performance security, subject to the stated release and guarantee conditions.
