artigo.texto: A previsão de instalação de um data center com investimento estimado em R$ 3 bilhões em Atibaia, no interior de São Paulo, tem provocado mobilização de moradores do Bairro do Tanque. O empreendimento, denominado Data Center Alfa e desenvolvido pela empresa DataSpots, ligada ao Grupo ON, tem previsão de iniciar as operações entre 2029 e 2030. A comunidade questiona a falta de informações sobre o projeto e manifesta preocupação com os possíveis impactos da estrutura sobre os recursos hídricos, o meio ambiente e a qualidade de vida na região. Como resposta, o movimento popular Fora Data Center organizou um abaixo-assinado que, até meados de novembro de 2026, havia reunido mais de 4 mil assinaturas. O grupo também elaborou uma petição solicitando que a Prefeitura encaminhe à Câmara Municipal um projeto de lei complementar para alterar o Plano Diretor e o Código de Obras, com o objetivo de estabelecer restrições à instalação de data centers de hiperescala no município. Os moradores defendem que a população tenha acesso aos estudos técnicos e participe das discussões antes do avanço das etapas de implantação. Empreendimento prevê estrutura de grande porte O terreno inicialmente previsto para receber o Data Center Alfa fica no Bairro do Tanque, em uma área de transição entre as zonas rural e urbana de Atibaia. A propriedade possui dimensão equivalente a aproximadamente 50 campos de futebol. Segundo as informações apresentadas sobre o projeto, a estrutura terá capacidade energética projetada de 50 megawatts (MW) e conexão à infraestrutura elétrica de 138 quilovolts (kV). A capacidade prevista não corresponde necessariamente ao consumo efetivo do complexo, que dependerá das instalações construídas e das condições de funcionamento. Data centers são estruturas utilizadas para processamento e armazenamento de dados, hospedagem de serviços digitais, computação em nuvem e aplicações de inteligência artificial. Para operar, precisam de fornecimento contínuo de energia elétrica e sistemas de refrigeração. Moradores apontam preocupação com abastecimento de água Uma das principais questões levantadas pela comunidade envolve a disponibilidade de água no Bairro do Tanque. Parte das famílias depende de poços particulares para o abastecimento doméstico, enquanto a rede pública não atende integralmente a região. O bairro também não possui cobertura completa de coleta e tratamento de esgoto. Os moradores temem que a instalação de uma estrutura desse porte aumente a pressão sobre os recursos hídricos locais, especialmente em razão da necessidade de refrigeração dos equipamentos. O consumo de água, porém, dependerá da tecnologia escolhida para o resfriamento. Existem sistemas que utilizam volumes expressivos do recurso e outros que operam com circuitos fechados ou mecanismos de menor necessidade de reposição. Sem a apresentação do projeto técnico, não é possível dimensionar o impacto sobre o abastecimento. Gabriel Tonobohn, morador do bairro há três anos e meio, relata dificuldades já enfrentadas pela comunidade durante os períodos de estiagem. “A gente mora em um bairro que não tem saneamento, não tem água encanada, não tem esgoto. Então, todo mundo que mora no bairro onde vai ser colocado esse data center depende de poço para ter água. A maioria usa um poço caipira e já está ficando sem água na época de seca”, afirma. Possíveis impactos ambientais e sonoros estão entre as preocupações O movimento Fora Data Center também aponta riscos relacionados à retirada de vegetação nativa da Mata Atlântica, a possíveis alterações no lençol freático e ao aumento da temperatura no entorno do empreendimento. Outra preocupação envolve a eventual utilização de reservatórios de óleo diesel para abastecer geradores de emergência, equipamentos que podem manter o funcionamento de data centers em situações de interrupção no fornecimento de energia. Os moradores temem que problemas de armazenamento ou vazamentos possam atingir o solo e a água subterrânea. Entretanto, as características dos reservatórios previstos para o Data Center Alfa ainda precisam ser esclarecidas por documentação técnica. A existência desses equipamentos, por si só, não comprova a ocorrência de contaminação. A emissão de ruídos também preocupa quem vive nas proximidades. Gabriel afirma que a região não dispõe de barreiras acústicas suficientes e que sons produzidos por equipamentos já existentes podem ser ouvidos dentro das residências. “Qualquer barulho que acontece na rua, a gente ouve, mesmo que esteja longe. A gente ouve quando a subestação de energia soa um alarme, não conseguimos dormir. Então, se você tiver um ruído de um data center ali, certamente todo mundo vai ouvir, todo mundo vai ficar incomodado com isso”, relata. A comunidade também questiona os possíveis efeitos do aumento da temperatura provocado pelos equipamentos e sistemas de refrigeração. O receio é de que mudanças nas condições ambientais e sonoras afetem as famílias que vivem há décadas no bairro. Gabriel afirma que muitos moradores possuem vínculos familiares e residenciais antigos na região e teme que eventuais impactos tornem o local inadequado para a permanência dessas pessoas. Autorização para conexão elétrica foi concedida em 2025 A discussão sobre o empreendimento também envolve intervenções previstas na infraestrutura de transmissão de energia. Em outubro de 2025, o Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) autorizou a conexão relacionada ao Data Center Alfa à infraestrutura elétrica da região. O documento prevê a ampliação de aproximadamente 15 quilômetros de linha de transmissão e a instalação de dois novos módulos de entrada de linha em 138 kV. As intervenções estão relacionadas à conexão do empreendimento à Subestação Atibaia 2 e à ampliação da capacidade de atendimento energético. Em 17 de junho de 2026, a concessionária ISA Energia apresentou, em audiência pública, um estudo de impacto de vizinhança referente à implantação dos ramais de seccionamento para interligação da Li

artigo.texto: Natalie Hassell lives about a mile from what could become one of the largest data centers in the country. “Less as the crow flies,” she said. She lives in Dallesport, Washington, a rural community in Klickitat County along the Columbia River near the Oregon border. A few months ago, she learned a developer was shopping around a proposal for a hyperscale data center campus down the road, the type often used to train and run artificial intelligence models “ Too close for comfort for me,” she said. “I just don't think it belongs. We're a neighborhood. We're not an industrial area here.” If built out to full capacity, the nearly 300-acre site could one day house a one-gigawatt data center covering millions of square feet. Only two data centers in the U.S. have greater energy capacity, according to the energy infrastructure tracking firm Cleanview, though plans for larger facilities are underway across the country. Hassell and other community members are organizing to block the project by putting pressure on local officials, working with nonprofits and activists in the area, and advocating for local and statewide moratoria on new data center construction. Local businessman Scott Webster owns the property and contracted the real estate developer Cushman and Wakefield to shop it around. The marketing materials became public after community members in Klickitat County, where Dallesport is located, submitted a public records request. “Our objective is not simply to sell property,” Webster said in an emailed statement. “We want to find the right development partner who shares our vision for creating a meaningful, long-term economic opportunity for Dallesport and Klickitat County.” Webster said he believes the project could bring jobs and infrastructure improvements to the area, and he supports a community benefits agreement that would establish commitments to that effect. No permit applications have been filed on behalf of the project, but according to the pitch deck, Cushman and Wakefield is in talks with the Bonneville Power Administration to secure up to 1GW of energy. The document says power could come from hydroelectricity produced by the Columbia River, solar, or liquified natural gas via a proposed pipeline expansion. Jenn Sharp, one of the community members fighting the project, said she already has a gas pipeline 1,600 feet from her front door and doesn't want to see it extended. “We've got the pipeline coming here just north of us in our backyard. We have the threat of a high voltage… power line running up the Columbia to power data centers in Portland,” she said. “All of the tangential threats that this industry is bringing to rural communities sits really heavily with me. These developers know that they're going into communities that are not sophisticated enough to know what questions to ask.” Though the proposal indicates plans to use renewable energy sources and explore the possibility of a closed-loop water system, Sharp and Hassell are both concerned about the resource and environmental costs on the community. But their concerns go beyond the potential on-the-ground impacts. They said AI is moving too fast, and they see data center opposition as a way to slow it down. “I don't like the whole concept of artificial intelligence,” Hassell said. “I think there's a lot of surveillance technology going on. I'm not for all these Flock cameras around. … I feel like it's being shoved in our faces.” Hassell has written to each of the Klickitat County Commissioners urging them not to allow the project to go forward. Sharp plans to advocate for a state-wide data center moratorium during Washington’s upcoming legislative session. “ I have very strong feelings that AI is a significant threat to our planet and to humans,” Sharp said. “Unfortunately, given the current politics, there are no constraints or recognition of what AI is doing. … So, personally, I want there to be a pause, not just on data centers but on AI, so that the human race can catch up.”

artigo.texto: Em vez de depender apenas de baterias químicas gigantes, a engenharia chinesa transformou duas represas em uma montanha numa bateria hidráulica de escala nacional. Por que armazenar água no alto de uma montanha funciona como uma bateria gigante? Pense na caixa d’água no telhado de uma casa: você gasta energia para bombear a água até lá em cima e depois ela desce sozinha pela gravidade quando você abre a torneira. Na engenharia elétrica, esse princípio recebe o nome de armazenamento hidrelétrico reversível. Em Fengning, a água acumulada no reservatório superior guarda energia potencial gravitacional equivalente à de milhões de baterias automotivas, mas sem degradação química ao longo de décadas. Assim, a rede elétrica ganha um pulmão mecânico capaz de absorver sobras de geração e devolver eletricidade em poucos minutos. Quais são os números, turbinas e túneis subterrâneos da Usina de Fengning? Projetada e operada pela estatal State Grid Xinyuan, subsidiária da State Grid Corporation of China, a obra exigiu escavações profundas no maciço rochoso para abrigar tubulações de alta pressão e salas de máquinas. Capacidade total instalada: atinge 3,6 gigawatts (3.600 megawatts), potência suficiente para abastecer milhões de consumidores simultaneamente nos horários de pico noturno. - Conjunto de unidades geradoras: opera com 12 bombas-turbinas reversíveis de 300 megawatts cada, incluindo duas máquinas de velocidade variável fornecidas pela Andritz Hydro para ajuste fino da rede. - Produção anual limpa: gera cerca de 6,61 bilhões de quilowatt-hora por ano, volume que substitui 480 mil toneladas de carvão mineral e evita 1,2 milhão de toneladas de dióxido de carbono. - Casa de força subterrânea: fica enterrada no interior da montanha em uma caverna principal com cerca de 414 metros de comprimento, protegida contra variações climáticas extremas. - Subestação blindada subterrânea: utiliza equipamentos isolados a gás de 500 quilovolts dentro da rocha para enviar energia diretamente às linhas de transmissão de Pequim e Tianjin. Como os dois reservatórios alternam entre bombeamento e geração ao longo do dia? Durante a tarde, quando parques eólicos e usinas solares produzem mais eletricidade do que as cidades consomem, o excesso de energia alimenta os motores elétricos de Fengning. As turbinas giram no sentido inverso e funcionam como bombas gigantes, empurrando a água do reservatório inferior pelos túneis inclinados até o lago superior. Ao anoitecer, quando o sol desaparece e o consumo residencial dispara, comportas de aço abrem os condutos forçados. A água despenca de volta pelo desnível da montanha, gira as mesmas 12 turbinas e injeta eletricidade estável na rede em menos de dois minutos. Como a usina de Fengning foi estruturada para abastecer a região de Pequim com energia limpa? Construída para integrar os grandes parques eólicos e solares de Zhangjiakou à rede elétrica da capital chinesa, a obra enfrentou invernos rigorosos e terrenos montanhosos íngremes. A infraestrutura entrou em operação gradual a partir dos Jogos Olímpicos de Inverno de 2022 e alcançou sua capacidade máxima de 3,6 gigawatts no encerramento de 2024. Abaixo, um vídeo do New China TV que aprofunda o tema: Quais normas técnicas garantem a segurança das barragens e cavernas subterrâneas? Como a água sobe e desce todos os dias, as encostas dos reservatórios sofrem ciclos rápidos de pressão que não existem em hidrelétricas comuns. Por isso, as bombas-turbinas seguem protocolos internacionais como a norma IEC 60193, que testa modelos hidráulicos contra vibração e cavitação. No Brasil, projetos semelhantes de barragens e usinas reversíveis obedecem às regras da ABNT NBR 6118 para resistência do concreto estrutural e às diretrizes técnicas do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS). Assim, evita-se erosão nos taludes e fadiga nas tubulações de aço sob alta pressão. Quando é indispensável contratar um engenheiro hidráulico ou geotécnico? Qualquer empreendimento que envolva barragens de acumulação, reservatórios em desnível ou escavações subterrâneas exige o trabalho integrado de um engenheiro civil especialista em obras hidráulicas e de um engenheiro geotécnico. Não é uma estrutura que possa ser adaptada sem estudos profundos de maciço rochoso porque a infiltração de água sob alta pressão pode provocar deslizamentos nos taludes ou colapso das cavernas. Contexto importante: Este artigo é informativo. Para projetos estruturais locais similares, recomenda-se avaliação de engenheiro civil especialista em estruturas hidráulicas e engenheiro geotécnico, especialmente em contextos de risco de infiltração sob alta pressão, instabilidade de taludes e comprometimento estrutural de barragens.

artigo.texto: Rapid growth in data center construction is creating demand for material handling equipment and warehouse automation to manage the rising volumes of technology components like servers, racks, components, and spare parts, according to a report by Interact Analysis. The rising demand for logistics services occurs because all the technical hardware that powers data center operations must be stored, staged, integrated, and moved. Of the different types of facilities in the data center ecosystem, that demand is rising fastest at spare parts & staging warehouses, which act as consolidation centers for components sourced from multiple OEMs for both the build out and the replenishment of spare parts, according to the report titled “Data Centers Drive Growth for Material Handling and Robotics.” Over the longer term, investments in robotics within data centers themselves also hold a lot of potential, although it will likely remain unrealized in the short- to mid-term, given the complexity of the various tasks required. Interact Analysis described four types of data centers: Hyperscale data centers are very large facilities operated by major cloud and internet companies; colocation facilities provide shared space, power, cooling and connectivity to multiple customers (broadly analogous to a third-party logistics model); enterprise data centers support the requirements of a single organization; and edge data centers are smaller facilities located closer to users and devices to reduce latency. And finally, some additional logistics demand will also be generated by server integration facilities, which assemble, configure, and test complete server racks before shipping them to data centers, reducing on-site installation time and accelerating deployment and replacement cycles.

artigo.texto: Senate approves bill to speed up permitting reviews, force data centers to pay for energy costs WASHINGTON (AP) — The Senate approved bipartisan legislation Thursday aimed at speeding up permitting reviews to build power plants, transmission lines and other energy infrastructure as lawmakers seek to increase the nation’s energy supplies to meet surging demand and lower electricity prices. The legislation’s sweeping changes would shorten the timeline to start big energy projects and make sure data centers pay for the energy they use. Anger over data centers and rising electricity prices helped usher in a wave of Democrats pledging to clamp down on the energy-hungry behemoths. The 62-33 vote is the first major action by Congress since midterm elections that soundly repudiated President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans. The bill now goes to the House, which approved a more limited, industry-friendly version last year. The Senate bill would overhaul several environmental laws to make it easier to build energy infrastructure, drawing criticism from Democrats and environmental groups about limits on judicial review and changes to bedrock laws such as the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act. Trump urged approval of the bill, calling it a “BIG WIN for U.S. ENERGY INDEPENDENCE and DOMINANCE” in a recent social media post. The bill, formally known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, will ensure the U.S. can build pipelines, mines and power plants more quickly, “lowering Energy Costs for American Families,” Trump wrote. Fifteen Democrats, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, voted for the bill. Two Republicans, Josh Hawley of Missouri and Mike Rounds of South Dakota, voted no. Industry groups back bill, but environmentalists fear it would weaken safeguards Major industry groups representing developers in clean energy and the oil and gas sector support the bill as a way to deliver more electricity to the grid and avoid delays for infrastructure projects that can stretch a decade or more. However, many environmental organizations have denounced the measure, saying it would lock in fossil fuel development, weaken environmental safeguards and make it harder for communities to challenge energy project approvals. “Make no mistake: This backroom deal will pave the way for even more fossil fuel projects like gas power plants for data centers, oil and gas pipelines and (liquefied natural gas) terminals while sacrificing fundamental and common-sense public health and environmental protections for communities across the U.S.,” said Jen Duggan, executive director of the Environmental Integrity Project. Benefits for renewable energy are outweighed by likely increases in greenhouse gas emissions and air and water pollution from the fossil fuel industry, Duggan and other critics said. She called the bill “a gift to some of the biggest polluters in America” and complained that it was being rushed through a lame-duck Congress without public hearings or sufficient debate. Democrats push for amendments A final vote on the measure was held up this week as Oregon’s two Democratic senators pushed to add amendments, including one to ban data centers on public lands. Sens. Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden are among several Democrats in both chambers who say the party should use its stronger position in the next Congress to pass legislation that boosts clean energy, such as solar and wind power, while limiting expansion of oil, natural gas and other fossil fuels. “Getting more renewable electrons where they are needed doesn’t tackle climate change if you simultaneously promote the burning of more fossil fuels. Unfortunately, this bill does exactly that,” Merkley said. Majority Republicans stymied Merkley’s effort to ensure votes on a host of amendments, including one that would block the Trump administration from continuing to cancel clean energy grants and other Democratic priorities for “purely political purposes.” The bill’s sponsors reneged on promises of “a robust amendment process,” he said. In the end, the measure was approved without amendments offered by rank-and-file senators. “I do think that this bill is very consequential to the future of this planet,” Merkley said. Major environmental groups, including the Sierra Club and National Wildlife Federation, oppose the bill, citing concerns about limits on judicial review and changes to the National Environmental Policy Act and other laws. The environmental policy law, known as NEPA, requires agencies to consider a project’s possible impacts and allows the public to be heard before a project is approved. The current review process often takes five years or more, and shortening that time frame is a key goal of the bill. “In America today, it takes too long and costs too much to build,” said Wyoming Sen. John Barrasso, the No. 2 Republican in the Senate. “Energy projects that would help lower prices remain frozen for years” as they await approval by the federal government. “Construction cannot start without first spending years in the regulatory penalty box,” driving up costs and creating uncertainty, Barrasso said. The bill’s four main champions — two Democrats and two Republicans — have released a detailed set of amendments designed to bolster support for the legislation. The four senators, who lead the chamber’s energy and environment panels, negotiated the deal a few weeks before the election. Republican Sens. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia and Mike Lee of Utah and Democratic Sens. Martin Heinrich of New Mexico and Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island say Americans are tired of paying more in utility bills while projects that could lower costs sit stuck in the planning phase for years. “We are going to make it easier to build in America again, and make life more affordable for American families,” Lee said. artigo.texto: McHenry County has hit the pause button on data centers. The County Board has approved a 12-month moratorium on the controversial projects. The vote was 17-1, with only board member Terri Greeno, R-Crystal Lake, voting no. Greeno said before the vote the county was able to implement battery storage regulations quickly and hoped the county wouldn’t need a year to update its ordinances for data centers. County Board Chair Mike Buehler, R-Crystal Lake, defended the moratorium in response to Greeno’s comments. “I think our goal is to get it right. If it takes us a year to do it, that’s what ... we’re going to do,” Buehler said. Resident Zaynab Ritchie asked the board to implement the moratorium, citing potential pollution, negative health effects, noise and electricity and water consumption. “Please enact the data center moratorium and prioritize your people’s needs over the needs of a machine,” Ritchie said. Board member Joe Gottemoller, another Crystal Lake Republican, was active in pushing for the moratorium and said its approval was a “step in the right direction.” Gottemoller said the county doesn’t have ordinances to regulate data centers and was concerned someone would apply for a data center and be allowed to operate it without regulations. He said data centers are very large buildings and should not have any regulations on them. It was the last meeting for both Gottemoller and Greeno as County Board members, as they lost their reelection bids this month to Democrats Edward “Bud” Bowie Jr. and Austin May, respectively. The data center moratorium is meant to give the county time to come up with regulations for the data projects. No applications are currently active for data centers in the county, officials have said. Adam Wallen, the county’s director of planning and development, previously said the 12-month moratorium is there so the county can develop standards so it’s prepared when a data center applicant comes along. The board can extend, tweak or repeal the moratorium during the 12-month timeframe. McHenry’s is not the first data center moratorium an area county has approved. Neighboring Lake County approved an eight-month pause in September. The counties’ actions only apply to unincorporated areas. Municipalities set their own rules.

artigo.texto: 24 Novembro 2026 "São necessários estudos de amplitude global para avaliar outros efeitos danosos dos grandes data centers", escreve Vivaldo José Breternitz, Doutor em Ciências pela Universidade de São Paulo, professor, consultor e diretor do Fórum Brasileiro de Internet das Coisas, em artigo publicado por EcoDebate, 23-11-2026. Eis o artigo. Os centros de dados ao redor do mundo deverão aumentar suas emissões de carbono em 70% até 2030, impulsionadas principalmente pelo maior uso de combustíveis fósseis nos Estados Unidos e na China, segundo a Agência Internacional de Energia (AIE). A Agência estima que os centros de dados dobrarão o consumo de eletricidade até o fim da década, sendo que a expansão do uso da inteligência artificial (IA) responderá por cerca de 75% desse crescimento. Para o diretor-executivo da AIE, Fatih Birol, o setor energético global atravessa uma transformação estrutural; segundo ele, não há perspectivas de retorno ao cenário anterior às recentes crises geopolíticas e energéticas. A agência avalia que o aumento da demanda por eletricidade será impulsionado por dois fatores além do maior uso de IA: o crescimento da população mundial e a expansão do uso de sistemas de refrigeração. 🔍 Adicione o Instituto Humanitas Unisinos – IHU às suas fontes favoritas do Google Embora as empresas do setor de data centers estejam entre os maiores consumidores de energia renovável do mundo, a AIE projeta um crescimento rápido do consumo de combustíveis fósseis para abastecer os novos centros de dados, pois na China, até 2030, cerca de metade da eletricidade consumida pelos centros de dados de IA deverá vir da queima de carvão. O restante será suprido principalmente por fontes renováveis, além de pequenas participações de energia nuclear e gás natural. Moradores do interior de SP tentam barrar a chegada de datacenter de R$ 3 bi: ‘Ninguém está feliz' https://t.co/ZJOwwvZn7D — Oliver Stuenkel 🇧🇷 (@OliverStuenkel) November 23, 2026 Já nos Estados Unidos, a tendência é diferente. A expectativa é que o gás natural forneça cerca de 60% da eletricidade utilizada pelos centros de dados até o fim da década. Segundo a agência, há planos para a instalação de aproximadamente 180 gigawatts (GW) em novas usinas movidas a gás destinadas ao setor, capacidade próxima à atualmente instalada em toda a União Europeia. Na União Europeia, o cenário é distinto. A AIE estima que aproximadamente 70% da eletricidade consumida pelos centros de dados em 2030 terá origem em fontes renováveis, complementadas por energia nuclear e gás natural, com participação mínima do carvão. Para elaborar suas projeções, a agência analisou o mercado global de servidores de IA, cujas vendas cresceram 18 vezes desde 2020, além de monitorar por satélite a construção de 93 grandes instalações dedicadas à tecnologia. São necessários estudos de amplitude global para avaliar outros efeitos danosos dos grandes data centers, tais como poluição sonora e da água utilizada em sua refrigeração.

Jornal do Carro levou a picape intermediária da marca chinesa para um dia na pista de testes e descobriu detalhes sobre versões e ambições de mercado do modelo O Denza B5 será o primeiro modelo da marca de luxo da BYD produzido no Brasil. Alexandre Baldy, vice-presidente sênior da companhia para o Brasil, confirmou durante evento realizado nesta terça-feira (24) que a fábrica de Camaçari, na Bahia, começará a fabricar o SUV híbrido plug-in 4x4 em 2027. A confirmação vem quatro meses depois de Stella Li, vice-presidente global da BYD, revelar ao Jornal do Carro que a empresa estudava trazer o B5 para a linha baiana. Em julho, durante o Festival de Goodwood, na Inglaterra, a executiva citou meados de 2027 como provável data de início da produção e apontou a expansão da rede de recarga rápida como prioridade para a marca no País. E o preço, pode cair? Hoje, o B5 importado da China custa R$ 405 mil na versão GL e R$ 505 mil na GS. A fabricação local pode abrir espaço para uma redução, mas a BYD ainda não anunciou quanto pretende cobrar pelo SUV baiano. O B5 chegará à linha de Camaçari depois de superar a marca de 3,7 mil emplacamentos no Brasil entre janeiro e outubro de 2026. Só no mês passado foram 577 unidades, resultado que garantiu ao SUV da Denza o quinto mês seguido na liderança do segmento de luxo. No acumulado do ano, o BMW X1 ainda estava à frente, com 3.949 unidades. Fábrica de Camaçari mira 600 mil carros por ano Segundo Baldy, o investimento da BYD em Camaçari já ultrapassa R$ 11 bilhões. A atividade industrial no complexo reúne quase 9,5 mil trabalhadores, dos quais 1,1 mil foram contratados nas últimas semanas. O plano prevê operação em três turnos e capacidade para fabricar 300 mil veículos por ano na primeira fase. A segunda acrescentará outros 300 mil, o que elevará o total a 600 mil unidades anuais. A companhia já iniciou os pedidos de licença para a expansão. Atualmente, a linha baiana monta veículos com kits de peças que vêm da China. A fábrica está na fase final de implantação das áreas de estamparia e soldagem. Com elas, a BYD poderá dar forma às chapas de metal e unir as peças da carroceria em Camaçari, duas etapas que ampliam a participação de componentes fabricados no Brasil. Como é o Denza B5 que será fabricado na Bahia O Denza B5 tem carroceria sobre chassi, construção comum em picapes, e pesa de 2.897 kg na versão GL a 3,055 toneladas na GS. Ainda assim, as duas aceleram de 0 a 100 km/h em 4,8 segundos, de acordo com a fabricante. Quem dá conta de toda essa massa é um conjunto híbrido plug-in com motor 1.5 turbo a gasolina e dois elétricos, um em cada eixo. Juntos, entregam 687 cv de potência e 77,5 kgfm de torque, com tração nas quatro rodas. A bateria de 31,8 kWh fica integrada à estrutura de aço do chassi. Ela permite percorrer até 81 km só com eletricidade pelo PBEV. O B5 aceita recarga de até 11 kW em corrente alternada e 100 kW em corrente contínua. A energia também pode fazer o caminho inverso. Com o cabo fornecido nas duas versões, é possível usar a bateria do carro para alimentar aparelhos elétricos por meio do V2L. Ambas as configurações têm bloqueios eletrônicos dos diferenciais dianteiro e traseiro, que ajudam a manter a tração quando uma das rodas perde aderência. É na suspensão, contudo, que a GS leva vantagem sobre a GL. O sistema hidráulico adaptativo DiSus-P permite variar a altura da carroceria em até 14 cm. Na posição mais alta, o vão livre do solo chega a 31 cm, ante 22 cm na versão de entrada. A capacidade de reboque é a mesma para as duas, de até 2,5 toneladas quando o trailer tem freios próprios. O que muda entre o B5 de R$ 405 mil e o de R$ 505 mil? Com cerca de 4,90 metros de comprimento e 2,80 m de entre-eixos, o B5 acomoda cinco pessoas e tem porta-malas de 470 litros. Na GL, de R$ 405 mil, os bancos dianteiros já oferecem ajustes elétricos, ventilação e massagem. O motorista tem à frente um quadro de instrumentos de 12,3 polegadas e pode consultar informações projetadas no para-brisa. No centro do painel fica a tela de 15,6 polegadas, com Apple CarPlay e Android Auto. Teto solar panorâmico e som, cortesia da Devialet, com 18 alto-falantes também vêm de série. Na GS, de R$ 505 mil, quem viaja no banco dianteiro direito ganha uma tela própria de 12,3 polegadas. Os bancos recebem revestimento de couro Nappa e aquecimento nas duas fileiras. Atrás, os passageiros também passam a contar com ventilação nos assentos. No exterior, as rodas de 20 polegadas distinguem a GS da GL, que usa aro 18. Já o pacote de assistência inclui, desde a versão de entrada, controle de cruzeiro adaptativo, frenagem automática de emergência, monitoramento de pontos cegos e câmeras com visão de 360 graus.

artigo.texto: Pennsylvania legislators railed against Olyphant Borough Council’s recent decision to settle a developer’s lawsuit and warned of the precedent it sets to allow Project Triboro’s seven data centers to move forward without conditional use hearings in exchange for $101 million. “I’m perplexed and confounded by the decision,” state Rep. Kyle Mullins, D-112, Blakely, said Thursday. “To totally extinguish the opportunity for the conditional use public hearing process is extremely disappointing to me as a resident and as an area leader.” Olyphant council voted 5-2 twice on Tuesday to approve a settlement with Victor, New York-based ERCOR Triboro LLC and subsequently approve a community benefits agreement, or CBA, that will pay the borough $101 million over 15 years. Prior to council’s votes, more than two dozen Lackawanna County residents spoke out against the settlement and CBA during a nearly three-hour special meeting. In the aftermath of the settlement, Mullins, state Sen.-elect Brian Wrightson, D-40, Archbald, and state Sen. Katie Muth, D-44, admonished Olyphant for voting away the conditional use hearing process that would have given residents the opportunity to cross-examine the developer’s witnesses and present their own evidence. Muth, whose district is in Southeast Pennsylvania, has emerged as a leading figure in the state’s data center opposition movement over her criticism of the industry and support of a three-year moratorium. She spoke in Lackawanna County in October at a community conversation on data centers hosted at the Mid Valley Secondary Center in Throop. “I’m really terrified about this quote-unquote settlement option,” Muth said Thursday, explaining she immediately reached out to Lackawanna County Commissioner Bill Gaughan when she learned of it. “This is obscene — they can’t settle away people’s due process rights through the conditional use process.” In a statement Wednesday, Wrightson vowed to demand answers and fight for community transparency. “Developers claim they want to be good neighbors, but when residents push back and demand answers, the response is litigation rather than meaningful public engagement. That is not how responsible development should work,” Wrightson said. “Let me be absolutely clear: development decisions that could affect generations of Pennsylvanians must put the interests of residents first, not those of developers or special interest groups.” ERCOR sued Olyphant in June asking a judge to compel the borough and its zoning officer to issue a zoning permit for seven data centers and a substation built within the footprints of four approved 1-million-plus-square-foot warehouses along Marshwood Road and Route 247. Olyphant approved final land development plans for the warehouses in 2022, and ERCOR contended that gave it vested approval to build the data centers under Olyphant’s previous zoning, which did not regulate the industry. Olyphant council voted in April to adopt a zoning amendment regulating and restricting data centers. During Tuesday’s meeting, Solicitor John Brazil said ERCOR’s lawsuit wanted Olyphant’s pre-data-center zoning to apply, which would have no restrictions. “The issue was not whether we were going to get a data center. It was going to be whether or not they had the right to build up there with no restrictions, or they would have to follow our conditional use ordinance,” Brazil said Tuesday. “This lawsuit, in terms of the settlement, requires them to comply with our conditional use ordinance, all of the requirements, and go above and beyond that. If they are successful in the lawsuit, they do not have to comply with any additional requirements, and that was the settlement of the lawsuit.” Both Mullins and Muth called it a “dangerous precedent.” The conditional use process places the burden of proof on developers to make a case with exhibits and experts that they will meet the town’s conditions, Muth said. Agreeing to the conditions under the settlement is not proof, she said. “It’s like you’re giving data centers their red carpet plan — you’re letting the big dog win, and these people should resign if they can’t serve the public and they’re just willing to settle away the rights of the people they represent. They shouldn’t be in office,” Muth said. “It’s disgraceful. They’re literally opening up the door for Pennsylvania — every other municipality — including the ones right next to them.” It is imperative that residents challenge Olyphant over its decision in court, Muth said. “Their rights are being stripped away,” she said. Wrightson also defended the importance of the public hearing process. “Throughout the past year, municipalities across our region have considered data center development proposals through public meetings, giving residents opportunities to ask questions, raise concerns and understand what these projects could mean for their communities,” he said. “By voting 5-2 to approve a settlement involving litigation and bypassing the public hearing process, Olyphant Borough Council has denied residents an important opportunity to participate. People who live, work and raise their families in this community deserve to be heard. They deserve answers about the potential consequences of a development of this magnitude before decisions move forward.” Mullins said the precedent is both concerning and dangerous. “The threat of lawsuits is quite revealing and certainly doesn’t leave the impression of them claiming to be good neighbors,” he said. “Is this how the data center industry plans to proceed and conduct themselves in our hometowns?” Monday Update THEN: Olyphant council voted Tuesday to settle a data center developer’s lawsuit and enter into a community benefits agreement worth $101 million. NOW: Pennsylvania legislators admonish Olyphant officials for ceding the public hearing process under conditional use regulations.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- On Nov. 19, CATL opened its first NING SERVICE Experience Center in Türkiye, establishing a battery repair, sales and training hub in Istanbul for electric-vehicle owners, commercial customers and energy storage operators. Image source: CATL Key Takeaways ·Developed with Ascendum Türkiye, the center covers more than 1,200 square metres and combines battery repair with sales and customer services. ·The facility provides battery testing, diagnostics, repair, maintenance, refurbishment and technical training. ·NING SERVICE operates 1,429 professional service locations across more than 80 countries and regions, according to CATL. Inside the Istanbul center The facility, located in Istanbul's Tuzla district, is Türkiye's first dedicated battery depot repair center and integrated sales-and-service hub, CATL said. Its service areas cover battery testing, diagnostics, repair, maintenance and refurbishment, while the site also includes exhibition and retail space, training rooms and a customer lounge. The exhibition area presents CATL products and systems for electric mobility and energy storage, including battery protection plates, portable power stations and integrated charging-and-storage units. The center will handle products used in passenger and commercial vehicles as well as energy storage systems. Beyond workshop services, NING SERVICE's broader aftermarket offering includes battery recycling, spare-parts logistics and warehousing. The Istanbul facility will also serve as a training and certification base for local technicians, who must complete training under CATL standards before servicing customer batteries. Market context CATL cited Türkiye's National Energy 2040 plan, which targets 20 million electric vehicles and 140 GWh of battery storage capacity by 2040. The projected growth of battery use in transport and energy storage underpins demand for local diagnostic, repair and lifecycle-support services. Local partnership and technical training The center combines CATL's battery technology and service standards with Ascendum Türkiye's local service infrastructure and customer network. CATL said the facility will anchor a nationwide service network supported by CATL-certified engineers. Ascendum Türkiye CEO Tolga Polat said the center is the first business initiative launched under Ascendum Green.Shift. The company plans to develop specialised technical teams and gradually extend its service network across Türkiye. CATL said the partnership is intended to place trained personnel and replacement parts closer to batteries already operating in the local vehicle and energy storage markets, reducing reliance on cross-border support. NING SERVICE's wider network CATL reported that NING SERVICE has more than 9,900 service engineers and over 10,000 technicians certified for new-energy after-sales work. Its overseas network operates a 24-hour response mechanism. The company also operates 95 deep-repair centers. CATL said these facilities can service 76.8% of EV models and cover 90% of battery repair cases. Its Intelligent Eagle Eye System, deployed at more than 150 repair facilities, records repair processes for traceability and quality control. What to watch next NING SERVICE aims to extend its network to 100 countries and regions by 2027 and reach 10,000 service locations worldwide by 2030. In Türkiye, CATL and Ascendum plan to continue building out the service network beyond the Istanbul center and expand local technical capabilities.

artigo.texto: Power plant, data center being eyed for Fayette A new power plant and data center complex is being proposed in Fayette County. EmberClear, a Houston, Texas-based energy infrastructure developer, is pursuing the Dunbar Power Project, which would be built on an 837-acre site in Dunbar Township to the north of the Penn State – Fayette campus. About 137 acres would be used for a 1.4-gigawatt natural-gas fired plant on land owned by the Fay-Penn Business Council. Another 650 acres to the east of it would be set aside for a potential data center project. The sites are zoned for industrial and power generation uses, EmberClear said on its website. The combined-cycle plant would use natural gas and steam power to generate electricity that would be put back onto the grid, said EmberClear chief engineer Jim Palumbo. The electricity generated by the plant would not go to the data center, which would draw its own power from the grid, Palumbo said. Palumbo said to the best of his knowledge, no data center company has been lined up. In a statement on its website, EmberClear touted the existing water, sewer, natural gas and infrastructure nearby, including a gas hub two miles from the site connecting six major pipelines. A final decision on investment is targeted for 2028, with commercial operation slated to begin in the second quarter of 2031, EmberClear said. News of the project surprised Dunbar Township supervisors, who had not known it was in the works until a lunch meeting last Thursday with Bill Decenzo, owner of the proposed data center parcel, and Fayette County Board of Commissioners Chairman Scott Dunn, supervisors said in a Facebook post Monday night. “The township was completely blindsided by it,” said township board Chairman George Stash. “We just are going to have to work together to try to soothe any concerns that there are, and just keep moving forward.” Aside from a stormwater agreement, Stash said, there wouldn’t be any regulatory hurdles at the township level, he said. Both sites are already zoned M-1 (light industrial), Stash said. The data center site had previously been used for industrial purposes like strip mining and a dynamite factory. While some residents have asked the township to pursue legal action, Stash said an expensive fight in court would deplete the township’s resources to the point where it might be unable to provide crucial services. “As long as they meet the requirements within the law, the township would be in a position where it wouldn’t be able to deny anything as long as it meets all requirements,” he said. Pollution and air quality requirements would be handled by the state Department of Environmental Protection and federal Environmental Protection Agency, Stash said. In a statement Tuesday, Dunn said he had not been involved in recruiting EmberClear, and had only heard from the company when it asked about county zoning. Thursday’s lunch meeting had been requested by one of the property owners, he said. “I have no knowledge of any details or site plans of this project,” he said. “What I do know from outside sources is they have applied for a PJM connection to the grid. I have zero knowledge about any specific data center plans. They have not applied for any county permits.” Dunn said county zoning ordinance would require the property to pass inspections and comply with environmental regulations. EmberClear said the project has secured a spot in PJM’s Cycle 1 interconnection queue, and is also going through the air permitting process. On its website, EmberClear said it has lined up an engineering, procurement, and construction contractor and is obtaining equipment for the site. Palumbo said officials from the company would be visiting Fayette County next month, and would be attending an upcoming county board meeting on a proposed data center ordinance. The meeting will take place at 10 a.m. Dec. 11 in the Lafayette Meeting Room at the Gallatin Building, 2 West Main St.

artigo.texto: Amazon planeja adquirir a Decart por cerca de US$ 7,5 bilhões, ameaçando chips de IA para data centers da Nvidia Em 23 de novembro, no horário da Costa Leste dos EUA, a Amazon anunciou a aquisição da tecnologia e equipe da startup israelense Decart por cerca de US$ 7,5 bilhões. A transação visa fortalecer a integração de software do chip Trainium para desafiar o ecossistema CUDA da Nvidia em data centers. Com planos de comercializar externamente seus chips a partir de 2027, a Amazon transita de cliente a concorrente direta. Embora a liderança da Nvidia permaneça sólida no curto prazo, a investida representa um risco estratégico relevante no médio e longo prazo para sua participação de mercado. TradingKey - Amazon desembolsa aproximadamente US$ 7,5 bilhões para adquirir a Decart e reforçar o poder computacional do Trainium, ameaçando potencialmente a dominância da Nvidia em data centers no médio e longo prazo. Em 23 de novembro, no horário da Costa Leste dos EUA, a Amazon (AMZN) anunciou oficialmente planos de desembolsar aproximadamente US$ 7,5 bilhões para adquirir o Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), principal tecnologia de software proprietária da startup israelense de IA Decart, integrando também seus três cofundadores e sua equipe de ponta de P&D composta por cerca de 100 a 120 pessoas. Após o anúncio, as ações da Amazon acumularam alta de mais de 4% considerando o pregão regular e o after-hours. Gráfico do preço das ações da Amazon, Fonte: TradingView A transação da Amazon não apenas estabelece um recorde expressivo para o setor de IA de Israel e para as recentes aquisições de infraestrutura da própria Amazon, mas também é amplamente interpretada por Wall Street e pela indústria de semicondutores como uma peça estratégica fundamental na preparação para vender oficialmente seus chips próprios Trainium ao mercado externo em 2027 e desafiar diretamente a dominância da Nvidia (NVDA) em chips de IA para data centers. Fundada em 2023, a Decart conta com um quadro de acionistas de peso, que inclui Sequoia Capital, Benchmark, Radical Ventures, Nvidia, entre outros. Segundo informações, tanto a Nvidia quanto a Anthropic mantiveram negociações para adquirir a Decart, mas a Anthropic desistiu após o processo de due diligence. No final, foi a Amazon — que vinha colaborando intensamente com a Decart desde 2025 para testar o Trainium3 — que pavimentou o caminho para despontar como rival da Nvidia. Nos últimos anos, o motivo pelo qual a Nvidia conseguiu conquistar mais de 80% de participação de mercado e margens brutas impressionantes no segmento de aceleradores de IA para data centers reside não apenas na liderança de poder computacional de suas arquiteturas de hardware, como Hopper, Blackwell ou Rubin, mas, sobretudo, no fosso defensivo proporcionado pelo ecossistema de software CUDA, construído ao longo de mais de uma década. A aquisição da Decart pela Amazon representa justamente um avanço na integração entre hardware e software voltado para atingir essas defesas do ecossistema da Nvidia. Em primeiro lugar, o valor central do DOS reside na otimização profunda de software em baixo nível e na capacidade de compilação e agendamento entre diferentes plataformas de hardware. Sem comprometer a precisão dos modelos, a solução consegue aliviar significativamente os gargalos de largura de banda de memória e a latência de processamento durante o treinamento e a inferência, permitindo que as cargas de trabalho corporativas de IA migrem com maior fluidez das plataformas de GPUs da Nvidia para os chips Trainium da Amazon, corroendo pela raiz a fidelidade dos usuários ao ecossistema CUDA. Em segundo lugar, o CEO da Amazon, Andy Jassy, planeja vender os chips Trainium diretamente para construtores terceirizados de data centers e grandes clientes corporativos a partir de 2027. Isso significa que a Amazon passará oficialmente de uma grande cliente e opção de locação de infraestrutura em nuvem da Nvidia para uma concorrente direta em hardware de chips e soluções integradas de sistemas. No curto prazo, a posição de liderança da Nvidia não será abalada da noite para o dia — afinal, a empresa acaba de ver a confiança do mercado restabelecida pela reintegração de Jensen Huang, e seus sistemas integrados full-stack e os efeitos de lock-in de clientes continuam muito consolidados. No médio e longo prazo, no entanto, os movimentos estratégicos da Amazon representam uma ameaça potencialmente considerável para a Nvidia. O impacto concreto poderá ser avaliado caso a Amazon consiga assegurar grandes encomendas de laboratórios independentes de IA além da Anthropic, de iniciativas de IA soberana ou de provedores de nuvem de segundo escalão, após o início oficial das vendas externas dos chips Trainium no próximo ano. artigo.texto: New agreement with the UK Battery Industrialisation Centre expands G®CELLS manufacturing development into Europe, following fast-charging battery breakthroughs, Rio Tinto collaboration and initial customer evaluations. DALLAS, Texas, November 23, 2026 – Graphene Manufacturing Group Ltd. (TSXV: GMG) (OTCQX: GMGMF) announced a new milestone in its international battery development strategy, signing an initial service agreement with the UK Battery Industrialisation Centre (UKBIC) in Coventry, England, to manufacture its next-generation G®CELLS Graphene Aluminum-Ion Battery technology. The agreement represents another step toward expanding GMG's battery manufacturing capabilities beyond Australia and advancing the potential commercialization of its ultra-fast-charging graphene batteries for industrial energy storage, automotive applications, mining equipment and other high-performance energy markets. Under the agreement, GMG will develop, manufacture and supply battery materials from its Battery Development Centre in Brisbane, Australia, while UKBIC will manufacture and form the battery cells at its Coventry facility. Initial production activities will focus on pouch-format G®CELLS, establishing an additional manufacturing development pathway in the United Kingdom. Battery Breakthroughs Support Manufacturing Expansion The UK agreement follows GMG's previously announced improvements in its G®CELLS battery technology, developed under a Joint Development Agreement with Rio Tinto, with technical support from the Battery Innovation Center of Indiana. GMG reported several significant performance milestones in October 2026: - 48% increase in battery energy density - 1,000 charge-and-discharge cycles without measurable performance reduction under the reported test conditions - 94% energy efficiency - Six-minute fast charging These results, if replicated at commercial scale, could position GMG's graphene battery technology for applications requiring rapid charging, high power output, extended battery life and reduced equipment downtime. Importantly, GMG also recently announced that it had begun supplying G®CELLS pouch cells to potential customers for early-stage testing and evaluation, marking progress toward commercial validation. Global Expansion Across Europe, Mexico and Asia-Pacific The UK manufacturing agreement adds to GMG's expanding international footprint. Earlier this month, the company announced an exclusive distribution agreement with Brenntag Química, S.A.U., part of Brenntag SE (XETR: BNR), initially covering Spain, Italy and Portugal for its THERMAL-XR®, G® LUBRICANT and G® FLUID graphene products. GMG also established an exclusive distribution arrangement with GrafnoMex for G® LUBRICANT in Mexico, targeting opportunities in automotive manufacturing, transportation and industrial applications. The company's broader portfolio includes G FLUID™ graphene-enhanced coolant for AI data centers, THERMAL-XR® energy-efficiency coatings and G® LUBRICANT, which has demonstrated fuel-consumption reductions of up to 10% in company-reported testing. Commercialization Opportunities Through 2027 GMG previously reported more than 300% year-over-year revenue growth for fiscal 2026 and has expanded its graphene manufacturing capabilities through its Gen 2.0 Graphene Manufacturing Plant in Queensland. The addition of UKBIC to its battery development program provides GMG with another manufacturing development resource as it works to transition G®CELLS from laboratory testing and early customer evaluation toward scalable production. For investors monitoring GMG/GMGMF, the combination of UK battery manufacturing, Rio Tinto collaboration, improving battery performance, international distribution agreements and expanding graphene production capacity represents several potential catalysts heading into 2027. Successful manufacturing validation and customer adoption could strengthen GMG's position in the expanding markets for next-generation batteries, energy storage, advanced materials, AI infrastructure and industrial energy efficiency. However, the initial UKBIC service agreement does not itself establish commercial-scale production or guaranteed customer orders. About Graphene Manufacturing Group Ltd. artigo.texto: Portugal e outros sete Estados-membros defenderam hoje a entrada em vigor, sem novos atrasos, do mercado de carbono europeu sobre emissões de edifícios e transporte rodoviário, numa altura em que vários países contestam a aplicação do mecanismo. Numa carta dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, Wopke Hoekstra, os ministros do Ambiente da Dinamarca, Finlândia, Alemanha, Luxemburgo, Países Baixos, Portugal, Espanha e Suécia manifestam "forte apoio" ao Sistema de Comércio Europeu de Licenças de Emissão 2 (CELE 2). O CELE 2 é um mercado de carbono complementar ao CELE original. Enquanto o CELE original abrange as emissões da produção de eletricidade e de calor, da indústria pesada, da aviação e do transporte marítimo, o CELE 2 incide sobre novos setores, como as emissões criadas pela utilização de combustíveis em edifícios e no transporte rodoviário. Criado em 2023, o CELE 2 tinha entrada em vigor inicialmente prevista para 2028, mas países mais dependentes dos combustíveis fósseis, como a Itália ou a Polónia, têm apelado a que essa data seja adiada ou que o sistema seja aligeirado. Foi perante esta pressão que, na cimeira do Conselho Europeu de Outubro, os líderes da União Europeia (UE) comprometeram-se a avaliar o impacto do CELE 2 antes da sua entrada em vigor em 2028. Na carta hoje dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, que partiu da iniciativa da Dinamarca, os oito ministros frisam que o CELE 2 é hoje "mais importante do que nunca", numa altura em que "a perturbação dos fluxos de energia através do Estreito de Ormuz voltou a expor a vulnerabilidade da Europa". "É evidente que temos de reduzir a nossa dependência dos combustíveis fósseis importados, de modo a diminuir a nossa exposição às tensões geopolíticas e aos choques de preços, que prejudicam a competitividade europeia, afetam negativamente as empresas e as famílias, colocam em risco a nossa segurança energética e nos tornam vulneráveis a pressões políticas", defendem. Os ministros consideram, por isso, que, "ao proporcionar um meio economicamente eficiente de acelerar a descarbonização dos setores dos transportes rodoviários e dos edifícios", o CELE 2 "reforça a segurança energética da Europa, reduzindo a dependência das importações de combustíveis fósseis e promovendo a eletrificação". "O CELE 2 desempenha, assim, um papel fundamental no reforço da resiliência da Europa e da sua autonomia estratégica aberta", insistem. Os ministros recordam ainda que o CELE 2 é "parte integrante de um compromisso mais amplo, que procura alcançar um equilíbrio delicado entre ambição, eficiência em termos de custos e solidariedade". Dirigindo-se ao comissário europeu do Clima, os ministros manifestam-se "disponíveis para trabalhar de forma construtiva com a Comissão", para garantir que o CELE 2 entra em vigor "em conformidade com o calendário já acordado".

artigo.texto: Quercus contesta instalação de centro de dados em Coruche Entre os possíveis impactos, a Quercus aponta riscos para o abastecimento público e para a Paisagem Protegida Local do Açude do Monte da Barca e defende a adoção de medidas que garantam o cumprimento dos limites legais de ruído. A Quercus contestou esta terça-feira a instalação de um centro de dados destinado ao treino de inteligência artificial em Coruche, estimando que a infraestrutura possa consumir o equivalente a 40% a 50% da eletricidade utilizada anualmente no concelho. Num comunicado enviado à Lusa, a Quercus junta-se à oposição ao projeto da Associação de Defesa do Património de Coruche, alertando para as necessidades energéticas e para os potenciais impactos sobre os "recursos hídricos, a paisagem e as populações". Segundo a associação ambientalista, o centro de dados, com uma potência de 6,4 megawatts (MW), deverá ocupar uma parcela de 7.209 metros quadrados no Parque Empresarial do Sorraia e entrar em funcionamento no final de 2027. Promovido pelo fundo de investimento Aura Capital, através da Aura Technologies, o projeto prevê a criação de 30 postos de trabalho, sem especificar se serão diretos ou indiretos, ainda de acordo com a Quercus. Na nota, a associação destaca que a venda do terreno recebeu uma pronúncia favorável da Câmara de Coruche, no distrito de Santarém, que atribuiu "uma bonificação de 40% associada ao alegado contributo para a economia local", além de incentivos fiscais, nomeadamente isenções do Imposto Municipal sobre as Transmissões Onerosas de Imóveis (IMT) e do Imposto Municipal sobre Imóveis (IMI). De acordo com os cálculos apresentados pela associação ambientalista, a infraestrutura poderá consumir cerca de 44,9 gigawatts-hora (GWh) por ano, considerando uma taxa média de utilização de 80%. Ou seja, indica a Quercus, esse consumo corresponderia a cerca de 42% dos 107,9 GWh de eletricidade consumidos no concelho de Coruche em 2024, com base em dados da Pordata. "Caso venha a funcionar continuamente à potência máxima, poderá atingir os 56,1 GWh/ano, cerca de 52% do consumo elétrico anual do concelho", refere a associação, ressalvando que não é ainda conhecido se os 6,4 MW anunciados correspondem à potência elétrica total do centro ou apenas à capacidade computacional instalada. Neste último caso, advertiu, poderão "faltar os consumos dos sistemas de refrigeração, alimentação elétrica e restantes infraestruturas de suporte", elevando as necessidades energéticas da instalação. A associação critica igualmente "a ausência de informação sobre o sistema de arrefecimento previsto", considerando que a utilização de mecanismos baseados na evaporação poderá aumentar a pressão sobre os recursos hídricos da região. Entre os possíveis impactos, a Quercus aponta riscos para o abastecimento público e para a Paisagem Protegida Local do Açude do Monte da Barca e defende a adoção de medidas que garantam o cumprimento dos limites legais de ruído. A Quercus adianta que já pediu à Comunidade Intermunicipal da Lezíria do Tejo, da qual Coruche faz parte, que se pronuncie publicamente contra o projeto, alegando existir uma acumulação excessiva de infraestruturas desta natureza na região. A associação defende ainda que o diploma anunciado pelo Governo para regular a instalação de centros de dados em Portugal deve impor restrições concretas ao consumo de energia e água e sujeitar os novos projetos a uma declaração de impacto ambiental favorável. "Temos sérias dúvidas de que os ganhos socioeconómicos justifiquem o consumo intensivo de energia e de água, a descaracterização da paisagem, a emissão de CO2 ou o ruído causado por estas infraestruturas", afirma Mariana Garanhão, responsável pelo acompanhamento das políticas públicas na Quercus, citada no comunicado. Segundo a Quercus, a Aura Technologies planeia instalar pelo menos outros dois centros de dados em Portugal.

artigo.texto: - Mulilo has secured commercial and financial close for the 77 MW / 308 MWh Leeuwpoort Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) near Carletonville, the first large scale BESS project to reach financial close in Gauteng. - It is the third Mulilo BESS project to close this year, following Mercury and Hartebeesfontein, and will operate under a 15 year power purchase agreement with the National Transmission Company South Africa (NTCSA). - Reatile Group is the strategic empowerment partner, with a local community trust also participating, while Absa, Nedbank and Standard Bank form the lender consortium. Mulilo has announced the successful commercial and financial close of the Leeuwpoort Battery Energy Storage System project, marking a milestone in the delivery of South Africa’s next generation of grid supporting energy infrastructure. Located near Carletonville in the Merafong City Local Municipality, Gauteng, the 77 MW / 308 MWh utility scale facility will connect to the Midas Main Transmission Substation. It is expected to strengthen the resilience and flexibility of the national grid in a strategically important industrial region, where energy demand is shaped by extensive mining activity. As the first large scale battery storage project to reach financial close in the province, Leeuwpoort represents a significant step for Gauteng and for South Africa’s energy transition and grid modernisation. The project was awarded under Bid Window 2 of the Battery Energy Storage Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme (BESIPPPP). It is the third Mulilo BESS project to reach financial close this year, following the Mercury and Hartebeesfontein projects. Leeuwpoort will use the Haohan battery energy storage system supplied by BYD Energy Storage. Once operational, it will provide storage capacity and ancillary services to the transmission system under a 15 year power purchase agreement with NTCSA. Mulilo said the project reflects the strength of its partnership model and its commitment to meaningful participation. Reatile Group is the strategic empowerment partner, while a local community trust will ensure long term community participation and shared socioeconomic benefits. As lead sponsor, Mulilo will also provide construction management, asset management, operations and maintenance oversight, and social impact management services throughout the project’s lifecycle. Mulilo CEO Jan Fourie said: “The financial close of the Leeuwpoort project marks another significant milestone in Mulilo’s commitment to strengthening South Africa’s energy system through utility scale battery energy storage. Projects such as Leeuwpoort play a critical role in enhancing grid stability, unlocking network capacity, and improving energy security. Together with our partners and the support of the South African government, we are proud to deliver lasting value for the country while creating meaningful economic opportunities for local communities.” Sunette Smith, Chief Commercial Officer of Reatile Group, said: “Reatile Group is proud to partner on Leeuwpoort, an important investment in strengthening South Africa’s energy security and enabling the transition to a more resilient and sustainable energy system.” Financial close was made possible by Mulilo’s shareholders, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Norfund, together with close collaboration with Reatile Group, the Department of Electricity and Energy, Eskom, the Independent Power Producers Office, NTCSA and the Merafong City Local Municipality. A lender consortium comprising Absa Bank Limited, Nedbank Limited and Standard Bank of South Africa Limited also backed the project, signalling continued confidence in Mulilo’s development and delivery capability. Key advisers included Arup, Bastion, Bowmans, Deloitte, ENS, Fasken, Marsh and Pepper Tree Capital. Author: Bryan Groenendaal

With these additions, Juniper’s operational portfolio has reached approximately 2.95 GWp of renewable energy capacity and 698 MWh of BESS capacity.

artigo.texto: MaxVolt Energy Industries is expanding its battery technology portfolio with the development of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery packs for electric two-wheelers and plans to introduce 21700-series cells into its battery pack architecture. The company is also undertaking research and development in sodium-ion battery technology following the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). Speaking during the company's H1 FY27 earnings conference call on November 16, 2026, co-founder and chairman Vishal Gupta said MaxVolt is working to introduce LFP chemistry into its two-wheeler battery portfolio, which currently relies predominantly on nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) chemistry. The company is also evaluating the 21700 cell format as an addition to its existing 1865-series cell architecture. Testing is underway as part of its product development programme. The move is intended to expand the range of cell formats available for its battery pack manufacturing operations. MaxVolt Energy evaluates sodium-ion battery technology with DRDO Separately, MaxVolt Energy has signed an MoU with DRDO for work related to sodium-ion battery technology. Co-founder, CEO and CBO Satendra Shukla confirmed during the earnings call that the collaboration is at an initial stage. The company did not disclose the specific research programme or the institute involved in the development work. The management indicated that sodium-ion technology remains a longer-term development area rather than an immediate commercial opportunity. Gupta said sodium-ion batteries currently face challenges relating to energy density and pricing compared with LFP chemistry. The company also indicated that there is currently no significant market demand for sodium-ion battery packs, citing voltage and sizing constraints. The technology remains under testing, with the management suggesting that it could take more than two years before sodium-ion batteries reach a scale at which they can compete more closely with LFP. Battery development across mobility and energy storage MaxVolt's product development activities extend beyond two-wheelers. The company is expanding its three-wheeler battery portfolio, including solutions with capacities of 150Ah and 200Ah, alongside systems of up to 16kW. In the battery energy storage systems (BESS) segment, MaxVolt is developing solutions in the 500-600kWh range, with plans to expand its offering further as additional manufacturing capacity becomes operational. The company currently uses NMC chemistry primarily for two-wheeler applications, while LFP is used across its three-wheeler and energy storage battery segments. Its ongoing development programme also includes improvements to its battery management system (BMS), with a focus on incorporating AI-based capabilities for earlier battery fault diagnosis. MaxVolt is also developing its battery passport system, which is intended to maintain information covering battery manufacturing, servicing and lifecycle status. The system is expected to support battery tracking from deployment through end-of-life management. The technology developments form part of the company's broader effort to expand its battery pack portfolio across electric mobility and energy storage applications.

artigo.texto: The Washington County Chamber of Commerce will host a presentation on December 2 at Hagerstown Community College to discuss the opportunities and challenges associated with data center development as the industry continues to generate discussion throughout the region. Joe Kroboth will lead the presentation, which comes amid growing interest in the possibility of a data center development in Washington County. Kroboth is deputy county administrator for Loudoun County, Virginia, where he oversees community development and public safety services. He previously spent seven years as Washington County’s public works director before serving in Loudoun County for 14 years, giving him firsthand experience with the growth of the data center industry. Paul Frey of the Washington County Chamber of Commerce said the presentation will give residents and business owners an opportunity to learn more about the industry and issues surrounding potential development. “We’ve been talking for the last few weeks about data centers, and specifically maybe one in Washington County, and maybe Hagerstown with an annexation opportunity with the Burkholder and McDade properties,” Frey said. The potential development was also discussed during a recent Hagerstown Mayor and Council meeting, where officials considered annexation and possible regulations that could apply if the properties are developed as a data center. Frey said those discussions are important as local officials consider the infrastructure and other requirements associated with such a project. “If it is a data center, what type of energy are they going to use? Will they have water? What are the setbacks?” Frey said. “And so that’s an important topic here in Washington County and frankly in Maryland.” Maryland Senator Paul Corderman has said in the past, “This whole data center conversation has really become a boogeyman, and has really caused a lot of unnecessary division in my mind, where people just need to look at the merits of what’s what’s happening here and make a decision made on facts, not a decision made on a bunch of fear mongering.” Frey said the issue extends well beyond Washington County, as communities across the country consider the growing demand for data centers and the resources needed to support them. The Chamber’s December 2 presentation will address both the challenges and opportunities associated with the industry. “I encourage folks, if you want to know about data centers, the challenges, the opportunities, come see us December 2,” Frey said. Frey said the presentation will tie into discussions taking place locally, throughout Maryland and across the country as communities consider potential data center developments.

During the evening peak, they supply more than 40% of electricity consumption and charge at an average price around 70 euros per MWh lower than the price at which they sell. Bulgaria is a rather surprising leader in battery storage. Local market conditions have enabled 6,23 GW of battery storage capacity to be put into operation in the country, with the ability to store more than 19 GWh of energy. At least, that is according to the Bulgarian transmission system operator ESO. At the end of May, capacity stood at 3,43 GW. Storage capacity therefore amounts to around 85% of the installed capacity of photovoltaic power plants, which has reached 7,3 GW in the country. artigo.texto: Energy Vault Holdings, Inc., a global energy infrastructure company supporting grid reliability and next-generation AI and high-performance computing infrastructure, has announced the closing of $78 million in construction and bridge financing for the SOSA Energy Center (“SOSA”), its 150 MW / 300 MWh battery energy storage system (“BESS”) in Madison County, Texas. Furthermore, the bridge financing will be repaid with the already committed $80 million preferred equity investment on project completion. Together, the construction financing, the preferred equity investment, and draw on the OIC preferred facility are intended to support SOSA through construction and into commercial operation on a non-recourse basis. Moreover, this project alongside others show how Texas emerges as a leading energy hub in the US. Additionally, SOSA was the first energy storage asset formally acquired and placed into development under Asset Vault. This is the Company’s platform dedicated to owning and operating energy storage and AI infrastructure assets. Once complete, SOSA will operate in the ERCOT North market on a merchant basis. Additionally, it will have the flexibility to enter a contracted offtake agreement as market conditions evolve. Construction Start Date and Key Timelines Construction at SOSA began in the fourth quarter of 2025, with site control and environmental and interconnection milestones in place. Since then, civil work has been completed. Additionally, a substation has been installed, with Energy Vault self-performing engineering, procurement and construction. Also, major equipment is expected on site in the coming months ahead of commercial operation expected in 3Q27. “Storage earns its place in a portfolio the way any infrastructure does, by being financed on its fundamentals,” said Cory Magnuson, President of Asset Vault at Energy Vault. “A bank, a strategic partner and an institutional investor have each backed SOSA on those terms. Furthermore, SOSA Energy Center reinforces our Asset Vault strategy of building projects that generate recurring revenue, robust EBITDA margin. Also, it reinforces long-term operating cash flows.” Lastly, the SOSA Energy Center represents an approximately $100 million investment in Madison County. Also, it is estimated to generate $9.3 million in tax revenue for North Zulch ISD and Madison County over a 10-year period. Moreover, construction is also expected to create 65 jobs in the local community.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- On Nov. 19, CATL opened its first NING SERVICE Experience Center in Türkiye, establishing a battery repair, sales and training hub in Istanbul for electric-vehicle owners, commercial customers and energy storage operators. Image source: CATL Key Takeaways ·Developed with Ascendum Türkiye, the center covers more than 1,200 square metres and combines battery repair with sales and customer services. ·The facility provides battery testing, diagnostics, repair, maintenance, refurbishment and technical training. ·NING SERVICE operates 1,429 professional service locations across more than 80 countries and regions, according to CATL. Inside the Istanbul center The facility, located in Istanbul's Tuzla district, is Türkiye's first dedicated battery depot repair center and integrated sales-and-service hub, CATL said. Its service areas cover battery testing, diagnostics, repair, maintenance and refurbishment, while the site also includes exhibition and retail space, training rooms and a customer lounge. The exhibition area presents CATL products and systems for electric mobility and energy storage, including battery protection plates, portable power stations and integrated charging-and-storage units. The center will handle products used in passenger and commercial vehicles as well as energy storage systems. Beyond workshop services, NING SERVICE's broader aftermarket offering includes battery recycling, spare-parts logistics and warehousing. The Istanbul facility will also serve as a training and certification base for local technicians, who must complete training under CATL standards before servicing customer batteries. Market context CATL cited Türkiye's National Energy 2040 plan, which targets 20 million electric vehicles and 140 GWh of battery storage capacity by 2040. The projected growth of battery use in transport and energy storage underpins demand for local diagnostic, repair and lifecycle-support services. Local partnership and technical training The center combines CATL's battery technology and service standards with Ascendum Türkiye's local service infrastructure and customer network. CATL said the facility will anchor a nationwide service network supported by CATL-certified engineers. Ascendum Türkiye CEO Tolga Polat said the center is the first business initiative launched under Ascendum Green.Shift. The company plans to develop specialised technical teams and gradually extend its service network across Türkiye. CATL said the partnership is intended to place trained personnel and replacement parts closer to batteries already operating in the local vehicle and energy storage markets, reducing reliance on cross-border support. NING SERVICE's wider network CATL reported that NING SERVICE has more than 9,900 service engineers and over 10,000 technicians certified for new-energy after-sales work. Its overseas network operates a 24-hour response mechanism. The company also operates 95 deep-repair centers. CATL said these facilities can service 76.8% of EV models and cover 90% of battery repair cases. Its Intelligent Eagle Eye System, deployed at more than 150 repair facilities, records repair processes for traceability and quality control. What to watch next NING SERVICE aims to extend its network to 100 countries and regions by 2027 and reach 10,000 service locations worldwide by 2030. In Türkiye, CATL and Ascendum plan to continue building out the service network beyond the Istanbul center and expand local technical capabilities.
