artigo.texto: O mercado de créditos de carbono ganhou espaço nas discussões da COP31, com avanços nas regras para comercialização internacional e na estruturação de mecanismos de financiamento voltados à preservação ambiental. Embora as negociações sobre combustíveis fósseis tenham enfrentado impasses e impedido um acordo final mais abrangente, a aprovação do artigo 6 representou um dos principais resultados da conferência nesse campo. O mecanismo permite que a conservação de florestas e a adoção de práticas produtivas sustentáveis também tenham valor econômico. Cada tonelada de dióxido de carbono (CO₂) retirada da atmosfera ou cuja emissão é evitada, por meio da manutenção da vegetação nativa e de sistemas como a agrofloresta cabruca, pode dar origem a um crédito de carbono, negociado para compensar emissões. O cenário entre a COP30 e a COP31 aponta mudanças importantes na governança climática e na destinação de recursos para projetos ambientais. Entre os avanços está a aprovação do comércio internacional de créditos de carbono com base no artigo 6, enquanto outros temas da agenda climática permaneceram sob impasse, especialmente aqueles relacionados aos combustíveis fósseis e à resistência de grandes países produtores. Outro destaque é o desenvolvimento do mercado regulado de carbono no Brasil. De acordo com a Secretaria Extraordinária de Mercado de Carbono, vinculada ao Ministério da Fazenda, o intervalo entre as duas conferências foi marcado pelo avanço na implementação desse sistema e pela consolidação de uma coalizão global voltada à cooperação internacional. Na área de financiamento, o presidente do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), Aloizio Mercadante, mencionou a expectativa de captar aproximadamente 39 bilhões em investimentos destinados a iniciativas climáticas e projetos ambientais. Impactos para reservas ambientais e áreas de cabruca O fortalecimento dos instrumentos de financiamento climático também pode ampliar as oportunidades para proprietários de áreas protegidas, especialmente na Mata Atlântica. Nesse contexto, iniciativas de Pagamento por Serviços Ambientais (PSA) e ações de gestão territorial ganham relevância. A Reservas Votorantim, por exemplo, destaca benefícios associados à conservação de áreas de Mata Atlântica e Cerrado. Além da proteção contra invasões, desmatamentos e incêndios, os proprietários podem contar com suporte técnico e jurídico, isenções no Imposto sobre a Propriedade Territorial Rural (ITR) e participação em iniciativas como o PSA Carbonflor. Para acessar essas possibilidades, entretanto, é necessário que as áreas estejam organizadas do ponto de vista técnico e ambiental. Um exemplo é a Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural (RPPN) Serra dos Teiús, localizada em Ipiaú, no sul da Bahia. Reconhecida como unidade de conservação de interesse público e caráter perpétuo, a reserva possui 1,5649 hectare no bioma Mata Atlântica. Sua criação foi oficializada pela Portaria nº 007, de 29 de janeiro de 2026. Para propriedades com esse perfil, especialmente aquelas que desenvolvem ou têm potencial para sistemas agroflorestais de cabruca, a elaboração de um plano de manejo é uma etapa importante. O documento deve reunir informações sobre as condições ambientais da área, recursos hídricos, medidas de prevenção de ameaças, cronograma de atividades e indicadores de acompanhamento. Além de orientar a administração permanente da reserva, esse planejamento pode facilitar o acesso a programas de conservação e a iniciativas de financiamento climático.

artigo.texto: Base Power, a US-based energy company, has agreed with Cumberland Electric Membership Corporation (Cumberland EMC) to deploy 30 MW of residential battery storage in Tennessee. The batteries are to be installed across the service territory of the cooperative, where they will be linked as a networked fleet. Base is to install and maintain every unit, while Cumberland EMC will decide when the fleet charges and discharges. The cooperative will dispatch that fleet at system peaks in order to reduce demand and to cut its wholesale power costs. For its members, each battery is offered at $695 upfront plus $19 a month, and it can back up a home for up to 36 hours. The program is the first partnership that Base has formed in Tennessee and in the territory of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA). Installations are expected to begin in early 2027, and members can join a waitlist in the meantime. Cumberland EMC and Base Power plan 30 MW of home batteries A 30 MW fleet of home batteries is to be deployed in Tennessee, where Cumberland EMC will dispatch it at system peaks and Base Power will maintain each unit. artigo.texto: Green Energy Storage (GES), an Italy-based maker of flow batteries for stationary storage, has received €10 million (~ $10.92 million) in financing from Intesa Sanpaolo. The bank has arranged it as a structured finance transaction through its Banca dei Territori division, which has worked with its IMI Corporate & Investment Banking division. The funds are to pay for the staff, materials and facilities that GES needs in order to scale up its hydrogen-manganese battery under the IPCEI programme. They are also to let the company run its first large-scale installations under real operating conditions, before the product is certified and industrialised. According to GES, the battery works at room temperature, and its power and energy modules can be sized independently of each other. The company, which is based in Povo in the province of Trento, has set itself the aim of reaching technology readiness level (TRL) 6 by the end of 2026. Intesa Sanpaolo lends €10 million to flow battery maker GES With €10 million from Intesa Sanpaolo, the Trentino SME Green Energy Storage is to scale up its hydrogen-manganese flow battery and to run its first large units. artigo.texto: A Odata Brasil recebeu autorização do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) para comprar uma empresa responsável pelo projeto de implantação do Data Center Anhanguera, localizado em Osasco, São Paulo. O ativo é atualmente controlado pela GP Participações Empresariais e pela Tattva, do grupo BEP Energia. A operação ainda depende do aval de outros órgãos antitruste. Ao Cade, as companhias informaram que o data center ainda não entrou em operação e que ainda não possui capacidade instalada. Atualmente, o data center detém apenas o parecer de acesso emitido pelo Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS), documento necessário para a conexão do empreendimento à Rede Básica do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). Caso a aquisição seja concluída e o projeto entre em operação, a empresa desenvolverá as mesmas atividades já exercidas pela Odata Brasil. Em manifestação ao Cade, a Odata destacou que a operação representa uma oportunidade de negócio alinhada à sua estratégia de desenvolvimento e expansão no mercado de data centers no Brasil. No momento, a companhia é responsável por oferecer colocation a clientes do segmento atacadista, incluindo provedores de nuvem em modelo hyperscale, empresas dos setores financeiro, de telecomunicações e diversas outras áreas com atuação em múltiplos segmentos. No Brasil, a Odata possui data centers nos estados de São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro, além de unidades na Colômbia, Chile e México. Já os vendedores destacaram que a venda pode contribuir para o desenvolvimento de seus negócios.

artigo.texto: Oman BESS Projects are moving through the procurement stage, with bidders receiving additional time to prepare proposals for five standalone battery energy storage facilities. The programme will deliver 950MW of combined power capacity and 3,800MWh of energy storage across five locations. Nama Power & Water Procurement Company (Nama PWP) is overseeing the independent power producer (IPP) tender. The deadline extension gives prospective developers more time to complete their technical and commercial submissions. Meanwhile, the procurement represents a significant investment in Oman’s electricity infrastructure. It will strengthen grid flexibility and support the country’s expanding renewable energy generation capacity. MEED reported the latest bidding extension on November 23, 2026. However, the revised submission deadline and total construction cost have not been publicly confirmed. Oman BESS Projects cover five construction locations The procurement comprises five standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) facilities distributed across four governorates. Together, the installations will provide 950MW of power capacity and 3,800MWh of storage. The largest installation will occupy approximately 149,535 square metres in Sohar, Al Batinah North Governorate. It will deliver 500MW of power capacity and 2,000MWh of storage. Furthermore, the facility will connect to Oman’s electricity grid through a 220kV connection. Four additional installations will provide the remaining 450MW of capacity. The Al Mabellah facility in Muscat Governorate will deliver 100MW and 400MWh of storage. It will connect to the electricity network through a 132kV connection. Similarly, the Ayjah facility in South Al Sharqiyah Governorate will provide 100MW and 400MWh. Its planned grid connection will also operate at 132kV. The Jalan Bani Bu Ali installation will contribute 150MW and 600MWh of storage. Its connection will involve the Sadah and Jalan Bani Bu Ali wind farm substations. Meanwhile, the Sadah facility in Dhofar Governorate will deliver 100MW and 400MWh. It will connect to the Sadah wind farm substations through a 132kV connection. The five installations will collectively provide four hours of storage at their combined rated power capacity. Consequently, they will help balance electricity supply and demand during periods of fluctuating generation. Separately, Oman is advancing a 1GW battery storage development under a $1 billion agreement between Nama Holding and China’s State Grid International Development. The programme covers two 500MW installations at Duqm Industrial Station and Al-Subaikhi Station in Ibri. The Duqm-Ibri BESS project is distinct from Nama PWP’s 950MW procurement, although both initiatives will strengthen grid flexibility and support renewable energy integration. Oman BESS Projects support renewable energy integration The procurement aligns with Oman’s strategy to increase renewable energy generation and strengthen electricity supply security. Nama PWP’s 2026–2032 Power Seven-Year Statement identifies energy storage as an important component of future electricity planning. The company highlights battery storage’s potential to support renewable integration and peak-demand management. According to the statement, renewable sources contributed approximately 9% of Oman’s electricity production in 2025. The country targets increasing this contribution to at least 30% by 2030. Consequently, large-scale storage infrastructure will become increasingly important as additional solar and wind projects enter development. Battery systems can store surplus electricity and release it when renewable generation declines. Meanwhile, Oman’s electricity demand continues to increase. Nama PWP projects peak demand across the Main Interconnected System will rise from 7,863MW in 2025 to 14,147MW by 2032. The five facilities will therefore strengthen the electricity system’s flexibility and capacity management. They will also complement investments in renewable generation and transmission infrastructure. The procurement also comes alongside a separate 1GW battery storage agreement involving Nama Holding and China’s State Grid International Development. Signed in November 2026, that agreement covers two 500MW facilities at Duqm Industrial Station and Al Subaikhi Station. The Oman Investment Authority valued those separate developments at approximately US$1 billion. However, the agreement does not represent the financial value of the five-facility procurement managed by Nama PWP. The five-facility procurement remains at the competitive bidding stage. Nama PWP will proceed with the developer selection process following the submission of proposals. The successful developers will subsequently advance the facilities towards financing, construction and eventual operation.

artigo.texto: Botetourt County says Google data center construction could wind down over next week BOTETOURT COUNTY, Va. (WSET) — Construction activity at Google's proposed data center in Botetourt County could continue for several more days, even after a judge voided the county's agreement with the company. Botetourt County Communications Coordinator Brent Watts says the county learned from its board chair that activity at the site could continue for the next several days, possibly another week. Watts says crews need time to wind down construction and secure equipment already at the site. "They have to wind down construction. They can't just pack up and leave because there's a lot of things that are there that have to be kind of buttoned up," Watts said. The update comes as nearby residents continue looking for answers about what the court ruling means for the project. RELATED: Judge rules Botetourt County Google data center deal violated law, halts construction Courtney Pritt lives about 1,500 feet from the proposed data center site. She says her family thought they had found their forever home, but the project has already brought concerns about noise. "The first time we heard the blasting, I ran outside to get the dogs, who just froze in place, and I took them inside. That was not a great experience," Pritt said. Even after the judge's ruling, Pritt says she noticed activity at the property, including pallets being brought onto the site. She contacted the sheriff's office for answers but says she was directed elsewhere. "I'm just wondering who will be enforcing this?" she asked. Her son, Cooper Pritt, has seen data centers firsthand while training in Leesville. He worries about what the development could mean for the surrounding landscape. "They honestly look like prisons. They're gated- barbed wire fences, just really dark. I feel like this here is a really bright land, and it's just going to drain everything out of it. All of the color, all of the life," Cooper said. ABC13 went to the construction site to ask workers whether construction was still underway. They declined to comment. We also took questions directly to members of the Board of Supervisors. Board member Brandon Nicely said the county is still weighing its options following the judge's decision. "What will you do to make sure you're more transparent with people from now on?" ABC 13 asked. "Well, it's up to our attorneys and all that to make sure we don't get out of line. We felt like we were, so, you know, we acted what we thought was perfectly legal. I think we still have a little bit of... We don't really care for the judgment that much, as anybody would, but we're trying to decide which way we want to go now, so we're going to do our best," Nicely said. But several major questions remain unanswered. ABC13 asked county leaders what will happen to Google's money that has already been spent on capital improvements, whether the county plans to appeal the ruling and what Google's next steps will be. We also asked whether the county plans to hold another vote on the agreement. Board members declined to comment on those questions. For families like the Pritts, the uncertainty continues as they wait to learn what will happen next with the project just down the road from their home. ABC13 will continue following the county's response and Google's next steps.

artigo.texto: Larsen & Toubro (L&T), through two of its verticals, namely its Renewables business and L&T Electronic Products & Systems (LTEPS), has jointly secured a 300 MW/900 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) order. According to an L&T press release, the order is for a BESS project at Khavda in Gujarat, with a three-hour storage duration. The project will have a power capacity of 300 MW and an energy storage capacity of 900 MWh. By storing surplus renewable energy during periods of high generation and releasing it during peak demand, the system will help maximise clean energy utilisation, strengthen grid stability, and enhance the flexibility and reliability of power supply. L&T Uses Liquid-Cooling Technology The advanced BESS solution will incorporate liquid-cooling technology to deliver higher power density, enhanced safety, and a longer operating life. The facility will play a crucial role in improving grid flexibility and enabling greater integration of renewable energy into India's power network. The order further strengthens L&T's position in the energy storage sector and reflects the trust and confidence that clients place in the Company's ability to deliver complex projects at scale. Building L&T's BESS Business Since Larsen & Toubro (L&T) carved out a separate renewable energy vertical within its infrastructure segment in 2024, the company has seen rapid growth in its renewable energy and energy storage businesses. L&T recently secured orders for three Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects from a Middle Eastern client, collectively contributing 6 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of storage capacity. The projects feature four-hour BESS installations, each capable of storing and dispatching energy to support grid stability and renewable energy integration.

https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBM.resumo: A expansão da infraestrutura de data centers no Brasil entrou no centro de uma nova disputa sobre incentivos fiscais, financiamento público e soberania digital. A Coalizão Direitos na Rede (CDR) critica o Projeto de Lei 305/2026, que institui o Programa de Desenvolvimento de Data Centers Regionais (PRODATA BRASIL), por prever benefícios a grandes empreendimentos sem estabelecer garantias suficientes de proteção ambiental, participação das comunidades e desenvolvimento tecnológico nacional. De autoria do deputado federal Duda Ramos (PODE/RR), o projeto prevê incentivos tributários para a instalação de data centers nas regiões Norte e Nordeste, prioridade no acesso a financiamentos do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) e da Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep), além de garantias ao capital estrangeiro. Para a CDR, a proposta repete problemas identificados na mobilização contra o REDATA (PL 278/2026), que também previa incentivos fiscais para o setor sem estabelecer previamente salvaguardas socioambientais e mecanismos para assegurar a soberania digital brasileira. A entidade não se opõe à expansão da infraestrutura digital, mas questiona o modelo de atração de investimentos baseado em benefícios ao setor privado sem contrapartidas que garantam retorno econômico, tecnológico e social ao país. "Não somos contra o desenvolvimento tecnológico nem contra investimentos em infraestrutura digital. Somos contra um modelo que oferece benefícios ao setor privado antes de garantir direitos, proteger os territórios e assegurar que a riqueza e o conhecimento gerados permaneçam no Brasil", afirma André Fernandes, fundador e integrante da diretoria do IP.rec (Instituto de Pesquisa em Direito e Tecnologia do Recife), entidade integrante da CDR. Demanda por energia e água entra no debate Um dos principais pontos de preocupação envolve o impacto ambiental dos empreendimentos. Data centers demandam grandes volumes de energia e água e ocupam extensas áreas territoriais. Na avaliação da Coalizão, a disputa entre estados para atrair esses investimentos pode resultar em renúncias fiscais, oferta de terrenos, infraestrutura dedicada, prioridade de acesso à rede elétrica e flexibilização de exigências. A entidade também questiona a capacidade de geração de benefícios econômicos de longo prazo. A instalação física de servidores, argumenta a CDR, não assegura a criação de empregos duradouros, o desenvolvimento de tecnologia nacional, a realização de pesquisas científicas ou a formação de um ecossistema local de inovação. O projeto prevê diretrizes de sustentabilidade, como utilização de fontes renováveis, redução do consumo de água e gestão de resíduos. Para a Coalizão, entretanto, essas medidas não substituem avaliações de impactos cumulativos, licenciamento ambiental adequado e participação efetiva das comunidades afetadas, incluindo consulta prévia, livre e informada aos povos indígenas, quando aplicável. Outro questionamento diz respeito à ausência de critérios detalhados para enquadramento dos empreendimentos, monitoramento, transparência e avaliação dos resultados. Esses aspectos, segundo a entidade, ficam para regulamentação posterior. A CDR cobra do Congresso Nacional a realização de um debate público e a definição de contrapartidas concretas antes do avanço do PL 305/2026. Para a organização, a política de expansão dos data centers precisa considerar não apenas a capacidade de atrair infraestrutura e capital estrangeiro, mas também o controle dos recursos estratégicos, a proteção dos territórios e a geração de conhecimento e tecnologia no Brasil.

artigo.texto: Por que os data centers de IA fazem tanto barulho? Veja vídeo Qual o som da inteligência artificial? Ou melhor, o som de um centro de dados de IA? Esse é um dos motivos pelos quais praticamente ninguém quer ter um desses data centers como vizinho. Mas o Brasil já concentra quase metade de todos os data centers da América Latina, e até 2030 esse mercado deve dobrar de tamanho. Então, cada vez mais brasileiros terão um deles como vizinho. Mas voltando ao barulho, de onde ele vem? Os centros de dados abrigam milhares de computadores. E, assim como o seu laptop, esses computadores esquentam quando estão trabalhando muito. Isso acontece porque, dentro dos computadores, existem pequenos chips que realizam incontáveis cálculos a cada segundo para manter a internet funcionando, transmitir vídeos e alimentar sistemas de IA. À medida que a eletricidade passa pelos chips, uma pequena parte dessa energia é convertida em calor a cada cálculo realizado. artigo.texto: The Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh Limited (APTRANSCO) has invited bids for setting up 1,000 MW/4,000 MWh of standalone battery energy storage systems (BESS) across selected substations in Andhra Pradesh. Interested developers can submit their bids until December 14, 2026, at 5 PM, while the bid opening is scheduled for December 17. The projects will be developed under the Build, Own and Operate (BOO) model and will be used to meet power storage requirements on demand. The tender covers two separate components, comprising 500 MW/2,000 MWh of BESS capacity supported through Viability Gap Funding (VGF) under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF), and another 500 MW/2,000 MWh without VGF support. The procurement will follow a tariff-based competitive bidding process. Tender Details And Bid Timeline According to the tender notice, listed as APTRANSCO/BESS/Phase-II/2026-27, the bidding process was published on November 19, 2026. A pre-bid meeting has been scheduled for December 2, 2026, at 11 AM. The tender fee has been set at ₹59,000. The estimated project value and earnest money deposit (EMD) have not been specified in the tender listing. The projects will be established at selected APTRANSCO substations, with the storage systems intended for on-demand utilisation. VGF And Non-VGF Routes For Storage Development The division between VGF-supported and non-VGF-supported capacity provides two procurement routes for BESS developers. While 500 MW of the proposed capacity will receive financial support through PSDF, the remaining 500 MW will be developed without VGF assistance. The tender adds to Andhra Pradesh's efforts to expand grid-scale energy storage infrastructure, as battery storage becomes increasingly important for managing renewable power integration and electricity demand.

artigo.texto: Contemporary Amperex Technology stock: CATL targets 13,000 trucks Published on 11/23/2026 at 10:45 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS Commercial vehicle expansion - CATL's initial commercial agreements cover 13,000 heavy freight trucks across 14 Chinese logistics companies. - The 1+X system combines a swappable chassis battery with a 77-kilowatt-hour auxiliary pack. - CATL plans 900 QIJI exchange stations by December 31, 2026, and 2,000 through 2027. Contemporary Amperex Technology detailed the deployment of a dual-battery system for heavy electric trucks on November 18, according to East Asia Brief. Initial commercial agreements cover 13,000 vehicles with 14 Chinese freight companies, including China Post Group and SF Holding. Battery system targets freight The 1+X architecture pairs a swappable chassis battery with a fixed 77-kilowatt-hour auxiliary pack behind the cab. The chassis formats provide 432 or 513 kilowatt-hours, while the reserve unit supports direct-current charging at up to 3C. CATL says the layout can raise usable depth of discharge from roughly 70% to more than 95%. The system is designed to keep trucks moving when the main pack is empty, with the vehicle controller switching to the auxiliary battery within milliseconds. Swapping network expands The company plans 900 QIJI exchange stations across domestic freight routes by December 31, 2026, and 2,000 operational stations through 2027. The next-generation stations are designed to replace chassis packs in five minutes. For a truck traveling 400 kilometers a day, CATL projects annual energy savings of about 130,000 yuan against a diesel equivalent. The source also reports projected three-year operating-cost savings of more than 460,000 yuan, although those figures are company projections. artigo.texto: This story was originally published by Capital B News in partnership with the Pulitzer Center’s AI Accountability Network, and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration. By the time Zakiya Mabery learned that a $2 billion data center was planned just a 10-minute walk from her house, officials had already approved it. The 200-acre facility in Augusta, Georgia, was first authorized in 2022 without a public hearing that would’ve allowed the community to voice their concerns. Just months before the facility known as Project Eisenhower came to be, Mabery bought her home in a new housing development called Hayne’s Station. Since then, two-thirds of the people who’ve moved into the community have been Black. “We would’ve never purchased a house if we knew a data center was coming,” she said about the project that began construction earlier this year. Mabery’s experience exposes the racial divide in America’s data center boom—not just in where facilities are built, but in who gets a chance to question them. Majority-Black communities are more than two times more likely to host a data center than majority-white ones and far less likely to receive the chance to hear about the projects before they’re approved or offer their opinion through public comment. “It seems like [processes] are being built to silence citizens,” Mabery said at an Augusta Planning Commission meeting this past summer. In recent years, dozens of AI data centers in communities home to hundreds of thousands of Americans have been approved without a public hearing. For Black communities, the data center boom is extending a familiar pattern of environmental racism that has plagued families for generations. Black communities are hosting infrastructure that generates wealth elsewhere. Meanwhile, they live with the pollution and disinvestment that undermines economic opportunity and contributes to poor health outcomes and premature deaths in their neighborhoods. The stakes are growing as tech companies pour hundreds of billions of dollars into new infrastructure. President Donald Trump has pulled the levers of government in favor of these companies as he’s cast AI dominance as a competition the United States cannot afford to lose to China. His administration has ordered agencies to exempt data centers projects from federal environmental review and to revise federal rules to accelerate their construction. At the same time, he has pushed federal agencies to limit the opportunities for public comment as the building boom reaches communities already carrying generations of industrial burdens. The opportunity for residents to speak their mind is consequential to the outcome of a data center project. On average, communities that have received a hearing before construction are nearly 80 percent white on average. Those without one are roughly 60 percent people of color. When communities have received a public hearing, data centers have been blocked 66 percent of the time. When they don’t, they’re approved 80 percent of the time, according to Zoned Out, a tool created by researchers at Harvard University. “We know disparities already exist in our communities, and now in the case of data centers, we’re seeing the targeting that happens without any say. It is systemic injustice,” said Aino Halonen, a former AI worker who led the Harvard study. The racial disparities showed up during November’s midterm election. More than 40 jurisdictions nationwide allowed voters to decide if they wanted data centers in their communities via ballot measures. White residents made up an average of over 83 percent of the population in these places, compared with less than 5 percent for Black residents. In Georgia, Mabery and her neighbors want a voice in what happens to their homes, health, and finances. Data centers have increased PM 2.5 air pollution, which Black Americans die from at the highest rate in the US. The pollution can penetrate deep into the lungs and bloodstream, causing respiratory and cardiovascular disease. It is linked to asthma attacks, strokes, dementia, and cancer. Carbon emissions from data centers are also connected to the intensification of climate change. America’s largest data centers are responsible for an estimated 25.7 million metric tons of climate change-causing carbon dioxide emissions annually—more than emissions from entire countries like Kenya and Guatemala. “These are not emotional concerns. This is where we live. We invested here. We live and bear the impact here,” Augusta resident Charles Zabel said about the data center. “We ought to have a voice in this. So far, we have not had a meaningful voice in this discussion. Representation does not mean protecting a project. Representation means protecting the people who already call this place home.” Researchers at George Washington University Law School joined American University researchers to analyze the placement of more than 5,200 data centers in the US, finding the major racial divide in where they’re found. The researchers accounted for income, population density, home values, and proximity to major power lines, and compared neighborhoods within the same state to test whether economics or geography explained the racial disparities in where data centers were located and the benefits the communities received. Even after those adjustments, neighborhoods with larger Black, Latino, and Asian populations remained most likely to have these negative experiences with data centers. “Even when you control for all of that, race stands out,” said Dhanaraj Thakur, director of the Fair Technology Initiative at George Washington University. “I think it’s important to show that this is not some anecdotal thing that’s happening in a few cities like Memphis or elsewhere,” he added. “It’s actually happening across the country.” The difference often comes down to zoning. artigo.texto: 24 horas com o VERDADEIRO PREMIUM da Motorola! PRIMEIRAS IMPRESSÕES do Motorola Signature 27! O TecMundo testou por um dia inteiro em primeira mão o novo Motorola Signature 27 no Rio de Janeiro!. Após diversos rumores e vazamentos, a Motorola enfim anunciou a chegada do Motorola Edge 70 Neo, seu novo smartphone intermediário da série 70. O modelo traz um conjunto de especificações até bem competente, como uma câmera primária de 50 megapixels e uma bateria de 7.000 mAh. O grande destaque desse lançamento da Motorola é justamente essa bateria mais parruda, que se tornou tendência entre os aparelhos intermediários de diversas fabricantes. Esse modelo ostenta os 7.000 mAh e oferece capacidade suficiente para pelo menos dois dias de uso contínuo, além da compatibilidade com carregamento de 45W. No quesito das câmeras, o conjunto também não decepciona e a companhia entrega uma ilha traseira com sensor primário de 50 MP por meio do sensor Sony LYTIA 710 (f/1.8). Ao lado desse componente, foi inserido um pequeno sensor macro de dois megapixels para fotografar objetos muito próximos. A câmera frontal tem 32 MP para as selfies. Tela, processador e disponibilidade As demais especificações do Motorola Edge 70 Neo ainda são interessantes, pois a companhia montou esse smartphone com uma tela bem grande de 6,8 polegadas. Esse display funciona por meio de um painel Extreme AMOLED na resolução de 2.772 x 1.272 pixels, com taxa de atualização de 144 Hz e brilho máximo de 5.200 nits. Já na parte mais interna, quem comanda todas as operações do celular é o Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, uma plataforma lançada pela Qualcomm em meados de 2024 para smartphones intermediários. Para completar o trio dessas especificações, há opções únicas de 8 GB de memória e 128 GB de armazenamento, expansível até 1 TB via cartão microSD. - O modelo da Motorola chega com Android 16 de fábrica e a companhia promete três anos de atualizações do sistema operacional e cinco anos de updates de segurança; - Há proteção Corning Gorilla Glass 7i no vidro e durabilidade militar MIL-STD-810H; - Ele será vendido nas cores Pantone Gray Lilac, Milky Blue, Mountain View e Sage. Por enquanto, o Motorola Edge 70 Neo estará disponível apenas na Índia por 34.999 rúpias indianas (cerca de R$ 2.200 em conversão direta). Ainda não há informações sobre o lançamento para outros países. Ficha técnica Já que o assunto é celular, a versão beta da One UI 9.5 trouxe novidades como o App Lock, Tap to Share e mais opções de personalização. artigo.texto: Novo sistema de comércio de emissões deve aumentar a demanda por créditos de carbono e atrair investidores para projetos ambientais FOTO: Magnific ECONOMIA VERDE Regulamentação do mercado de carbono pode ampliar investimentos no Brasil a partir de 2027 Por Redação A regulamentação do mercado de carbono no Brasil pode abrir uma nova frente de investimentos e ampliar a participação do país no setor de ativos ambientais. Com a criação do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE), instituído pela Lei nº 15.042/2024, o país avança na estruturação de um mercado regulado, que funcionará paralelamente às negociações voluntárias já existentes. O modelo prevê a inclusão gradual de 16 setores econômicos até 2031, quando o sistema deverá estar plenamente operacional. Empresas que ultrapassarem 25 mil toneladas anuais de emissões de dióxido de carbono equivalente estarão sujeitas a limites de emissão e poderão precisar adquirir cotas para compensar os volumes excedentes. Entre os segmentos previstos para as primeiras etapas estão alumínio, siderurgia, cimento, petróleo e gás natural, papel e celulose e vidro. A expectativa é que a regulamentação amplie a demanda por créditos ambientais e crie oportunidades para empresas, gestores de recursos e fundos de investimento. O sistema será baseado no mecanismo conhecido como cap and trade, pelo qual o governo estabelece limites de emissões e permite a negociação de cotas. Empresas que emitirem abaixo do teto poderão comercializar seus excedentes, enquanto aquelas que ultrapassarem o limite precisarão adquirir permissões adicionais. Mercado pode ampliar demanda por créditos Estudo da ICC Brasil e da consultoria WayCarbon aponta que o Brasil acumula 148 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono em créditos gerados, com potencial de expansão da demanda de até 530% com a implantação do mercado regulado. Atualmente, o mercado voluntário funciona por meio de contratos entre empresas interessadas em compensar emissões e responsáveis por projetos ambientais, principalmente nas áreas de conservação florestal, reflorestamento e energia. A regulamentação deve ampliar as possibilidades de negociação e conferir maior liquidez aos ativos. A entrada de empresas obrigadas a cumprir metas ambientais também tende a aumentar a procura por esses ativos, hoje adquiridos principalmente por companhias que assumem compromissos voluntários de redução ou compensação de emissões. Investidores acompanham novas oportunidades A regulamentação também estabelece condições para ampliar a presença dos créditos de carbono no mercado financeiro. A Lei nº 15.042/2024 prevê que esses ativos, quando negociados no mercado financeiro e de capitais, sejam considerados valores mobiliários, sujeitos à supervisão da Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM). Fundos de investimento, incluindo os Fundos de Investimento nas Cadeias Produtivas Agroindustriais (Fiagros), estão entre os veículos com potencial para direcionar recursos a projetos ambientais. Apesar das perspectivas de crescimento, especialistas alertam para os riscos envolvidos. Créditos vinculados a projetos ainda em desenvolvimento apresentam maior incerteza, enquanto ativos já certificados oferecem maior previsibilidade, embora possam ter preços mais elevados. O avanço do setor dependerá da definição de regras, da segurança jurídica e da capacidade de atrair compradores e investidores para um mercado sujeito a oscilações de preços e demanda. O cronograma oficial prevê o início das obrigações de relato de emissões em 2027, com a implementação gradual das demais exigências. A negociação plena de cotas está prevista para começar a partir de 2030, com consolidação do sistema em 2031. Na avaliação de especialistas, o novo modelo poderá posicionar o Brasil entre os principais mercados de carbono do mundo, aproveitando o potencial nacional de geração de créditos e atraindo investimentos para iniciativas de descarbonização.

artigo.texto: By Pexcel John Bacon, Reporter THE Philippines should establish transparent carbon market rules and involve workers and affected communities in policymaking to attract private investments while ensuring a fair transition to a low-carbon economy, the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) said. “If you want the private sector or others to invest in carbon pricing and projects, you need to have a credible and transparent institutions,” IISD Energy Program Director Philip Gass told a joint hearing of the House Committee on Climate Change and the Committee on Sustainable Development Goals on Tuesday. Mr. Gass also urged lawmakers to get communities and workers involved in designing carbon pricing policies, saying their participation would strengthen public support for the system. He said the Philippines could build on existing laws and institutions to develop its carbon pricing system, starting with emissions reporting before introducing a price on carbon. “Report first, apply a price later,” he said, adding that companies and regulators would need time to establish reliable monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) systems. Mr. Gass said MRV standards should be harmonized to the size of emitters. He also raised the need for transparent rules to ensure that carbon credits represent actual and verifiable emissions reductions. Domestic carbon pricing could help the government mobilize funding for climate programs as international climate finance faces growing constraints, he said. “The international system is strained and international climate finance is under stress,” he said. Carbon pricing revenues could be directed toward climate mitigation, adaptation and resilience programs, while also helping cushion households and businesses from the effects of higher energy costs, he added. IISD Senior Policy Advisor Mary Grace Gabis-Reyes said emissions trading systems covered about 25% of global greenhouse gas emissions and generated a record $80 billion in revenues in 2025. Ms. Reyes cited developments in Asian carbon markets, including Japan’s move toward a mandatory emissions trading system and Vietnam’s pilot emissions trading system. In the Philippines, she noted the government has taken steps to develop its carbon market through the adoption of a voluntary forest carbon market roadmap in February, an agreement with Singapore under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement in April, the submission of its third National Determined Contribution (NDC) in September, and the issuance of Executive Order No. 127 in October. The country’s third NDC retained its target to reduce and avoid 75% of projected greenhouse gas emissions from 2025 to 2035, with the unconditional component raised to 7% from 2.71%, Ms. Reyes said. IISD Lead for Carbon Pricing and Philippine Energy Transition Francesse Joy Cordon-Navarro said carbon projects should include clear safeguards for communities, particularly Indigenous Peoples whose ancestral domains may be affected. “Free, prior and informed consent must be explicit and meaningful, and it must take place early on rather than after the principal terms have already been set,” Ms. Navarro said. She said benefit-sharing agreements should specify who is eligible to receive benefits, how much they would receive and when, as well as the remedies available if project developers fail to meet their commitments. IISD Senior Policy Advisor Lorelei S. Astrera said the shift could also affect household energy and transport costs, local businesses and access to essential services. “National gains can exist alongside concentrated local losses,” Ms. Astrera said, calling for policies that anticipate the effects of the transition, protect vulnerable households and give affected groups a voice in decisions on how carbon revenues are spent.

artigo.texto: Vigo County commissioners respond to Sandcut battery storage concerns as project heads to zoning board VIGO COUNTY, Ind. (WTHI) — Vigo County commissioners say they have questioned the developer of a proposed battery storage facility near Sandcut about water, fire safety and the project’s impact on neighbors as the proposal heads toward another public hearing. Commissioners Mark Clinkenbeard and Chris Switzer spoke with News 10 after a commissioners meeting where representatives from NextEra Energy Resources answered questions about Sandcut Storage. Their comments follow a Vigo County Council meeting where residents criticized the way they learned about the proposal and how local officials handled the zoning process. The two commissioners defended that process and said the county’s earlier vote approved rules for battery storage facilities, not the Sandcut project itself. A separate decision on the proposed facility is expected to come before the Area Board of Zoning Appeals. “Now, this particular project will move forward to the BZA, and they will give it an up or down,” Clinkenbeard said. “They may request some more time to get some more answers. I’m not sure.” A hearing on the petition was previously scheduled for Dec. 9 at 10 a.m. at the Vigo County Annex Building. Clinkenbeard encouraged residents to attend. The board could seek additional information rather than make an immediate decision. What’s being proposed? NextEra is proposing a battery energy storage system, or BESS, in the Sandcut area of northern Vigo County. A battery storage facility takes in electricity, stores it and sends it back to the grid later. It does not generate electricity from fuel. The company lists a planned capacity of up to 350 megawatts. That figure describes how quickly the facility could deliver power, not how much energy it could store or how long it could operate at full output. On its Sandcut Storage project page, NextEra estimates a $414 million investment and about 175 construction jobs. The company says the figures are estimates and subject to change, and that the project remains subject to necessary permits and approvals. Clinkenbeard said he believes stored electricity could benefit the local area, though he said the company could not discuss potential contracts. The specific customers and destination of electricity from the project have not been confirmed. Commissioners say they brought community questions to NextEra Switzer said commissioners invited NextEra representatives to address questions they had been receiving from residents. “We just asked a lot of questions that the community’s been asking us for, you know, a couple weeks now,” Switzer said. He said he had hoped more Sandcut residents would attend the commissioners meeting and have an opportunity to hear from the company directly. “We were hoping specifically a few people would be there that’s asked some really tough questions so they could get addressed and kind of have some conversation with NextEra in person,” Switzer said. Clinkenbeard said commissioners spent about half an hour asking questions and encouraged residents to attend the upcoming zoning board hearing. “We invite people to come to that meeting,” he said. “People can come and get some more information.” In News 10’s earlier reporting, several residents said they learned about the proposal from neighbors or social media and wanted more information about its potential effect on their community. “I felt like that we should have known about this and been aware,” longtime Sandcut landowner Mary Vandevender told News 10. She said she had attended a meeting but felt her questions had not been answered. “I’m not going to be okay with this,” Vandevender said. “I’m worried about my land, and I’m worried about my water.” Dustin Houser, who said he learned about the proposal through social media, questioned whether emergency responders would be prepared in the event of a disaster. “My initial concerns are the dangers of this system and that if there’s a disaster, are we prepared for it?” Houser said. Water and fire safety questions Both commissioners said water and fire response were among the subjects they discussed with the developer. Clinkenbeard said he also spoke with Soil and Water about potential water concerns. “We also just had a meeting with Soil and Water, Brendan Kearns, to talk about potential water issues,” Clinkenbeard said. “This facility will not use any water.” Distance from neighbors and screening Clinkenbeard said the developer plans to move the facility farther back from adjoining property owners. He also said vegetation is planned around the site, and commissioners would like to see an additional visual barrier. “They’re going to do, you know, vegetation around the facility, but we would also possibly like to see a berm put around there so that, you know, it’s not visible,” he said. Clinkenbeard also said commissioners asked whether the developer had reached out to nearby property owners about possible land-use agreements. “And they are working on that,” he said. He did not describe the terms of any agreement. Clinkenbeard said the county is trying to balance a landowner’s ability to use their property with the concerns of people living nearby. “We take that all into consideration, because it is important and we want everyone to feel safe,” he said. What the county has — and hasn’t — approved On Nov. 10, commissioners voted 2-1 to approve a countywide zoning change addressing battery storage systems. Switzer and Clinkenbeard voted in favor; Commissioner Mike Morris voted against it. The amendment allows battery storage to be considered as a special exception in specified agricultural, commercial and industrial zoning districts. A special exception requires a separate review. Some 67 GWh of new projects had qualified for the round, and about 43 GWh of them were offered, which was nearly three times the volume that was needed. The weighted average clearing price was €11,382/MWh-year, which was well below the reserve premium of €27,000/MWh-year and 12% lower than the average of the 2028 auction. South and Calabria have received the largest share, at 9.6 GWh, while Sicily has been given 3 GWh, Central-South 2.8 GWh and Sardinia about 0.5 GWh. Under the method that is used, storage is bought only while the marginal cost of new capacity remains below the saving that it brings in gas-fired generation. artigo.texto: Mercado global de painéis de fusíveis: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de painéis de fusíveis até 2035: crescimento impulsionado pela disponibilidade de data centers e pela modernização da rede elétrica Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Painéis de Fusíveis, o mercado chega a 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compras mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de painéis de fusíveis entra no período de previsão 2026-2035 como um segmento maduro, mas estrategicamente vital, do ecossistema de distribuição e proteção elétrica. Os painéis de fusíveis, definidos aqui como quadros de controle e distribuição montados que abrigam fusíveis, disjuntores, barras coletoras e dispositivos de monitoramento, seguem essenciais para proteger circuitos elétricos em ambientes industriais, comerciais e de infraestrutura. A trajetória do mercado é moldada menos pela nova construção residencial, onde os quadros de disjuntores dominam, e mais pela demanda de reposição em uma vasta base instalada, pelas exigências industriais especializadas de proteção de atuação rápida e pela rápida expansão de data centers e de conexões de energia renovável. À medida que a eletrificação avança e os operadores de rede investem em modernização, espera-se que cresça a demanda por painéis de distribuição de baixa tensão, painéis de média tensão, centros de controle de motores e sistemas de invólucros modulares. Ao mesmo tempo, a volatilidade das matérias-primas, a transição para painéis com monitoramento inteligente e as mudanças regulatórias em segurança e eficiência energética influenciarão a dinâmica competitiva. Este relatório oferece uma visão baseada em dados do tamanho, da estrutura e das tendências do mercado a partir de 2026, projetando a evolução até 2035 para fabricantes, distribuidores, investidores e consultores que buscam uma definição analítica transparente do escopo do produto e uma previsão consistente dos vetores de demanda e das restrições de oferta. O cenário-base para o mercado mundial de painéis de fusíveis prevê uma expansão moderada, porém constante, até 2035, com o valor global de mercado crescendo a uma taxa composta de crescimento anual de aproximadamente 4,2% entre 2026 e 2035. Essa projeção pressupõe a continuidade dos gastos de capital em data centers, na modernização das redes elétricas e na automação industrial, além de uma demanda de reposição sustentada nos mercados maduros. O crescimento em volume será mais modesto que o crescimento em valor, refletindo uma mudança de mix para conjuntos de maior valor agregado, como painéis com monitoramento inteligente, painéis de média tensão e soluções sob medida. Regionalmente, a Ásia-Pacífico continuará sendo o maior e mais dinâmico mercado, sustentado por investimentos em infraestrutura e pela expansão da indústria, enquanto a América do Norte e a Europa registrarão atividade constante de reposição e modernização. A América Latina e o Oriente Médio e África oferecerão oportunidades seletivas ligadas a projetos de infraestrutura elétrica. As principais incertezas incluem o ritmo das mudanças nas taxas de juros que afetam a construção, a volatilidade dos preços do cobre e do aço e a velocidade de adoção dos recursos de monitoramento digital. O índice de mercado, fixado em 100 em 2025, deve chegar a aproximadamente 151 em 2035, o que evidencia um crescimento acumulado sem implicar um ciclo de expansão acelerada. A dinâmica competitiva favorecerá fabricantes e integradores capazes de combinar ofertas modulares padronizadas com capacidades de engenharia e serviços, à medida que os clientes buscam cada vez mais soluções integradas de distribuição de energia em vez de componentes isolados. artigo.texto: Computational modeling based on first-principles density functional theory reveals that decorating a tungsten diselenide monolayer with nickel atoms substantially boosts its energy-storage and thermoelectric capabilities. Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides have attracted ongoing interest for these applications due to their high surface-to-volume ratios and tunable electronic configurations. The structural and electronic modeling showed that selenium vacancies within the tungsten diselenide lattice serve as favorable anchoring positions for nickel adatoms. This site preference facilitates robust nickel-to-substrate interactions that bolster overall structural stability. These simulations confirmed both the dynamical and thermal stability of the optimized nickel-decorated framework under modeled conditions. Further electronic-structure and charge-density evaluations demonstrated considerable hybridization between nickel 3d orbitals and the surrounding tungsten and selenium states, creating pronounced local charge redistribution directly around the active nickel sites. Adsorption calculations for both lithium ions and sodium ions revealed favorable binding energies across the modified surface. Furthermore, the integration of nickel adatoms substantially elevated the material’s quantum capacitance across a wide span of gate voltages and operating temperatures, highlighting a markedly improved theoretical charge-storage capacity compared to unmodified monolayers. In addition to electrochemical storage benefits, the researchers modeled the monolayer’s thermoelectric behavior through coordinated electronic and phonon band engineering. The calculations predicted a notable thermoelectric power factor of approximately 1.50 mW m⁻¹ K⁻² alongside a peak dimensionless figure of merit of roughly 0.80 at a temperature of 700 Kelvin. artigo.texto: Prefeitura afirma que não há projeto de data center em análise em Atibaia Administração municipal diz que foi consultada informalmente sobre possível empreendimento, mas afirma que não recebeu nenhum pedido formal de implantação ou licenciamento ambiental Foto: Ilustrativa/Magnific A Prefeitura de Atibaia esclareceu que não existe, até o momento, nenhum projeto formalmente protocolado para a implantação de um data center no município. O assunto ganhou repercussão nas redes sociais e passou a gerar questionamentos de moradores e da imprensa sobre os possíveis impactos ambientais e estruturais de um empreendimento desse porte. ✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do Portal Atibaia News Em nota, a Administração Municipal afirmou que não há processo em andamento, análise técnica ou procedimento de licenciamento ambiental relacionado à instalação de um data center na cidade. A Prefeitura também confirmou que, no passado, foi procurada informalmente para uma conversa de caráter consultivo sobre uma possível iniciativa no setor. Segundo o município, o encontro não representou compromisso, negociação formal ou autorização para a implantação de qualquer empreendimento. A Administração destacou que Atibaia tem atraído o interesse de empresas e investidores de diferentes setores, especialmente por sua localização estratégica, próxima ao entroncamento de duas importantes rodovias do Estado de São Paulo, além do desenvolvimento nas áreas de tecnologia e economia. A Prefeitura ressaltou ainda que, caso uma proposta de instalação de data center seja formalmente apresentada, ela deverá passar pelos procedimentos legais e pelas análises dos órgãos competentes. Entre as etapas previstas está a apreciação do Conselho Municipal de Defesa do Meio Ambiente de Atibaia (COMDEMA), dentro de suas atribuições, além do cumprimento das exigências de licenciamento e autorização nas esferas municipal, estadual e federal. - Acompanhe o Portal Atibaia News para mais informações de Atibaia e região.

artigo.texto: Portugal e outros sete Estados-membros defenderam esta segunda-feira a entrada em vigor, sem novos atrasos, do mercado de carbono europeu sobre emissões de edifícios e transporte rodoviário, numa altura em que vários países contestam a aplicação do mecanismo. Numa carta dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, Wopke Hoekstra, os ministros do Ambiente da Dinamarca, Finlândia, Alemanha, Luxemburgo, Países Baixos, Portugal, Espanha e Suécia manifestam “forte apoio” ao Sistema de Comércio Europeu de Licenças de Emissão 2 (CELE 2). O CELE 2 é um mercado de carbono complementar ao CELE original. Enquanto o CELE original abrange as emissões da produção de eletricidade e de calor, da indústria pesada, da aviação e do transporte marítimo, o CELE 2 incide sobre novos setores, como as emissões criadas pela utilização de combustíveis em edifícios e no transporte rodoviário. Criado em 2023, o CELE 2 tinha entrada em vigor inicialmente prevista para 2028, mas países mais dependentes dos combustíveis fósseis, como a Itália ou a Polónia, têm apelado a que essa data seja adiada ou que o sistema seja aligeirado. Foi perante esta pressão que, na cimeira do Conselho Europeu de outubro, os líderes da União Europeia (UE) se comprometeram a avaliar o impacto do CELE 2 antes da sua entrada em vigor em 2028. Na carta esta segunda-feira dirigida ao comissário europeu do Clima, que partiu da iniciativa da Dinamarca, os oito ministros frisam que o CELE 2 é atualmente “mais importante do que nunca”, numa altura em que “a perturbação dos fluxos de energia através do Estreito de Ormuz voltou a expor a vulnerabilidade da Europa”. “É evidente que temos de reduzir a nossa dependência dos combustíveis fósseis importados, de modo a diminuir a nossa exposição às tensões geopolíticas e aos choques de preços, que prejudicam a competitividade europeia, afetam negativamente as empresas e as famílias, colocam em risco a nossa segurança energética e nos tornam vulneráveis a pressões políticas”, defendem. Os ministros consideram, por isso, que, “ao proporcionar um meio economicamente eficiente de acelerar a descarbonização dos setores dos transportes rodoviários e dos edifícios”, o CELE 2 “reforça a segurança energética da Europa, reduzindo a dependência das importações de combustíveis fósseis e promovendo a eletrificação”. “O CELE 2 desempenha, assim, um papel fundamental no reforço da resiliência da Europa e da sua autonomia estratégica aberta”, insistem. Os ministros recordam ainda que o CELE 2 é “parte integrante de um compromisso mais amplo, que procura alcançar um equilíbrio delicado entre ambição, eficiência em termos de custos e solidariedade”. Dirigindo-se ao comissário europeu do Clima, os ministros manifestam-se “disponíveis para trabalhar de forma construtiva com a Comissão”, para garantir que o CELE 2 entra em vigor “em conformidade com o calendário já acordado”.

artigo.texto: O mercado brasileiro de armazenamento de energia pode atrair mais de R$ 57 bilhões em investimentos até 2035, segundo estimativa da Deloitte. Em 2026, o setor segue impulsionado pelo avanço da energia solar e pela busca por melhor aproveitamento de energia, mais autonomia e segurança energética, diante de eventos climáticos extremos, por exemplo. Nesse cenário, a Fortlev Solar abriu inscrições gratuitas para a Masterclass Fortlev Solar: Armazenamento de Energia para integradores, na cidade de Vitória. O evento presencial acontece no hotel Golden Tulip Porto Vitória, localizado próximo à Praça do Papa, no dia 24 de novembro. Para se inscrever, basta gerar o ingresso na plataforma Sympla (inscreva-se aqui). A capacitação responde a uma demanda crescente do mercado, impulsionada por fatores como interrupções no fornecimento de energia, gestão mais eficiente do consumo, redução de custos e mudanças no setor elétrico, que têm levado integradores e consumidores a considerar o armazenamento de energia em novos projetos. O objetivo do encontro é preparar os profissionais do segmento de energia solar para oferecerem a melhor solução às demandas da região. Segundo o gerente de Engenharia da Fortlev Solar, Eduardo Nascimento, o armazenamento de energia deixou de ser uma tecnologia do futuro para se tornar uma realidade presente no mercado brasileiro. "Com a Masterclass, nosso intuito é preparar integradores e clientes para esse novo cenário, apresentando soluções confiáveis e aplicações práticas que ampliem as oportunidades de negócio e permitam desenvolver projetos mais eficientes, seguros e rentáveis", afirma. Durante a Masterclass, os participantes terão acesso a conteúdos sobre as principais soluções de armazenamento de energia disponíveis no mercado. Entre elas estão os sistemas híbridos, nas quais a energia gerada pelos módulos solares é utilizada para atender o consumo da instalação. Quando há excedente de geração, essa energia pode ser armazenada nas baterias e ser utilizada depois, à noite, em horários de maior consumo ou em eventuais interrupções no fornecimento da rede elétrica. Também serão apresentados os sistemas BESS (Battery Energy Storage System), desenvolvidos para aplicações comerciais e industriais de maior porte, oferecendo ainda mais flexibilidade. Além de operar em conjunto com a geração solar, também podem ser carregados diretamente pela rede elétrica, o que permite aplicações voltadas ao gerenciamento de energia, redução de custos, backup e maior eficiência operacional, mesmo em locais que não possuem geração fotovoltaica. Durante a Masterclass, os participantes conhecerão essas aplicações na prática, entendendo onde cada solução faz mais sentido e quais oportunidades elas criam para clientes e integradores. Atualmente, a Fortlev Solar comercializa soluções para os dois modelos: o sistema híbrido, composto por inversores e baterias, e o BESS, recentemente incorporado ao seu portfólio. De modo geral, os conteúdos da Masterclass terão foco em inovação, confiabilidade e expansão internacional. Os participantes terão acesso a informações técnicas, com aprofundamento sobre aplicações e tecnologias, oportunidades do segmento, além de promover um contato mais próximo entre integradores, fabricantes e especialistas. Motivos para o consumidor investir em armazenamento de energia Autonomia - Usar energia própria à noite e em dias nublados. Economia - Reduzir custos em horários de tarifa alta. Segurança – Backup contra apagões e falhas da rede. Sustentabilidade – Aproveita 100% de energia renovável. Valorização – Imóvel mais atrativo e tecnológico. Sobre a Fortlev Solar A Fortlev Solar é uma fabricante de kits fotovoltaicos e soluções para energia solar, com atuação voltada a integradores de todo o país. A empresa trabalha com equipamentos de diferentes marcas e desenvolve soluções próprias para aplicações no setor fotovoltaico, buscando facilitar a instalação, a operação e a comercialização de sistemas solares. Fundada em 2019, a empresa faz parte do Grupo Fortlev, que atua há mais de 30 anos no mercado de reservatórios de água, tubos e conexões em PVC. A Fortlev Solar oferece suporte aos integradores em diferentes etapas do projeto, com portfólio de produtos, soluções financeiras, atendimento técnico e estrutura de distribuição. artigo.texto: A lawsuit between a company building a multi-billion dollar data center and Pulaski County could turn on one elected official’s efforts either to – depending on whom you believe – implore her fellow JPs to show up for a vote or to talk them into voting a certain way. The case involves AVAIO Digital, which has sued Pulaski County, Pulaski County Judge Barry Hyde and Justice of the Peace Julie Blackwood, for what it believes has been a coordinated effort to stop or slow its progress in building a $6 billion data center near Wrightsville. While the broader case is perhaps months away from going to trial, AVAIO asked U.S. District Judge Lee Rudofsky to approve a preliminary injunction that would preclude the county from enforcing a new ordinance until the lawsuit is settled. The ordinance, which adds heightened requirements for data centers to obtain county approval, was passed by the Pulaski County Quorum Court in October. Hyde vetoed the ordinance, but there were enough votes on the Quorum Court to override Hyde’s veto. The hearing on the matter started on Friday, and there appeared to be a chance that at least two of the sides – AVAIO’s and Hyde’s – were ready to reach an agreement. But Rudofsky refused to sign off on a consent decree between the two, and the deal fell apart. But it was Blackwood’s part in the affair that never seemed far from the surface. AVAIO’s attorneys attempted to show that she had texted and called her fellow justices of the peace, and for AVAIO’s purposes, she had done so to convince them into voting for the ordinance, which was aimed at putting some controls on big operations like data centers. Blackwood, however, has testified that she was merely calling them to make sure they attended the meeting to vote or calling constituents to encourage them to call their JPs. She denied talking to JPs about substantive matters other than to share information about data centers. Rudofsky didn’t seem to buy that defense, telling her attorney, John Adams, during Adams’ closing remarks that it seemed clear to him that Blackwood had broken the state’s open meetings law by discussing AVAIO’s plans with other justices of the peace. “It looks pretty bad for your client,” Rudofsky said. Adams said the subject of data centers was “on everyone’s lips” and that whether Blackwood had called or not, the ordinance would have passed. He added that Blackwood was simply trying to impress upon her fellow justices of the peace the importance of showing up. “It doesn’t seem that’s what the text messages say,” said Rudofsky, referring to remarks she made in her texts and emails about the proposed ordinance being critical to AVAIO. The judge went so far as to say that he would consider nullifying the ordinance because of Blackwood’s actions, and using that as the key argument for agreeing to the preliminary injunction, although he noted that the Quorum Court could and likely would pass a similar ordinance in short order. Much of Monday’s long session, which ran for 10 hours, was spent with AVAIO laying out the case that it had spent a lot of time and effort – dollar figures were rarely mentioned – preparing for work to begin, that it had received all of the necessary approvals to start that work and that delays would hurt its business interests. Tom Nesel, project manager for AVAIO, said he first became aware that the company was interested in a site in Pulaski County in summer 2023. A year later, he said, AVAIO started the process of buying the land – land that is now being cleared – which required the company to make non-refundable payments to the landowner. AVAIO acquired the deed in August 2026, after getting construction approvals from the county, he said. Through questioning from AVAIO attorney Fred Davis, Nesel retraced the steps he and the company had taken to get approvals from the county and to hire an engineering firm to help with the preliminary site plan. He said he got a letter in summer 2025 from Jim Craner, the county’s planning coordinator at the time, saying the site plan had been approved except for five conditions that still needed to be met. Those conditions have to do with getting a wetland permit from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The company also needs permits for stormwater, flood plain and driveways, and it will need to get an old and never-built subdivision in the area replatted to natural acreage. One issue that hasn’t been resolved, Nesel said, is the wetland permit. In communications with the Corps of Engineers, Nesel said he received an email from one official telling him that if AVAIO built spans or other necessary infrastructure over the top of a wetland area to avoid disturbing the ground, the company wouldn’t need a permit. Rudofsky asked why AVAIO hadn’t canceled the permit request. Nesel said the company would rather use culverts at or below ground level to traverse the wetlands, but if they are unable to get a permit to do that, they are prepared “to avoid the wetlands entirely.” Another AVAIO official, Kevin Murphy, said the company came to Arkansas – and Pulaski County in particular – because it “checked all the boxes,” for access to the things the company was looking for: clean water and water treatment, available land, the huge amount of electricity needed to run a data center and tax incentives from the state. Murphy said that part of the application process included spending a half-million dollars with Entergy as the utility provider worked on the details of providing power to AVAIO’s data center. It was one of the rare disclosures of dollars spent on the project, the details of which were protected during periodic court sessions where witnesses were questioned in private. He said AVAIO’s “core tenets” are to use setbacks to cushion the impact of their data center on surrounding neighbors and to limit water use and noise. artigo.texto: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID) has extended the bid submission deadline for five battery energy storage system (BESS) packages, each having a capacity of 100 MW/400 MWh, at the Rayalaseema Thermal Power Plant (RTPP) in Andhra Pradesh. The five packages together account for 500 MW/2,000 MWh of storage capacity. The packages form part of POWERGRID's larger plan to set up 1,250 MW/5,000 MWh of four-hour BESS capacity across Andhra Pradesh under the Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) route on a Build, Own and Operate (BOO) model. According to an extension notice dated November 20, 2026, the company has revised the deadline for submitting soft-copy bids from November 20 to November 25, 2026. The deadline for submitting requests for issuance of bidding documents has also been extended from November 18 to November 23, 2026. Scope of Work The five packages, identified as AP-BESS-01 to AP-BESS-05, cover the design, supply, erection, testing, commissioning, operation and maintenance of 100 MW/400 MWh battery storage systems at RTPP in Andhra Pradesh. The procurement follows a domestic competitive bidding process and will use a single-stage, two-envelope e-procurement system. POWERGRID has stated that all other terms and conditions of the bidding documents will remain unchanged following the extension. The broader 1,250 MW/5,000 MWh BESS initiative is aimed at adding four-hour battery storage capacity in Andhra Pradesh through multiple packages. The project is being tendered under the BOO model, under which the selected developers will be responsible for developing and operating the storage facilities. Andhra Pradesh's Wider BESS Deployment Plan The proposed storage deployment is spread across three locations in Andhra Pradesh. According to a separate tender document issued by Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation, the state has identified 500 MW/2,000 MWh at RTPP, 250 MW/1,000 MWh at the Talaricheruvu Renewable Energy Project and 500 MW/2,000 MWh at the NP Kunta Renewable Energy Project. All three installations are planned with a four-hour storage duration, taking the proposed capacity to 1,250 MW/5,000 MWh. The procurement is expected to support the integration of renewable energy into the state's electricity system through battery-based storage.

artigo.texto: Calibrant Energy Secures $145 Million for Solar and Battery Storage Projects Calibrant Energy has closed a $145 million debt facility to finance solar and battery energy storage projects across multiple U.S. power markets, including a 120-MWh battery energy storage system serving a hyperscale data center customer in the PJM region. Investec led the financing, with participation from Citi, Liberty Bank and Siemens Financial Services. The data center project comes as large electricity users face growing challenges securing grid connections and obtaining sufficient power to meet expanding demand. In the PJM market, where data center development is contributing to significant load growth, battery storage is emerging as one option for managing the impact of large new loads on the electric grid. On-site battery systems can give data centers greater flexibility in managing electricity consumption, potentially reducing peak demand and easing constraints on grid infrastructure. Depending on project design and operating arrangements, storage also can help large customers manage their power needs while interconnection and transmission upgrades are underway. “Data center operators are choosing on-site energy storage because it is a fast, reliable, and effective way to get online and operate as responsible grid citizens,” said Phil Martin, CEO of Calibrant Energy. Calibrant said the financing will support projects at multiple sites, including additional installations for the same hyperscale data center customer. The company has approximately 2.2 GW of projects and 5.9 GWh of battery storage capacity in operation, under construction or covered by exclusive development agreements. The transaction also reflects continued investment in energy infrastructure designed to serve large electricity users as demand from data centers and other energy-intensive facilities increases. “Investec is proud to support Calibrant and Macquarie on this transaction,” said Fred Petit, co-head of Energy & Infrastructure North America at Investec. He said the financing supports infrastructure needed to meet growing U.S. power demand. Calibrant Energy is backed by Macquarie Asset Management and develops, owns and operates on-site energy projects for large commercial and industrial customers.

artigo.texto: Minicurso 100% online acontece em janeiro de 2027 e aborda soluções baseadas na natureza, manejo agrícola e uso de inteligência artificial no monitoramento ambiental USP/Esalq abre 10 mil vagas para curso gratuito sobre mercado de carbono A Universidade de São Paulo (USP), por meio da Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Esalq), está com inscrições abertas para o minicurso gratuito “Mercado de Carbono e Soluções Baseadas na Natureza”. Voltada a profissionais, produtores e interessados em aprofundar conhecimentos sobre sustentabilidade, mudanças climáticas e projetos ambientais no Brasil, a iniciativa oferece 10 mil vagas na modalidade 100% online. A aula ao vivo será realizada no dia 19 de janeiro de 2027, das 19h às 23h, prazo limite também para a efetivação das inscrições. O encontro será conduzido por Danilo de Almeida, doutor pela Esalq/USP e especialista em tecnologias ambientais, e o conteúdo gravado permanecerá disponível aos participantes por até 30 dias após a transmissão. Conteúdo programático e certificação Leia também no Agrimídia: Com aplicação direta nas demandas atuais do agronegócio e da gestão ambiental brasileira, a ementa do curso contempla cinco eixos principais: - Fundamentos do mercado de carbono e mudanças climáticas; - Funcionamento dos mercados voluntário e regulado; - Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN); - Projetos de reflorestamento, manejo agrícola e florestal e mecanismos REDD+; - Monitoramento ambiental com uso de drones, inteligência artificial e tecnologia LiDAR. Os participantes terão direito a certificado gratuito emitido pela instituição, condicionado à comprovação de participação e ao aproveitamento nas avaliações previstas pela organização. Os interessados podem realizar a inscrição gratuitamente pelo site oficial do MBA USP/Esalq. Clique aqui para se inscrever! Fonte: Esalq/USP

artigo.texto: Madhya Pradesh’s Cabinet has approved a 200 MW floating solar project and an 800 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) under the second phase of the Omkareshwar Dam project, marking another major step in the state’s renewable energy expansion. The decision was taken during a Cabinet meeting held in Gandhi Sagar, Mandsaur, on Wednesday. The proposed 200 MW floating solar project will be developed at the Omkareshwar Reservoir and operated through the Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS). Following approval from the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), the bidding process will be conducted through an open tender coordinated by the designated bid process coordinator. With the addition of 200 MW under Phase 2, the combined floating solar capacity at Omkareshwar Reservoir will increase to 478 MW. This will comprise 278 MW developed under Phase 1 and the proposed 200 MW expansion under Phase 2. Once commissioned, the project is expected to become the world’s largest floating solar project located on a single reservoir. The first phase of the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park, with an installed capacity of 278 MW, has already been completed. Developed by Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Limited (RUMSL), the project secured a competitive tariff of Rs 3.21 per kilowatt-hour. The electricity generated from the project is being procured by Madhya Pradesh Power Management Company Limited. The Cabinet also granted in-principle approval for establishing the Ujjain Forest Zoo and Rescue Centre across approximately 210 hectares at Naulakhi in Ujjain. The proposed facility aims to strengthen wildlife conservation, provide rescue and rehabilitation services for animals in western Madhya Pradesh and promote tourism in the region. In another decision, the Cabinet appointed the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) as the national partner of Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation (MPIDC) for three years. The partnership will support investment promotion activities and help attract investments into the state. The government also approved 72 posts for establishing exclusive special courts in six districts, including Indore, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Singrauli, Bhopal and Rewa, to accelerate trials under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. Additionally, amendments to the Madhya Pradesh Civil Aviation Policy 2025 were approved. The Viability Gap Funding assistance period for introducing new air routes has been extended from one year to four years for domestic destinations and two years for international destinations, starting from the launch of air services.
